papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Since the publication of the ESMO Scale for Clinical Actionability of Molecular Targets (ESCAT) in 2018, precision oncology has evolved substantially. Tumour-agnostic therapy approvals, expanding real-world evidence datasets, and the clinical recognition of genomic resistance biomarkers have created the need to revise the original framework. METHODS: The ESMO Precision Oncology and Taxonomy Committee convened an international expert panel to revise the ESCAT classification. Through iterative review of the evolving evidence-base, structured feedback rounds, and consensus discussions, the panel developed an updated actionability scale and a novel resistance scale. The revision followed three principles: explicit grading of uncertainty within actionable tiers, formal inclusion of tumour-agnostic eligibility criteria, and systematic classification of resistance biomarkers to complement sensitivity designations. RESULTS: ESCAT version 2 (ESCAT v2) introduces several substantive changes. Tier I is restructured into three categories, proven, inferred, and extrapolated, that carry the same clinical directive but differ in the level of certainty within the supporting evidence. The guideline introduces formal tumour-agnostic gating criteria, the ESMO Tumour-Agnostic Classifier and Screener (ETAC-S). Tier II is refined into three sub-tiers graded by prospective interventional evidence, high-quality real-world or non-prospective evidence, and replicated case-level evidence. Tier X is subdivided into alterations that are tested and found not to be predictive (X-A) and biomarker-therapy matches in which the therapy lacks meaningful activity in the biomarker-defined population (X-B). A parallel four-level resistance scale ranges from clinically validated resistance (contraindication) to preclinical or computational evidence (research use only). CONCLUSIONS: ESCAT v2 provides a comprehensive, evidence-graded framework for interpreting actionability and resistance biomarkers in cancer, enabling more nuanced communication among clinicians, patients, regulators, and researchers while preserving a clear directive to act when evidence supports patient benefit.

papers.abstract_en: Immunotherapy with checkpoint inhibitors has revolutionized cancer therapy and enabled considerable therapeutic advances for treating various diseases, including lung cancer. However, the molecular determinants of variable patient outcomes remain unclear. Using long-read RNA sequencing, we mapped the landscape of alternative RNA splicing in human primary lung adenocarcinomas. We identified more than 149,000 full-length messenger RNA (mRNA) isoforms, more than half of which were unannotated and many that occurred in immune-related genes, particularly within the type I interferon response pathway. We functionally characterized retained introns in the STAT2 gene that produced altered protein isoforms that regulated immune signaling and interferon responses and correlated with patient survival after anti-programmed death-ligand 1 (PD-L1) immunotherapy. These findings position alternative splicing as a regulator of tumor immune responses and reveal intron retention in STAT2 as an interferon regulatory axis that correlates with PD-L1 checkpoint inhibitor response.

papers.abstract_en: IMPORTANCE: For patients with eosinophilic granulomatosis with polyangiitis (EGPA), guidelines recommend considering maintenance therapy after achieving remission. Data comparing maintenance therapeutic options are limited. OBJECTIVE: To compare the effects of rituximab and azathioprine maintenance therapies on remission duration for patients with EGPA who recently achieved remission of vasculitis after standard therapy, including prednisone tapering or withdrawal. DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: From March 7, 2018, to June 2, 2022, this double-blind, double-dummy, investigator-initiated, superiority, randomized clinical trial enrolled 98 participants with EGPA from 36 hospitals in France. Inclusion eligibility required a new EGPA diagnosis or relapsing EGPA within 30 to 360 days of achieving vasculitis remission (Birmingham Vasculitis Activity Score of 0 [range, 0-63, with higher scores indicating more severe disease activity]) after a standard induction regimen. Data were analyzed from April 1, 2025, to September 17, 2025. Additional analyses ended June 22, 2026. INTERVENTIONS: Participants were randomized to receive a predefined standardized tapering of oral prednisone and either 500 mg of intravenous rituximab every 6 months for 18 months and daily oral azathioprine placebo for 24 months (n = 49) or rituximab placebo every 6 months for 18 months and daily oral azathioprine for 24 months (n = 49). MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: The primary efficacy end point was the duration of total remission during the 28-month study period while taking 7.5 mg/d or less of prednisone. The 14 secondary end points included proportion of participants remaining in remission, rate of vasculitis relapse, and rate of asthma or rhinosinusitis exacerbations. RESULTS: All 98 randomized participants (mean age, 59.0 years [SD, 14.4]; 50 women [51%]) received at least 1 dose of the trial regimen and 92 (94%) completed the trial. The mean time in remission with prednisone at 7.5 mg/d or less was 91.1 weeks (95% CI, 80.9-101.2) vs 96.0 weeks (95% CI, 85.6-106.5) in the rituximab and azathioprine groups, respectively (P = .38). The proportion of participants who remained in remission during the 28-month study period with prednisone at 7.5 mg/d or less was 17 of 49 (34.7%) vs 11 of 49 (22.4%; relative risk, 1.51; 95% CI, 0.83-2.73; P = .18) in the rituximab and azathioprine groups, respectively. The proportion of participants with at least 1 vasculitis relapse was 7 (14.3%) vs 9 (18.4%) in the rituximab vs azathioprine groups, respectively, and for those with at least 1 clinically significant asthma exacerbation, rhinosinusitis exacerbation, or both, it was 16 (32.7%) vs 19 (38.8%). One participant in the azathioprine group died of SARS-CoV-2 infection before vaccine development. Rituximab recipients experienced a higher incidence of severe infections (23 [46.9%] vs 12 [24.5%], respectively), primarily due to severe SARS-CoV-2 infections. CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: For participants with newly diagnosed or relapsing EGPA, rituximab was not superior to azathioprine for improving the duration of total remission during 28 months while taking prednisone at 7.5 mg/d or less. TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT03164473.

papers.results: IMPORTANCE: The I-SPY2.2 trial tests personalized treatment strategies to improve outcomes while reducing exposure to standard chemotherapy in patients with high-risk early breast cancer (EBC). OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the…
papers.reason: 启发式模式收录（未接入语言模型精评）：按期刊层级与研究类型自动入选。
papers.abstract_en: IMPORTANCE: The I-SPY2.2 trial tests personalized treatment strategies to improve outcomes while reducing exposure to standard chemotherapy in patients with high-risk early breast cancer (EBC). OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the efficacy and safety of trastuzumab-deruxtecan (T-DXd), an antibody drug conjugate targeting low ERBB2 (formerly HER2) expression, combined with rilvegostomig (R), a bispecific antibody targeting programmed cell death 1 protein and T-cell immunoglobulin and ITIM domain as initial therapy in I-SPY2.2 (RT-DXd). DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This phase 2, multicenter, adaptively randomized neoadjuvant trial enrolled patients with high-risk stage II/III ERBB2-negative EBC (including those with ERBB2 low/ultralow tumors), as stratified by hormone receptor (HR) status and response-predictive subtypes. It was conducted at 30 sites in the US; efficacy data were analyzed continuously during the trial to update probabilities and other analyses before publication. INTERVENTIONS: Participants received up to 3 sequential treatment blocks, based on response and subtype: RT-DXd (block A), taxane-based therapy with/without immunotherapy (block B), and doxorubicin-cyclophosphamide (AC) with/without immunotherapy (block C). MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: The primary end point was pathologic complete response (pCR). Safety assessments included adverse events (AEs), with focused monitoring for interstitial lung disease (ILD). RESULTS: A total of 182 individuals (mean [SD] age: RT-DXd, 48.1 [13.1] years; control, 50.9 [12.0] years) participated in the trial. Eighty-eight were randomized to the contemporary control arm, and 108 of 289 remaining participants (37%) were randomized to RT-DXd; 3 participants did not receive block A treatment, and 11 did not receive the assigned control treatment, leaving the intention-to-treat population with 105 and 77 evaluable participants. Among 105 patients treated with RT-DXd in block A, the modeled pCR rate was 54% in immune-positive tumors, which met the predefined threshold for success. Similar pCR rates were observed in HR-positive, immune-positive disease (57%) and HR-negative, immune-positive disease (52%). Across all treatment blocks, overall pCR rates were similar to control regimens; however, among immune-positive patients who experienced pCR, 21 (62%) required only block A, and 33 (97%) avoided anthracycline-based chemotherapy. Enrollment was paused twice to evaluate grade 2 or higher ILD and resumed after data safety monitoring board approval. The most common AEs were fatigue and nausea. Serious AEs included pulmonary embolism and ILD (3 of 105 [2.9%] each). ILD occurred in 13 (12.4%), including 1 grade 3 event, and was identified early with serial chest computed tomography monitoring. CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: This randomized clinical trial found that treatment with RT-DXd demonstrated promising activity, with mostly low-grade toxic effects in immune-positive, ERBB2-negative EBC. Unlike immune-negative patients, many immune-positive patients who experienced pCR avoided standard chemotherapy, including anthracyclines, supporting further evaluation in biomarker-selected populations. TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT01042379.

papers.abstract_en: Immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) have transformed the treatment of advanced non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), yet a large proportion of patients do not respond. The lung microbiome is a key modulator of antitumor immunity, however, the functional contribution of active microbial communities and their interaction with host transcriptional programs in shaping ICI outcomes remain poorly defined. Here, we prospectively analyzed bronchoalveolar lavage (BAL) samples from 71 NSCLC patients prior to ICI initiation. We profiled the microbiome and host transcriptome in the BAL to look for microbial and host signatures in the lower airways associated with treatment response. We found that enrichment of the lower airway microbiome with oral commensals was associated with disease progression and worse prognosis of patients treated with ICI. Metatranscriptomics-derived microbial clustering revealed distinct functional profiles. The microbial cluster enriched with oral commensals, which was only present among patients with poor response to ICI, had differential regulation of pathways involved in the metabolism of short-chain fatty acids, methane, and pyruvate. This cluster also correlated with host immune pathways including upregulation of interferon signaling, neutrophil degranulation, and mitophagy, all of which could contribute to the poor response to immunotherapy. In a preclinical murine model of lung cancer with dysbiosis, inoculating lung tumor-bearing mice with oral commensals increased intratumoral neutrophils and Th17 responses and impaired ICI efficacy. Our findings support the concept that microbial communities in the lower airways influence tumor-immune interactions via defined metabolic-immune axes.

papers.abstract_en: RATIONALE AND OBJECTIVES: Cerebral tuberculomas (CTB) and lung cancer brain metastases (BM) frequently show overlapping appearances on conventional magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) but require entirely different treatment strategies. This study aimed to develop and validate a machine learning model integrating clinical and contrast-enhanced MRI features to noninvasively differentiate these two entities. MATERIALS AND METHODS: The internal dataset (n = 188, 122 CTB, 66 BM) was split into training/validation (n = 131) and internal test (n = 57) sets. Feature selection (univariate and stepwise logistic regression) was performed only on the training and validation set, yielding four predictors. Machine learning classifiers were trained using these predictors with repeated 5-fold cross-validation. An external test set (n = 51, 26 CTB, 25 BM) from another hospital was used for independent validation. RESULTS: Multivariate logistic regression retained four independent predictors: age (OR = 1.046, 95%CI: 1.003-1.091, p = 0.036), carcinoembryonic antigen (CEA) (odds ratios [OR] = 1.711, 95%confidence intervals [CI]: 1.235-2.370, p = 0.001), multiple lesions (OR = 0.080, 95%CI: 0.015-0.438, p = 0.004), and ring with mural nodule (OR = 11.289, 95%CI: 2.551-49.952, p = 0.001). The Gradient Boosting model built on these four features achieved the best performance, with an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.970 (95%CI: 0.925-0.998) on the internal test set and 0.957 (95%CI: 0.900-0.995) on the external test set. On the external test set, the model showed a sensitivity of 88.0% and a specificity of 92.3%. CONCLUSION: A Gradient Boosting model integrating age, CEA, multiple lesions, and ring with mural nodule effectively distinguishes CTB from BM with robust external test performance, providing a noninvasive tool to assist clinical decision-making.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE: Low-dose radiotherapy (LDRT) has shown potential in preclinical Alzheimer's disease (AD) models, but controlled clinical evidence is limited. We evaluated two whole-brain LDRT regimens in mild AD. MATERIALS AND METHODS: In this multicenter, participant-blinded, three-arm phase II trial, amyloid-positive participants were randomized 1:1:1 to sham irradiation, 0.04 Gy per fraction (0.24 Gy total), or 0.5 Gy per fraction (3 Gy total), delivered twice weekly for 3 weeks. The primary endpoint was change in Alzheimer's Disease Assessment Scale-Cognitive Subscale (ADAS-cog) score from baseline to 6 months. Twelve-month analyses were exploratory. Longitudinal outcomes were estimated using mixed-effects models. RESULTS: Forty-one participants were randomized; 36 were included in the modified intention-to-treat population and 30 completed 12-month follow-up. At 6 months, adjusted between-group differences in ADAS-cog change versus sham were -2.08 points (95% CI, -7.06 to 2.89; p = 0.401) for 0.24 Gy and -2.92 points (95% CI, -6.72 to 0.89; p = 0.129) for 3 Gy. At 12 months, the corresponding exploratory differences were -3.02 points (95% CI, -10.00 to 3.96; p = 0.386) and -5.36 points (95% CI, -10.58 to -0.14; nominal p = 0.044). No treatment-related adverse events or radiologic safety concerns were identified. CONCLUSIONS: The prespecified 6-month primary endpoint was not met. Exploratory 12-month and secondary analyses showed differences in selected cognitive outcomes, although the findings varied across doses and outcomes. These findings did not establish efficacy or a dose-response relationship and warrant confirmation in a larger trial with longer follow-up.

papers.abstract_en: PURPOSE: COPE evaluated serial circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) profiling with molecular tumor board (MTB) review during first-line therapy for advanced non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). EXPERIMENTAL DESIGN: COPE was a multicenter, randomized (2:1), noncomparative phase II trial. Arm A underwent serial plasma profiling with every report reviewed at a weekly virtual MTB; Arm B received standard management. The primary endpoint was 18-month overall survival (OS) in Arm A versus a prespecified 40% historical benchmark; no between-arm comparison was planned. RESULTS: Among 176 patients, 117 were assigned to Arm A and 59 to Arm B. Eighteen-month OS was 53.8% (95% CI, 44.3-62.5) and 65.7% (95% CI, 52.0-76.3), respectively. Baseline plasma profiling provided contributory information in 32 of 35 patients with noncontributory or unavailable tissue, increasing genotyping success from 69% to 97%. Paired baseline and early on-treatment samples were available in 90 patients (median, 21 days; range, 19-64). ctDNA clearance was associated with higher objective response rate (83% vs. 52%), longer progression-free survival (22.9 vs. 5.4 months; P<0.001), and longer OS (not reached vs. 17.1 months; P=0.004) than persistent detection. CONCLUSIONS: Serial ctDNA profiling with weekly MTB review was operationally feasible and complemented tissue genotyping. Clinical benefit was not demonstrated; early ctDNA kinetics require validation in interventional trials.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Radiation therapy (RT) is indicated for 77% of patients with lung cancer. Over 20% of patients are affected by radiation-induced lung injury. Computed tomography ventilation imaging (CTVI) estimates high and low functioning lung regions. During RT planning, CTVI can guide preferential avoidance of higher ventilated regions by redirecting dose to less well ventilated regions, sparing healthy lung tissue. The double-masked randomized Trans-Tasman Radiation Oncology Group (TROG) 21.08 VITaL trial will investigate if sparing healthy lung can improve the quality of life (QoL) for patients with stage 3 non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) treated with RT. METHODS: 165 patients will be recruited to test the hypothesis that patients receiving healthy lung-sparing RT have better QoL than patients receiving standard RT. CTVI will be generated from exhale and inhale breath-hold CT scan pairs. A healthy lung-sparing plan and a standard treatment plan will be created for each patient and randomly assigned in a 1:1 ratio for the patient's treatment. QoL will be assessed with the Functional Assessment of Cancer Therapy-Lung questionnaire before and after treatment. Secondary hypotheses include that patients in the healthy lung-sparing arm will have fewer treatment side effects, better lung function, be more likely to receive and complete adjuvant immunotherapy, and healthy lung-sparing treatment will be cost-effective. Patient follow-up will continue for three years. DISCUSSION: This prospective randomized trial will determine whether the incorporation of healthy lung-sparing RT based on CTVI improves QoL, reduces pulmonary toxicity, and increases eligibility to receive curative immunotherapy for patients with stage 3 NSCLC. TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT06127654).

papers.abstract_en: Most small cell lung cancers (SCLCs) exhibit low immunogenicity and intrinsic resistance to immunotherapy, yet the underlying mechanisms remain poorly understood. Here, we identify CREBBP loss, a frequent genetic alteration in SCLC, as a key suppressor of tumor cell-intrinsic immune responses that drives an immune-cold tumor microenvironment in Rb1/Trp53-driven autochthonous mouse models. Consistently, Crebbp deletion promotes immune escape in syngeneic SCLC models. Mechanistically, Crebbp loss suppresses Sting and major histocompatibility complex class-I expression by reducing histone H3 acetylation. Notably, HDAC inhibition restores histone acetylation, reactivates these silenced genes, and induces tumor cell-intrinsic immune responses. Moreover, pharmacological HDAC inhibition synergizes with immune checkpoint blockade to suppress tumor growth in both Crebbp-mutant and Crebbp-wild-type SCLCs, with a more prominent effect in Crebbp-mutant tumors. Collectively, these findings establish CREBBP loss as a key mechanism of immune evasion and immunotherapy resistance in SCLC, highlighting HDAC inhibition as a promising strategy to enhance immunotherapy efficacy.

papers.abstract_en: Lung reirradiation is seeing increased use, yet the evidence base guiding its practice remains limited despite significant technological advances. This paper provides a consensus approach addressing the technical factors underpinning clinical decision-making. It aims to answer the central question: how can clinical teams implement a safe, reproducible, and technically robust workflow for high-dose lung reirradiation? The recommendations are developed by an expert panel of radiation oncologists, medical physicists, and radiation therapists (RTT) from 14 European, American, and Canadian centres, synthesizing a broad range of clinical perspectives. The scope of this work/manuscript is to provide a structured, practical workflow applicable across diverse clinical settings. Using a clinical case, the manuscript demonstrates key conceptual principles, such as the rationale for advanced dose accumulation and the impact of anatomical changes during treatment, with clear, stepwise guidance to support consistent implementation and informed clinical judgement. Key recommended steps include retrieval of prior treatment data; consideration of prior positioning and motion management; and equieffective dose accumulation using deformable image registration or organ-at-risk (OAR)-focused rigid registration. Treatment planning should explicitly incorporate prior dose while balancing target coverage against OAR limits. Daily online volumetric image guidance is central to evaluating both bony and soft-tissue anatomy, enabling setup adjustments to protect critical structures approaching tolerance. Clear documentation and multidisciplinary communication are integral throughout. This consensus approach is intended to support both centres that aim to establish reirradiation practice and experienced teams seeking to harmonize best practices.

papers.abstract_en: This letter to the Editor addresses a fundamental inconsistency in the reporting of study design and validation status in the article by Zhou et al. published in Cancer Imaging. The authors state in the Methods section that the study retrospectively analyzed 125 patients, yet the Introduction and Discussion claim that the study prospectively validated the prognostic value of early tumour shrinkage (ETS) and depth of response (DoR). Prospective validation requires a priori model specification and evaluation on subsequently collected data, whereas retrospective analyses are inherently susceptible to selection bias and cannot establish prospective validity. The authors also conclude that they developed and validated a comprehensive predictive model, but no external validation, temporal validation, or clearly described internal validation procedure is reported. The ETS and DoR thresholds were derived from ROC analysis within the same cohort and then applied to the same patients for survival analysis, risking overfitting and optimistic bias. Additionally, the Results report "responders (n = 109) and non-responders (n = 12)," while the corresponding results in the original article by Zhou et al. [1] list the ratio as 12/109, reversing the group labels. We respectfully suggest that the authors clarify the actual study design, remove any claim of prospective validation if the study is retrospective, provide evidence of validation or remove the claim of a validated model, and correct the numerical inconsistency. Such corrections would uphold the scientific integrity of the literature.

papers.abstract_en: IMPORTANCE: Childhood cancer risk after assisted reproductive technology (ART) remains uncertain, particularly by procedure and cancer type. OBJECTIVE: To examine associations between ART and childhood cancer overall and by ART modality and cancer type. DESIGN, SETTING, AND POPULATION: Nationwide Danish cohort of 1 086 136 live-born children from 1996 to 2012, of whom 37 228 (3.4%) were conceived using ART, with follow-up through 2023. EXPOSURES: Maternal ART, classified as in vitro fertilization (IVF), intracytoplasmic sperm injection, or frozen embryo transfer. MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: Incident childhood cancer. Cox proportional hazards models estimated hazard ratios (HRs); Poisson models estimated incidence rates. Non-ART births were the primary reference; secondary analyses used children of women with a history of infertility and children conceived using IVF as reference groups. RESULTS: During a median follow-up of 20 years, 3736 cancers occurred. Compared with non-ART births (incidence rate, 18.3 per 100 000 person-years), children conceived using ART had higher cancer incidence (incidence rate, 23.6 per 100 000; HR, 1.26 [95% CI, 1.07-1.48]). Rates were higher after frozen embryo transfer (incidence rate, 41.1 per 100 000; HR, 2.18 [95% CI, 1.45-3.29]) and intracytoplasmic sperm injection (incidence rate, 27.9 per 100 000; HR, 1.48 [95% CI, 1.16-1.89]) but not IVF (incidence rate, 18.5 per 100 000; HR, 1.01 [95% CI, 0.79-1.28]). Frozen embryo transfer was associated with leukemia (incidence rate, 11.1 per 100 000; HR, 2.36 [95% CI, 1.06-5.28]), lymphomas (HR, 3.03 [95% CI, 1.13-8.12]), and soft tissue sarcomas (HR, 7.63 [95% CI, 2.82-20.62]); intracytoplasmic sperm injection was associated with lymphomas (incidence rate, 4.6 per 100 000; HR, 1.94 [95% CI, 1.07-3.54]), soft tissue sarcomas (incidence rate, 3.3 per 100 000; HR, 3.28 [95% CI, 1.54-7.00]), and central nervous system neoplasms (incidence rate, 8.2 per 100 000; HR, 1.63 [95% CI, 1.04-2.57]); no associations were observed for IVF. Findings were similar in secondary analyses using children of women with a history of infertility and children conceived using IVF as reference groups. CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: ART, particularly frozen embryo transfer and intracytoplasmic sperm injection, was associated with increased childhood cancer risk, but absolute risks were low. The consistent results in secondary analyses of children with maternal infertility history or conceived via IVF suggest that procedure-related, rather than infertility-related, factors warrant further investigation.

papers.abstract_en: Lung cancer remains the leading cause of cancer-related mortality worldwide, and low-dose CT (LDCT) screening has been shown to significantly reduce lung cancer deaths in high-risk populations. The American College of Radiology (ACR) introduced the Lung CT Screening Reporting and Data System (Lung-RADS) in 2014 to standardize the reporting and management of screen-detected pulmonary nodules. Since its inception, Lung-RADS has undergone iterative updates reflecting advances in evidence, clinical practice, and the expanding scope of lung cancer screening. This review summarizes the major updates to Lung-RADS, highlights areas of active discussion within the Lung-RADS Committee, and outlines future research directions. Key topics include the ongoing evaluation of volumetric versus diameter-based nodule measurement, the management of subsolid nodules and the balance between surveillance and intervention, the implementation of Category 0 for infectious or inflammatory findings, clarification of juxtapleural nodule classification, the approach to incidental findings, and the development of a Lung-RADS Atlas. Future directions address the integration of risk-based and category-based assessment approaches, the role of artificial intelligence and deep learning in nodule stratification, the potential incorporation of incidental nodules into Lung-RADS, and the prospect of international harmonization for lung cancer screening reporting and management. Lung-RADS has become an essential reporting and quality tool for lung cancer screening in the United States and increasingly worldwide. Continued refinement, guided by emerging evidence, multidisciplinary collaboration, and technological innovation, will be critical to advancing precision screening strategies and reducing the global burden of lung cancer.Clinical trial numberNot applicable.

papers.abstract_en: Tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKIs) have marked a turning point in the treatment of oncogene-addicted non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), offering unprecedented efficacy. Yet, most tumors eventually develop resistance and progress, often prompting discontinuation of the targeted agent and a switch to non-targeted therapies such as chemotherapy. We explored current evidence on maintaining inhibition of the oncogenic driver beyond progression in a narrative literature review through August 24, 2026, including clinical trials, retrospective analyses, case reports, case series, and preclinical models. Among all drivers, only EGFR-mutated NSCLC provided phase II/III evidence supporting maintenance of driver inhibition beyond progression. Combinations of EGFR-directed therapies with chemotherapy or MET inhibitors were associated with improved response rates and progression-free survival (PFS) compared with chemotherapy or MET inhibitor monotherapy, although these trials had several limitations. ALK and KRAS G12C evidence was limited to early-phase trials with small cohorts and modest clinical signals, while the remaining drivers (RET, METex14, NTRK, HER2, ROS1, BRAF, and EGFR exon 20) evidence was largely preclinical or anecdotal, making continuation experimental. Co-occurring resistance mechanisms, heterogeneous tumor evolution, and potential additive toxicity complicate interpretation of the backbone's contribution to clinical benefit. Continuation should therefore not be applied routinely but tailored to the pattern and site of progression, re-biopsy findings, CNS disease control, expected toxicity, and patient preferences. Given the rarity of many oncogenic drivers and the challenges of conducting adequately powered randomized trials, definitive data may remain available for several resistance scenarios.

papers.abstract_en: CASTOR1, a cytosolic arginine sensor and regulator of mTORC1 signaling, is identified here as a tumor suppressor in KRAS-driven non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). In a KRASG12D mouse model, CASTOR1 deletion enhances tumor initiation and progression, accompanied by increased proliferation. Although CASTOR1 is rarely mutated or deleted in human cancers, its expression progressively declines during tumor progression and is associated with increased AKT activation and CASTOR1 phosphorylation, consistent with functional inactivation. Loss of CASTOR1 results in constitutive mTORC1 hyperactivation, impaired arginine-dependent regulation of mTORC1 signaling, elevated p-4EBP1 and p-S6 levels, increased AKT and ERK activation, genomic instability, and resistance to KRASG12D inhibitors. Tumors and tumor-derived organoids deficient in CASTOR1 are resistant to KRAS inhibition, but this resistance can be overcome by cotargeting mTORC1 or dual PI3K/mTOR inhibition. These findings identify CASTOR1 as a critical link between nutrient sensing and oncogenic signaling and reveal its functional inactivation as an important mechanism contributing to KRAS-driven NSCLC progression and therapeutic resistance. The results further support rational combination therapies to overcome KRAS inhibitor resistance in CASTOR1-low NSCLC.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Extensive-stage small-cell lung cancer (ES-SCLC) remains an aggressive malignancy with poor survival despite platinum-etoposide chemotherapy. Although serplulimab plus chemotherapy has demonstrated a survival benefit in randomized trials, comparative real-world evidence remains limited. We therefore evaluated survival outcomes with first-line serplulimab plus chemotherapy versus chemotherapy alone in patients with ES-SCLC. METHODS: We conducted a single-center retrospective cohort study at Tianjin Chest Hospital. Patients with ES-SCLC who initiated first-line platinum-etoposide-based chemotherapy between January 2020 and December 2024 were screened, with follow-up censored on May 1, 2025. Patients were classified according to whether serplulimab was incorporated into first-line treatment. The primary endpoint was overall survival (OS), and the secondary endpoint was real-world progression-free survival (rwPFS). Treatment effects were estimated using Kaplan-Meier analyses and Cox proportional hazards models. Because of the limited sample size and event count, the primary adjusted Cox model was restricted to prespecified clinical covariates. Sensitivity analyses included treatment-year adjustment, restriction to patients treated during 2022-2024, reduced propensity score overlap weighting and stabilized trimmed inverse probability of treatment weighting (IPTW). RESULTS: The final cohort included 112 patients, of whom 30 received serplulimab plus chemotherapy and 82 received chemotherapy alone. Median OS was 18.69 months with serplulimab plus chemotherapy and 11.86 months with chemotherapy alone (HR = 0.49, 95% CI: 0.27-0.90; P = 0.021; log-rank P = 0.017). The association remained significant after parsimonious clinical adjustment (adjusted HR = 0.50, 95% CI: 0.27-0.93; P = 0.028). Sensitivity analyses yielded directionally similar OS estimates across treatment-year adjustment, 2022-2024 restriction, overlap weighting, and stabilized trimmed IPTW. Median rwPFS was also numerically longer with serplulimab plus chemotherapy, although the difference was not statistically significant (10.64 vs 8.18 months; HR = 0.76, 95% CI: 0.48-1.20; P = 0.244). CONCLUSIONS: In this single-center real-world cohort, first-line serplulimab plus chemotherapy was associated with longer OS than chemotherapy alone in patients with ES-SCLC, whereas the rwPFS difference was not statistically significant. The findings were directionally supported by multiple sensitivity analyses but should be interpreted cautiously because of the limited sample size, potential calendar-time confounding, and incomplete standardized safety assessment. Larger prospective studies are needed for confirmation.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: The optimal integration of surgery and definitive chemoradiotherapy (CRT) following modern neoadjuvant immunochemotherapy in stage IIB-IIIA/B non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC) remains controversial. Although immune checkpoint inhibitors have substantially improved outcomes in both resectable and unresectable disease, prospective randomized data directly comparing surgery and definitive CRT after neoadjuvant immunochemotherapy are lacking. METHODS: InDuRanS is a prospective, multicenter, randomized, open-label phase II trial conducted in Germany. Patients with (borderline) resectable stage IIB-IIIA/B (N2) NSCLC receive three cycles of neoadjuvant immunochemotherapy with durvalumab plus platinum-paclitaxel. Patients with persistent resectability are randomized 1:1 to surgery or definitive CRT. Both treatment arms receive consolidation durvalumab for up to 12 months. The primary endpoint is 2-year event-free survival in 158 randomized patients. Key secondary endpoints include progression-free survival, overall survival, safety and tolerability, health-related quality of life, and an extensive exploratory translational research program. DISCUSSION: InDuRanS is the first randomized trial to directly compare surgery versus definitive CRT within a contemporary multimodal treatment sequence incorporating both neoadjuvant and consolidation immunotherapy in stage IIB-IIIA/B NSCLC. Its results are expected to help define optimal local treatment strategies in an evolving therapeutic landscape. InDuRanS is currently active and open to enrollment as of April 2025, with primary completion anticipated in 2028 (NCT06810609).

papers.abstract_en: It remains largely unclear whether oncogenic super-enhancers (SEs) can drive expression of circular RNAs (circRNAs). In this study, we for the first time profiled the comprehensive circRNA landscapes of esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC) after suppressing genome-wide SE activities. We identified a novel SE-driven circPRRC2B, as the product of back-splicing of exons 2, 3, 4 and 5 of PRRC2B pre-mRNA, which was controlled by RNA binding protein HuR. Indeed, SE drives high levels of PRRC2B transcription, promotes production of PRRC2B pre-mRNAs, boosts back-splicing of PRRC2B pre-mRNAs, and elevates circPRRC2B expression. ETS1 acts as a key transcriptional factor in SE-driven PRRC2B transcription and circPRRC2B biogenesis. Interestingly, circPRRC2B, but not PRRC2B, could promote proliferation, invasion and metastasis of ESCC in vitro and in vivo. Mechanistically, circPRRC2B binds to TALDO1 and enhances BAP1-mediated TALDO1 de-ubiquitination in ESCC cells. Therefore, circPRRC2B stabilizes and sustains high expression of TALDO1, activates the pentose phosphate pathway (PPP), elevates the glutathione levels via supplying more NADPH via the PPP, inhibits production of reactive oxygen species in mitochondrion, maintains cellular redox equilibrium, and, thus, leads to cancer progression. Importantly, we developed antisense oligonucleotides targeting circPRRC2B which exhibited remarkable inhibition of ESCC growth. Our findings highlighted circPRRC2B as a key target preserving the PPP metabolic flux and redox homeostasis of malignant cells, thereby offering insight into developing novel therapeutics for cancers.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: If metastasis can be predicted, appropriate management of lung cancer will be possible to improve prognosis. Therefore, the main objective of this study is to develop a prediction model with appropriate performance for predicting metastasis based on patient data. METHODS: The study analyzed patient records from Kaggle, performing exploratory data analysis and preprocessing techniques such as missing values handling, encoding categorical variables, and outliers' removal. Next, Data normalization and feature engineering were applied. Imbalanced data was addressed using Synthetic Minority Over-sampling Technique (SMOTE). Supervised classification models, including boosting algorithms were developed and tuned via Grid Search algorithms. Performance was evaluated using accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, and ROC-AUC, with stratified k-fold cross-validation ensuring robustness. All processes were conducted using Python language on Google Collab. RESULTS: After data preprocessing, normalization, and selecting more related features, the dataset was stratified into training and testing subsets using an 80:20 split to ensure representative sampling classification models trained on training data. Class imbalance in the target variable was addressed using the SMOTE on the training set to balance classes without biasing the test set. Various machine learning models, including Logistic Regression, KNN, Decision Tree, Random Forest, and boosting algorithms (AdaBoost, XGBoost, LightGBM, Gradient Boosting), were developed and evaluated using metrics like accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, and AUC. SMOTE significantly improved model performance, with XGBoost emerging as the top performer, achieving the highest AUC (82%) and F1-score (74.83%). ROC curve analysis confirmed XGBoost's superior predictive power for metastasis. CONCLUSIONS: The development of a high-performing prediction model for lung cancer metastasis to other organs has significant implications for clinical practice. Early and accurate prediction of metastasis can enable timely interventions, potentially improve patient outcomes and reduce healthcare costs.

papers.abstract_en: IMPORTANCE: Obesity affects 15% of children aged 2 to 5 years and 22% of children aged 6 to 11 years in the US. Obesity in children is associated with dyslipidemia, hypertension, metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease, and obstructive sleep apnea. Compared with normal-weight peers, children with obesity have lower quality of life and are 5 times more likely to have obesity in adulthood. OBSERVATIONS: Body mass index (BMI; calculated as weight in kilograms divided by height in meters squared) is used to identify children at risk for excess adiposity, and guidelines recommend that clinicians screen for obesity using BMI starting at age 2 years. Among children, obesity is defined using standardized age- and sex-specific growth charts, with obesity defined as BMI in the 95th or higher percentile and severe obesity as BMI of 120% or greater of the 95th percentile. Obesity treatment in children includes intensive health behavior and lifestyle treatment, consisting of at least 26 contact hours of face-to-face group or family-based activities that incorporate nutrition, physical activity, and behavior change education delivered to the child and caregivers over a 3- to 12-month period. Intensive health behavior and lifestyle treatment reduces BMI by 0.7 compared with children who do not participate in intensive health behavior and lifestyle treatment. The only obesity pharmacotherapy currently approved by the US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) for children younger than 12 years is setmelanotide, a melanocortin-4 receptor agonist, which is indicated for 3 forms of rare monogenic obesity (LEPR, POMC, and PCSK1 genetic variants), Bardet-Biedl syndrome, and acquired hypothalamic obesity. Liraglutide is currently only FDA approved for youth aged 12 years or older; however, a randomized clinical trial among children aged 6 to younger than 12 years demonstrated that, compared with placebo, liraglutide reduced BMI by 7.4%. Metabolic and bariatric surgery is rarely used in children younger than age 12 years and evidence supporting its use in children is limited. Early identification and treatment of obesity during childhood may reduce risk of type 2 diabetes, dyslipidemia, hypertension, and mortality in adulthood. CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: Obesity in children is associated with chronic disease, such as hypertension, and with poor quality of life. Evidence-based treatment for obesity in children includes intensive health behavior and lifestyle treatment, and pharmacotherapy may provide additional benefit, although short- and long-term safety and efficacy data are limited. Early identification and treatment of obesity during childhood may reduce risk of type 2 diabetes, dyslipidemia, hypertension, and mortality in adulthood.

papers.abstract_en: Programming biological function-designing bespoke proteins to perform specified molecular tasks-is a foundational goal of molecular engineering. However, current design models remain fundamentally limited1-3: they typically require either natural proteins as starting points for optimization or manual reformulation of functional goals as geometric and sequence-level constraints to guide candidate generation. Here we introduce Pinal, a 16-billion-parameter foundation model that designs candidate proteins from natural-language descriptions of desired function. Trained on 1.7 billion synthetically annotated protein-text pairs, Pinal links functional intent to protein sequence and structure. In computational evaluations, generated candidates combined high predicted foldability with functional-description alignment and sequence diversity, providing a basis for prioritizing experimentally testable designs. We applied Pinal to four distinct design tasks-a fluorescent protein, a polyethylene terephthalate hydrolase, an alcohol dehydrogenase and a metabolic H-protein-and experimentally observed the intended function in each case, including catalytic activity for both designed enzymes. Without iterative experimental optimization, a Pinal-designed H-protein increased product titre by 1.7-fold relative to the corresponding native Escherichia coli H-protein in a multi-enzyme CO2 fixation pathway. These findings support natural language as a high-level interface for candidate generation in protein design, enabling programmable exploration with reduced reliance on manually specified structural or sequence constraints.

papers.abstract_en: Interactions among species are increasingly recognized as key determinants of climate change impacts on ecosystems1-5. However, we know little about how climatic perturbations affect interactions among top vertebrate predators. Here we show that, when an emergent disease caused the decline of shared prey (rabbits), after decades of neutral co-existence a mammalian carnivore (lynx) started to prey heavily on a top predatory raptor (kites). These predation bouts occurred exclusively under drought conditions and when lynx found rabbit remains under the raptor nests, consistent with the removal of a potential competitor. Drought-induced lynx predation depressed lifetime reproductive success and triggered territory abandonment and dispersal by the raptor, suggestive of a new arms race among predators. A reduction in raptor abundance was associated with an increase in an insectivorous bird (a small owl), showing that the new interaction had the potential to reach lower trophic levels. These results underline the importance of diet flexibility and mobility as important mediators of resilience to stressors. In the future, synergistic effects of multiple anthropogenic stressors may reshape the interactions and ecological roles of many apex predators, with potential cascading consequences for whole ecosystems. A key to forecasting the future impact of global change may reside in understanding how behavioural flexibility and interacting keystone species respond to interacting shocks.

papers.abstract_en: The accumulation of persistent plastics in the ocean is causing wide-ranging environmental problems1-3. Some commercially available compostable plastics4-7, developed to address these issues, degrade efficiently under industrial composting conditions; however, their degradation in marine environments, particularly in the deep sea, remains limited8-10. Here we demonstrate that thermally embedding enzymes into compostable polyesters (poly(butylene succinate) (PBS), poly(butylene succinate-co-adipate) (PBSA), poly(ε-caprolactone) (PCL) and poly(butylene adipate-co-terephthalate) (PBAT)) significantly accelerates their degradation in both coastal and deep-sea environments from water depths of 2-6 m to 5,503 m. Enzyme-embedded polyesters achieved near-complete degradation at a deep-sea depth of 757 m within 5 months. Furthermore, moderate biodegradation of enzyme-embedded polyesters was observed under extreme conditions on deep-sea floors of 5,503 m. In coastal seawater, films embedded with trace amounts (0.1 wt%) of enzyme underwent rapid degradation. The mechanical properties of enzyme-embedded polyesters were similar to those of enzyme-free polyesters. Chemical analysis confirmed the formation of low-molecular-mass degradation products and biochemical oxygen demand measurements supported the mineralization of the enzyme-embedded polyesters. The enzyme-embedding strategy enables enhanced marine degradation of compostable polyesters and represents a potential solution to marine plastic pollution.

papers.abstract_en: Magnetic tunnel junctions based on ferromagnets are canonical devices in spintronics, with wide-ranging applications in data storage, computing and sensing. They simultaneously exhibit mechanisms for electrical detection and control of magnetic order through the tunnelling magnetoresistance (TMR)1-5 and spin-transfer torque6-9 effects, respectively. It was long assumed that neither of these effects could be sizeable in all-antiferromagnetic tunnel junctions (AATJs), considering that they have no net magnetization. However, it was recently shown that AATJs based on chiral antiferromagnets do exhibit TMR due to their non-relativistic momentum-dependent spin polarization and cluster magnetic octupole moment, which are manifestations of their spin-split band structure10-13. However, the reciprocal effect, that is, the antiferromagnetic counterpart of spin-transfer torque, has been assumed non-existent due to the total electric current being spin-neutral. Here we report nanoscale AATJs that display this reciprocal effect, which we term octupole-driven spin-transfer torque (OTT). We demonstrate current-induced OTT switching of PtMn3|MgO|PtMn3 AATJs, with a TMR value of 363% at room temperature and switching current densities of the order of 10 MA cm-2. Our theoretical modelling explains the origin of OTT in terms of the imbalance between intra- and inter-sublattice spin currents across the AATJ, and, equivalently, in terms of the non-zero net cluster octupole polarization of each PtMn3 layer. This work establishes a new materials platform for antiferromagnetic spintronics and provides a pathway towards deeply scaled magnetic memory and room-temperature terahertz technologies.

papers.abstract_en: Large language models are enabling a new generation of health agents, yet their ability to address the diverse needs of individuals in everyday health settings remains underexplored1,2. Here we developed a comprehensive personal health agent that reasons over multimodal data from consumer wellness devices and medical records to provide personalized health support. Through analysis of web search and health forum queries, together with user-centred research involving end users and health experts, we identified four key user journeys: general health knowledge, personal data interpretation, wellness advice, and symptom assessment. These journeys informed three specialist sub-agents: (1) a data science agent that analyses longitudinal wearable and medical data, incorporating population-level statistics to contextualize numerical insights; (2) a health domain expert agent that integrates personal and contextual data with health knowledge to generate personalized insights; and (3) a health coach agent that synthesizes insights, supports multi-turn interaction and goal setting, applies specified psychological strategies and tracks progress. We integrated these capabilities in the personal health agent, an open-source multi-agent framework for dynamic, personalized health interactions. We evaluated the sub-agents and full system across 11 benchmark tasks using automated and human evaluation, with more than 7,000 annotations and 1,350 h of effort from health experts and end users. This represents the most comprehensive evaluation of a personal health agent thus far and provides a concrete foundation for improving access to high-quality personalized health support more broadly.

papers.abstract_en: Single-crystal materials are indispensable for high-performance applications, yet their deployment remains constrained by conventional manufacturing techniques that depend on strict quasi-steady thermal conditions1. This requirement fundamentally conflicts with the intense cyclic thermal fluctuations inherent to additive manufacturing2, historically preventing the 3D printing of large or architected single crystals. Here we present a free-form additive manufacturing approach that resolves this contradiction by using delicately controlled alternating and pulsed heat inputs to govern and direct single-crystal growth. Using this method, we demonstrate the fabrication of metre-tall, centimetre-diameter single-crystal Ti-6Al-4V alongside, to our knowledge, the first single-crystal lattice structures containing complex zigzag ligaments, effectively eliminating theoretical size constraints for single-crystal components. The resulting bulk single-crystal Ti-6Al-4V exhibits an order-of-magnitude increase in creep resistance over standard grain-size scaling predictions, driven by the synergistic elimination of grain boundaries and an additive manufacturing-induced hierarchical α/β-architecture that regulates dislocation density, mobility and void evolution. Furthermore, we demonstrate the broad applicability of this technique by printing single crystals of hard-to-process refractory metals, including W, Mo, Nb and MoNb alloys. Our work introduces a large-scale method for single-crystal additive manufacturing, expanding the accessible materials library and enabling high-performance, complex geometries previously unattainable by classical methods.

papers.abstract_en: The Amazon carbon sink is weakening as deforestation1-5, rising tree mortality6-8 and climate change disrupt the climatic conditions that sustain a humid tropical forest9-11. Forest loss reduces precipitation, increases temperatures and lengthens the dry season, driving higher carbon emissions1-4,11,12. Climate stress is stronger in more deforested regions, rendering forests progressively more flammable1,9,13. Large-scale climate events, such as El Niño, further amplify regional climate impacts9,14-17. Here we present an analysis of 15 years of Amazonian carbon fluxes derived from atmospheric CO2 measurements. We determine a carbon balance of 0.32 ± 0.08 PgC yr-1, with fires acting as the dominant source (0.40 ± 0.07 PgC yr-1) and forest uptake becoming increasingly unable to offset emissions. Furthermore, we investigate key drivers of the carbon emissions of Amazonia and identify three distinct year groups. Group 1 (2011-2014, 2017 and 2018) represents the role of the Amazon in the global carbon balance (0.11 ± 0.08 PgC yr-1) during wetter years with low human activity, such as deforestation, biomass burning and degradation. Group 2 (2019-2022) represents Amazon carbon emissions (0.43 ± 0.13 PgC yr-1) from human activities (mainly deforestation and degradation) during years with low climatic stress. Group 3 (2010, 2015, 2016, 2023 and 2024) has the highest carbon emissions (0.49 ± 0.07 PgC yr-1) and comprises warm and dry years (high climate stress), such as El Niño and the warming of the Tropical North Atlantic Ocean, associated with biomass burning.

papers.abstract_en: Anaerobic degradation of complex organic compounds to methane and carbon dioxide is common in the deep subsurface biosphere and has long been considered to require syntrophic cooperation, with methanogens confined to the terminal use of simple C1 and C2 substrates. Thermodynamic considerations, multi-omics analyses and microcosm experiments suggest that archaeal lineages are capable of methanogenic degradation of complex substrates1-6. However, experimental validation in pure culture was lacking. Here we report the isolation of a thermophilic archaeon, Methanoglobus dolicholipophagus AA-75, affiliated with Archaeoglobi, from a Chinese petroleum reservoir. Strain AA-75 not only converts methanol into methane, carbon dioxide and acetate, but also uses saturated fatty acids varying from C7:0 to C18:0 and unsaturated fatty acids including C16:1, C18:1 and C18:2 to produce methane. We term the latter lipotrophic methanogenesis, which integrates β-oxidation of fatty acids with the Wood-Ljungdahl pathway and the canonical methyl-tetrahydromethanopterin:coenzyme M methyltransferase and methyl-coenzyme M reductase complexes, together with an intracellular electron transfer system. A formaldehyde-methanol branch probably functions as an auxiliary route for C1 metabolism during methanogenesis. Methane produced from stearate is moderately 13C-enriched (δ13C-CH4 = -40.0‰ to -36.3‰), distinct from the strong 13C depletion characteristic of canonical methanogenic pathways. These findings demonstrate that methanogens can function as primary degraders of complex organic matter, challenging the classical syntrophic paradigm and calling for refinement of current models of carbon cycling in the deep subsurface biosphere.

papers.abstract_en: Moderately cold temperatures extend lifespan and promote health across species1-3, yet the molecular mechanisms underlying these benefits remain unclear. Here we define a metabolite-driven, multi-tissue signalling system that links cold temperature to enhanced longevity and proteostasis in Caenorhabditis elegans. Cold temperature upregulates the biopterin-synthesis enzyme CAT-4 (GCH1 in humans), increasing production of dihydrobiopterin (BH2), a transportable reservoir for the bioactive cofactor tetrahydrobiopterin (BH4). BH2 is produced in muscle and transported to distal tissues, including the intestine and neurons, where it is converted into BH4 by the salvage enzyme DHFR-1. BH4 functions as an essential cofactor for phenylalanine hydroxylase PAH-1, promoting tyrosine synthesis and extending lifespan. This BH2-BH4 axis also prevents disease-related protein aggregation and subsequent neuronal dysfunction during ageing. Importantly, increasing BH2 synthesis specifically in muscle is sufficient to promote longevity and suppress pathological protein aggregation in distal tissues, even at normal or elevated temperatures. In human cells, BH2 or tyrosine supplementation reduces aggregation of polyQ-expanded proteins associated with Huntington's disease, as well as mutant variants of TDP-43 and FUS that cause amyotrophic lateral sclerosis. Together, these findings identify BH2 as a cold-induced metabolite of which the synthesis, intertissue transport and conversion into bioactive BH4 preserve organism-wide proteostasis and extend lifespan.

papers.abstract_en: Carbonylation is an important process used to produce aldehydes, carboxylic acids and esters1-5 that is usually catalysed by homogeneous metal complexes with ligands and iodide promoters6-12. Koch has reported that protons of mineral acids can also catalyse carbonylation13. Previous studies have demonstrated that Brønsted acidic zeolites can act as a heterogeneous, Koch-type catalyst for carbonylation of alcohols and olefins, but the products in this case are limited to tertiary carboxylic acids14-18. Here we show that targeted use of spatial confinement in a zeolite together with a high CO/olefin ratio can help break this limitation. We report that, with FER zeolite and a CO/olefin ratio of 360, olefin carbonylation can produce primary and secondary carboxylic acids as the main products; ethylene carbonylation to propanoic acid (PA) is achieved with 80% selectivity over 100 h and propylene carbonylation to isobutyric acid (IBA) is achieved with 95% selectivity over 750 h. The propylene and ethylene carbonylation selectivities decrease to 61% and 57%, respectively, as the CO/olefin ratio decreases to 24 and 90, respectively. Experiments in combination with theoretical calculations suggest that T2-O5 in eight-membered ring (8-MR) cavities of FER zeolite are the primary active sites for ethylene carbonylation and T3-O1 in ten-membered rings (10-MRs) are the primary active sites for propylene carbonylation. Our findings open new directions for olefin carbonylation and provide critical insights into the prerequisites for developing new zeolite-based carbonylation processes.

papers.abstract_en: WEE1 phosphorylates and inhibits the activity of cyclin-dependent kinases to prevent mitotic entry and establish a G2 DNA damage checkpoint1-3. Consequently, WEE1 inhibitors have been developed to be synthetically lethal in TP53-mutated tumours that become reliant on this WEE1-mediated checkpoint, and such inhibitors are undergoing clinical trials. However, WEE1 inhibitors also have efficacy in TP53-wild-type tumours, and many trials have been terminated owing to high levels of toxic side effects, suggesting that WEE1 has unknown functions. Here we show that WEE1 promotes cell cycle re-entry from quiescence (G0) by opposing the activity of the E3 ubiquitin ligase, anaphase-promoting complex-cyclosome bound to CDH1 (APC/CCDH1). WEE1 phosphorylates CDH1 (FZR1) at key residues that mediate the interaction between CDH1 and APC/C. Cells with loss of function of WEE1 during G0/G1 have delayed S phase entry, impaired G1/S transition, abnormal S phase accumulation of cyclin-dependent kinase inhibitor p21Cip1/Kip1 and a p21-dependent G2 arrest. Reduced expression of APC/CCDH1 or p21 renders cells more sensitive to acute WEE1 inhibition, and both pathways are downregulated in cells with acquired WEE1 inhibitor resistance. These results reveal a mechanism of cell cycle control that has implications for how WEE1 inhibitors should be used in the clinic.

papers.affiliation_highlight: Wageningen University & Research, Wageningen, the Netherlands.

papers.reason: 启发式模式收录（未接入语言模型精评）：按期刊层级与研究类型自动入选。
papers.abstract_en: Salt marshes protect coastlines by attenuating wind waves with their elevated marsh platform and above-ground vegetation1. Confidence in the persistence of this service under a changing climate requires knowledge on how extreme storms damage the platform and vegetation; however, a comprehensive, quantified understanding of salt marsh-wave interactions under extreme events is lacking. A unique experiment was conducted by transferring intact salt marsh to one of the world's largest wave flumes, and subsequently exposing it to increasingly higher waves that reach up to 2 m significant wave height. We show that marsh substrates can persist with negligible erosion, despite cumulative wave exposure. By contrast, the vegetation was progressively damaged during continued wave exposure, gradually reducing vegetation-related wave attenuation. Results emphasize that vegetation was most effective in attenuating waves at low-energy marsh coasts (up to 1 m), where attenuation exceeded 10% (up to 50%), whereas attenuation at high-energy marsh coasts (wave height > 1 m) does not exceed 10%. Our global assessment supports the differentiation between low- and high-energetic conditions resulting from the flume experiment. Our results suggest that the marsh platform remains stable under extreme wave events and that substantial wave attenuation by marsh vegetation is limited to low-energy marsh coasts.

papers.authors: Li Y, Chen R, Lv X, Wei S, Xu Y, Ding S
papers.affiliation_highlight: Department of Cardiovascular Surgery, Southeast University Affiliated Nantong First People's Hospital, Nantong, China.
papers.results: 恶病质ESCC较非恶病质者白蛋白、总蛋白、前白蛋白更低，IL-6、TNF-α、CRP、IL-1β更高（均p<0.05）。非恶病质 vs 恶病质ESCC：AUC 0.8594与0.8175（均p<0.0001）；对照 vs 恶病质ESCC：AUC 0.9439与0.8889。恶病质与更短总生存相关（HR 1.708，95% CI 1.011-2.887；p=0.026）；高miR-5187-5p表达（HR 3.635）与高miR-4433b-3p表达（HR 3.190）亦与更短总生存相关。与炎症指标及白蛋白的相关性为弱至中等。
papers.authors_conclusion: hsa-miR-5187-5p与hsa-miR-4433b-3p是ESCC相关恶病质及其炎症-代谢环境的候选循环标志物；因分析在同一队列内进行且未对肿瘤分期或其他临床病理因素进行充分校正，其判别与预后效能仍属探索性。
papers.ai_note: 判别效能在同一队列内推导并评估，无独立外部验证，AUC存在乐观偏倚且未报告95% CI；两组AUC（0.8594/0.8175）未明确对应哪一个miRNA，表述含混；生存分析仅单因素Cox，miRNA的HR未给出CI与P值，且未校正肿瘤分期、体重丢失程度、治疗情况，恶病质与miRNA预后的独立性无法判断；队列为病例对照式抽样且每组42例，样本量小、事件数有限；发现集仅4例/组，miRNA筛选稳健性不足；miRNA与炎症指标相关性仅弱至中等，支持“反映炎症-代谢”的机制性论据偏弱；摘要未报告多重比较校正。

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Cachexia in oesophageal squamous cell carcinoma is driven by systemic inflammation and malnutrition and is associated with poor survival. We evaluated whether circulating miRNAs can identify ESCC cachexia and reflect its inflammatory-nutritional phenotype. METHODS: We enrolled 126 participants: 42 healthy controls and 84 treatment-naïve patients with ESCC, equally classified as noncachectic or cachectic using international consensus criteria. Small-RNA sequencing in a discovery subset (n = 4/group) was followed by cohort-wide qRT-PCR. Exploratory within-cohort discrimination was assessed by receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis; survival associations were evaluated using Kaplan-Meier and univariate Cox analyses. RESULTS: Cachectic ESCC was characterized by lower albumin, total protein and prealbumin and higher IL-6, TNF-α, CRP and IL-1β than noncachectic ESCC (all p < 0.05). Circulating hsa-miR-5187-5p and hsa-miR-4433b-3p increased stepwise from controls to noncachectic and cachectic ESCC. For noncachectic versus cachectic ESCC, AUCs were 0.8594 and 0.8175, respectively (both p < 0.0001); for controls versus cachectic ESCC, AUCs were 0.9439 and 0.8889. Cachexia was associated with shorter overall survival (HR 1.708, 95% CI 1.011-2.887; p = 0.026), as were high miR-5187-5p (HR 3.635) and miR-4433b-3p (HR 3.190) expression. Correlations with inflammatory markers and albumin were weak to moderate. CONCLUSIONS: hsa-miR-5187-5p and hsa-miR-4433b-3p are candidate circulating indicators of ESCC-associated cachexia and its inflammatory-metabolic milieu. Their discriminatory and prognostic performance remains exploratory because analyses were conducted within the same cohort and were not comprehensively adjusted for tumour stage or other clinicopathological factors.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: The tumour immune microenvironment influences neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy success in esophageal adenocarcinoma (EAC). Complete responders show higher treatment-naïve intratumoral CD8+ T cell levels before treatment than non-complete responders. Understanding mechanisms driving CD8+ T cells exclusion from the TIME is essential to improving outcomes. METHODS: We performed spatial transcriptomics on treatment-naive CD8-low and high EACs (N = 12). Regions of interest (ROIs) were selected based on tumour annotation by a pathologist. Cancer (CK+) cells and immune (CD45+) cells were analysed within the same ROI. Findings were validated using bulk transcriptome data (TCGA) and metabolic profiling (SCENITH) of fresh tumour specimen (n = 5). RESULTS: Whole transcriptomic profiling showed cancer cell clustering based on T cell infiltration. Cancer cell transcriptomes of CD8-low tumours exhibited reduced antigen presentation and upregulated lipid and mitochondrial metabolism, while CD8-high tumours showed increased cytokine signalling and apoptotic pathways. In CD45+ compartments, CD8-low tumours were enriched for the PGC-1α pathway, linked to mitochondrial biogenesis and immunosuppressive myeloid populations. These findings were supported by TCGA data. SCENITH confirmed mitochondrial dependence of macrophages in CD8-low tumours. CONCLUSION: Our results suggest that mitochondrial metabolism and impaired antigen presentation contribute to T cell exclusion in EAC. These findings raise the hypothesis that targeting mitochondrial metabolism in these cancers can modulate the anti-tumour immune response and thereby improve the response to chemoradiotherapy.

papers.abstract_en: BackgroundLoss of appetite (LOA) is a highly prevalent and distressing symptom in advanced lung cancer, leading to malnutrition, poorer treatment tolerance, and reduced quality of life. Although acupuncture may help manage cancer-related symptoms, its effect on LOA in patients receiving immunotherapy is unclear. This study aims to assess the efficacy and safety of acupuncture for alleviating LOA in this population.MethodsThis multicenter, randomized, double-blind, sham-controlled trial will enroll 80 eligible patients with advanced lung cancer undergoing immunotherapy who experience LOA, defined as a Visual Analogue Scale (VAS) score ≥30 mm. Participants will be randomly assigned to either true acupuncture or sham acupuncture in a 1:1 ratio, administered over 24 sessions within a 12-week period. The primary outcome is the LOA response rate at week 12. Secondary outcomes include changes in LOA severity, nutritional and hematologic markers, patient-reported measures (appetite/cachexia, disease symptoms, psychological distress, and sleep), and tumor response. Safety and blinding success will also be assessed. Data will be analyzed using SPSS 20.0 and R software.DiscussionTo our knowledge, this is the first rigorously designed trial evaluating acupuncture for LOA in advanced lung cancer patients undergoing immunotherapy. The findings may inform integrative supportive care strategies for this patient population.

papers.abstract_en: RATIONALE AND OBJECTIVES: Organ-specific dose estimates are needed to characterize radiation exposure from repeated low-dose computed tomography (CT) lung cancer screening in the National Lung Screening Trial (NLST). The objective was to estimate study-level doses and participant-level cumulative doses in the NLST CT screening cohort. MATERIALS AND METHODS: This retrospective dosimetry study included 25,051 NLST CT screening participants from the Lung Screening Study and American College of Radiology Imaging Network components after excluding participants with any examination lacking a valid manufacturer-appropriate tube current-time input. Image-series metadata were linked with age, sex, height, and weight, and then valid records were grouped into 69,601 study-level screening examinations. Organ absorbed doses and effective dose were calculated using the National Cancer Institute dosimetry system for Computed Tomography with sex- and body-size-specific adult phantoms. Scan-range-related dose uncertainty was assessed with 50 stochastic simulations. RESULTS: Participants underwent a mean of 2.78 study-level screening examinations; the median study-level volume CT dose index was 3.30 mGy. Median (interquartile range) study-level lung, breast, heart wall, active marrow, and effective doses were 3.93 (3.13-4.96), 3.94 (3.14-5.04), 3.94 (3.14-5.01), and 1.26 (0.99-1.60) mGy, and 2.07 (1.65-2.59) mSv, respectively. Corresponding cumulative participant-level doses were 11.30 (8.89-14.50), 11.39 (9.01-14.75), 11.41 (8.93-14.66), and 3.63 (2.79-4.66) mGy, and 5.94 (4.69-7.64) mSv. Scan-range-related dose uncertainty was greatest for thyroid dose (mean coefficient of variation, 21.1%) and low for in-field organs. CONCLUSION: Using NLST low-dose CT screening data, we estimated participant-level cumulative organ and effective doses and characterized variation across organs and body-size groups.

papers.abstract_en: OBJECTIVE: To assess the added value of acetic acid chromoendoscopy (AAC) for the detection of dysplasia and oesophageal adenocarcinoma during Barrett's oesophagus surveillance endoscopies. DESIGN: Prospective, open label, stepped wedge cluster, randomised trial. SETTING: 18 Dutch community hospitals. PARTICIPANTS: Patients undergoing surveillance for Barrett's oesophagus were eligible, excluding those with known or previously treated dysplasia. INTERVENTIONS: Hospitals randomly shifted from surveillance without AAC (control) to AAC (intervention), with endoscopists trained before implementation. Targeted biopsies were obtained if lesions were present; random four quadrant biopsies were conducted. MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES: The primary endpoint was the neoplasia detection rate, defined as the percentage of participants with low grade dysplasia, high grade dysplasia, and oesophageal adenocarcinoma in any biopsy, confirmed by an experienced gastrointestinal pathologist. The secondary endpoint was the neoplasia detection rate in targeted biopsies. RESULTS: 2267 participants were included, of whom 1438 (63%) were allocated to surveillance without AAC and 829 (37%) to surveillance with AAC; AAC was applied in 679 (82%) allocated participants. Overall, neoplasia was diagnosed in 163 (7.2%) participants (111 (4.9%) low grade dysplasia, 30 (1.3%) high grade dysplasia, and 22 (1.0%) oesophageal adenocarcinoma). AAC use did not increase the neoplasia detection rate (7.4% (50/679) with AAC versus 7.1% (113/1588) without AAC; odds ratio 0.97, 95% confidence interval 0.65 to 1.44; adjusted for calendar time and Barrett's oesophagus length). Suspected lesions were detected in 95 (14.0%) participants receiving AAC versus 101 (6.4%) without AAC (P<0.001), but the targeted neoplasia detection rate was not higher (2.1% (14/679) versus 1.8% (29/1588); odds ratio 1.05, 0.49 to 2.24). CONCLUSIONS: Use of AAC did not improve detection of neoplasia in patients with Barrett's oesophagus undergoing endoscopic surveillance in routine clinical practice. papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: The tumor microenvironment exerts intense survival pressure on CD8+ tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes (TILs), yet the cellular basis for an earlier, less-exhausted state associated with response to immune checkpoint blockade (ICB) in non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC) remains unclear. We previously identified BCL2A1 as a CD8+ TIL-derived marker predictive of a response to PD-1 blockade. Here we combine deep single-cell discovery with experimental validation in primary human T cells to characterise the BCL2A1-associated CD8+ TIL state and its candidate upstream signal. METHODS: We integrated four transcriptomic cohorts-pre-treatment bulk RNA-seq with CD8+ TIL deconvolution (n=60), on-treatment scRNA-seq/TCR-seq (n=11), longitudinal scRNA-seq/TCR-seq (n=18), and an independent post-treatment cohort (n=59)-with in silico perturbation, pathway, and metabolic-flux analyses, and experimentally tested a key prediction of this state by flow cytometry in primary human CD8+ T cells. RESULTS: BCL2A1 high CD8+ TILs showed elevated BCL2A1 expression without coordinated upregulation of anti-apoptotic BCL2-family genes, maintained minimal exhaustion, and occupied an early, BCL6-, TCF7-, and NFKB1-regulated pseudotime state. Across longitudinal and post-treatment cohorts, they formed diverse, low-expansion repertoires rather than dominant expanded clones, with reduced biosynthetic flux (branched-chain amino acid and purine metabolism) consistent with a non-proliferative state. NF-κB signaling was elevated, and TNF-α was nominated as the leading candidate upstream ligand of BCL2A1. We then experimentally tested this prediction: in primary human CD8+ T cells, TNF-α induced BCL2A1 protein ≈13-fold (44.5% vs. 3.4% BCL2A1+; MFI 2.93-fold; P < 0.0001), whereas CD3/CD28 activation alone did not, establishing a TNF-α-specific, protein-level response. CONCLUSIONS: Combining integrative single-cell analysis with experimental validation in primary human T cells, we define BCL2A1 as a marker of an early, less-exhausted CD8+ TIL state associated with improved ICB outcomes in NSCLC; a survival-related role is supported by these associations but was not functionally tested.

papers.abstract_en: OBJECTIVE: Antibody-drug conjugates (ADCs) are being investigated in advanced small-cell lung cancer (SCLC), but the evidence is dominated by early-phase studies conducted in non-exchangeable treatment settings. We evaluated the activity and toxicity of ADCs while separating later-line monotherapy from frontline combination therapy, later-line combination therapy, and post-induction maintenance. METHODS: PubMed, Embase, the Cochrane Library, and Web of Science Core Collection were searched from inception and in 28 August 2026. ClinicalTrials.gov and the WHO International Clinical Trials Registry Platform (ICTRP) were searched on 28 August 2026. We constructed an arm-level dataset that recorded regimen, dose, clinical context, target, outcome definition, numerator, denominator, analysis set, and source. The primary quantitative synthesis was restricted to second-line or later ADC monotherapy; other clinical contexts were summarized descriptively. Single-arm proportions were synthesized using a binomial-normal random-intercept generalized linear mixed model on the logit scale. We reported 95% confidence intervals (CIs), between-study variance, heterogeneity, and 95% prediction intervals. An inverse-variance logit random-effects model with restricted maximum likelihood estimation and Hartung-Knapp inference was used as a sensitivity analysis. Fixed-time Kaplan-Meier survival estimates and inconsistently defined common adverse events were not pooled. RESULTS: 16 trial families evaluating eight ADCs across five target classes met the eligibility criteria. In the primary later-line monotherapy analysis, the pooled ORR was 25.7% (95% CI, 16.4%-37.9%), and the pooled DCR was 72.7% (95% CI, 60.7%-82.2%). The pooled incidences of grade ≥3 TEAEs and grade ≥3 TRAEs were 62.8% (95% CI, 59.6%-65.9%) and 45.5% (95% CI, 35.5%-56.0%), respectively. The prediction intervals for ORR, DCR, and grade ≥3 TRAEs were wide. Proportions observed in a new study may therefore differ substantially from the pooled estimates. Frontline combinations, later-line combinations, and maintenance therapy yielded context-specific signals but were not compared with later-line monotherapy. Target-stratified analyses were exploratory; B7-H3 and DLL3 estimates were based on small, non-comparative groups, whereas Trop-2 and SEZ6 were not pooled because fewer than three studies were available. CONCLUSIONS: Later-line ADC monotherapy showed antitumor activity but frequent clinically important toxicity, with substantial between-study variation. The evidence does not establish superiority by treatment line, regimen, agent, or molecular target; single-arm response estimates also do not demonstrate a survival benefit. Randomized, context-specific trials using harmonized efficacy and safety definitions are needed.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: In extensive-stage small cell lung cancer (ES-SCLC), lurbinectedin is approved for first-line maintenance treatment with atezolizumab and as monotherapy following disease progression, but prospective real-world data on its use are lacking. METHODS: Jazz EMERGE 402 was a prospective, observational, phase 4 trial (NCT04894591) that evaluated lurbinectedin for previously treated SCLC in a diverse, real-world population. The primary endpoint was overall response rate (ORR). Key secondary endpoints were progression-free survival (PFS), overall survival (OS), and safety. RESULTS: As of July 17, 2025, 267 patients received ≥ 1 lurbinectedin dose. At baseline, the median age was 67 years, 52 (19%) patients had an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group score ≥ 2, 67 (25%) had brain metastases, and 88 (33%) had platinum-resistant disease. ORR (95% confidence interval [CI]) was 29% (23%-36%) overall (n = 189) and 33% (25%-42%) in second-line treatment (n = 118). Patients with brain metastases had lower ORR (17% vs 32% without; odds ratio, 0.28 [95% CI: 0.10-0.76]). Median (95% CI) PFS and OS were 3.3 (2.6-4.1) and 7.6 (6.4-8.7) months. OS was shorter with platinum-resistant vs platinum-sensitive disease (5.8 vs 9.3 months; hazard ratio, 1.63 [95% CI: 1.17-2.28]). Eighty-eight (33%) patients had treatment-related adverse events, including anemia (8%) and neutropenia (7%); 21 (8%) discontinued treatment due to adverse events. CONCLUSIONS: In a broad, real-world population with previously treated SCLC, lurbinectedin was associated with clinically meaningful effectiveness and predictable and manageable safety. Lower ORR and OS were seen in patients with brain metastases and platinum-resistant disease, respectively.

papers.abstract_en: Lymph nodes (LNs), principal sites of antitumor immunity, may undergo immune-mediated regression; whether neoadjuvant chemoimmunotherapy (NCIT)-induced regression indicates prognosis in esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC) remains unclear. We aimed to establish and validate a lymph node regression grade (LNRG) system for prognostic stratification. This multicenter, retrospective cohort study analyzed 965 patients receiving PD-1-based NCIT and surgery at three Chinese tertiary cancer centers. LNRG was the ratio of summed viable tumor area to summed bed area (residual viable plus regressed preexisting tumor) across all dissected LNs. Negative LNs were assigned LNRG 0. Survival and predictive performance were assessed using Kaplan-Meier/Cox regression, time-dependent area under the curve, Brier score, net reclassification improvement, and integrated discrimination improvement. Overall, 28,882 LNs were evaluated; patients were classified as LNRG 0-4 in 385 (39.9%), 150 (15.5%), 26 (2.7%), 141 (14.6%), and 263 (27.3%), respectively. LNRG independently predicted disease-free and overall survival, with Grades 1-2 conferring the most favorable outcomes and Grade 4 the poorest. A random survival forest model incorporating LNRG, tumor regression grade, ypAJCC stage, and perineural invasion predicted 2-year disease-free survival in training and external validation cohorts. LNRG is a novel, independent prognostic indicator after NCIT.
