papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Radioiodine (RAI) alone exhibited limited efficacy in distant metastatic differentiated thyroid cancer (DTC). We hypothesized that pretreatment with anlotinib, a potent antiangiogenic tyrosine kinase inhibitor, would reduce tumor burden and improve therapeutic response. METHODS: This prospective, single-arm phase II trial enrolled patients with measurable distant metastatic DTC. All patients received anlotinib 12 mg/day orally for 12 weeks. After confirmation of RAI-avid target lesions on diagnostic ¹³¹I-WBS, patients were treated with 7.4 GBq RAI and followed up for another 12 weeks. Sequential therapy continued until no effect of RAI could be anticipated. Primary endpoints were objective response rate (ORR) and safety. Registered with the Chinese Clinical Trial Registry (ChiCTR2100045178; https://www.chictr.org.cn). RESULTS: 24 patients were enrolled. 14 (58%) were excluded due to non-RAI-avid target lesions; 10 (42%) with RAI-avid lesions received sequential therapy (median, 4.5 cycles). ORR was 60% (all partial responses), disease control rate 100%. With median follow-up 34.5 months, no disease progression or death occurred. In the subgroup of eight patients with bone target lesions, ORR was 50%. Grade 3 anlotinib-related adverse events occurred in 30% of patients; no grade 4/5 toxicities or grade ≥2 RAI-related events were observed. CONCLUSION: Sequential anlotinib followed by RAI therapy demonstrated promising antitumor activity (ORR 60%) and favorable safety in RAI-avid distant metastatic DTC, particularly in bone metastases. These findings are hypothesis-generating and require validation in a randomized trial with an RAI monotherapy control arm.

papers.abstract_en: INTRODUCTION: Although first-line immune-based combinations have reshaped the management of metastatic renal cell carcinoma (mRCC), relevant unmet clinical needs remain. Sarcomatoid feature is a negative prognostic factor that confers sensitivity to immunotherapy, yet the optimal ICI combination in this subgroup is still unclear. METHODS: The Meet-URO 33 is an Italian multicenter retrospective/prospective observational study enrolling patients with mRCC receiving first-line systemic therapy in routine clinical practice. In the present sub-analysis, objective response and survival outcomes were compared between ICI-ICI and ICI-TKI regimens in patients with documented sarcomatoid differentiation and IMDC intermediate-/poor-risk disease. RESULTS: Among 1695 patients enrolled from 58 centers, 180 (10.6%) had sRCC and among them, 107 (58.2%) were intermediate-risk and 56 (30.4%) were poor-risk. With a median follow-up of 21.8 months, in the I/P-sRCC population with available data (n = 155), univariable analysis showed longer overall survival (OS) with ICI-ICI compared to ICI-TKI (HR 0.58, p = 0.04). However, in propensity score-weighted analyses, point estimates slightly favored ICI-ICI, but no statistically significant differences were observed for OS, PFS, or ORR. CONCLUSIONS: In this real-world analysis comparing ICI-ICI and ICI-TKI in sarcomatoid mRCC, propensity score-weighted models showed no statistically significant differences between treatment combinations on clinical outcomes. These findings highlight the relevance of baseline disease and patients characteristics in shaping treatment outcomes and confirm the effectiveness of ICI-containing combinations in the treatment of sarcomatoid mRCC.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Reduced skeletal muscle (SM) quantity and quality may influence outcomes in bladder cancer, but most studies are associative and vulnerable to confounding and inconsistent covariate adjustment. We applied a directed acyclic graph (DAG)-informed framework to evaluate associations between computed tomography-derived SM characteristics and overall survival (OS) in patients receiving curative-intent radiotherapy-based bladder preservation or radical cystectomy. METHODS: This retrospective two-centre cohort study included patients treated between 2014 and 2024. Computed tomography imaging closest to definitive local therapy was analysed using an automated segmentation pipeline to quantify SM quantity, expressed as skeletal muscle index (SMI), and quality, expressed as intramuscular adipose tissue ratio (IMATR). A DAG was used to prespecify the adjustment strategy, and Cox models were fitted separately within radiotherapy and surgical cohorts. RESULTS: The final cohorts comprised 353 radiotherapy-treated and 117 surgically treated patients. In the radiotherapy cohort, higher SMI was associated with improved OS (HR 0.79, 95% CI 0.66-0.94, p = 0.007), while higher IMATR was associated with worse OS (HR 1.24, 95% CI 1.04-1.48, p = 0.014). In the smaller surgical cohort, point estimates were directionally discordant with the radiotherapy findings and imprecise: SMI HR 1.35 (95% CI 0.99-1.85, p = 0.057) and IMATR HR 0.86 (95% CI 0.62-1.21, p = 0.39). CONCLUSIONS: In this DAG-informed analysis, higher SMI and lower IMATR were associated with improved OS in radiotherapy-treated patients. Surgical estimates were imprecise and should be considered exploratory. These findings are hypothesis-generating and support further evaluation of CT-derived muscle characteristics as prognostic markers within radiotherapy-treated populations but cannot yet establish a differential benefit for radiotherapy vs cystectomy.

papers.abstract_en: Tumor-associated macrophages (TAMs) are pivotal orchestrators of immune evasion, yet the functional significance of the calcineurin signaling pathway in TAM plasticity remains elusive. Analyzing TCGA Lung Cancer datasets and clinical samples, we identified PPP3CA as the major calcineurin catalytic subunit in TAMs, whose downregulation correlates with poor patient survival and tumor progression. Myeloid-specific Ppp3ca knockout in mice accelerated tumor growth, reducing anti-tumor M1-like macrophages and CD8+ T cells while enriching pro-tumor M2-like TAMs. In vitro assays confirmed that Ppp3ca deficiency impaired the polarization of TAMs toward the M1 type. Mechanistically, we demonstrated that PPP3CA-mediated regulation of TAM plasticity is dependent on the NF-κB signaling pathway, as Ppp3ca loss significantly blunted NF-κB activation. Furthermore, pharmacological inhibition of calcineurin using cyclosporin A (CsA) effectively recapitulated the myeloid-deficient phenotype, shifting TAMs toward a pro-tumorigenic M2 state and promoting tumor malignancy, providing an experimental explanation for the elevated cancer risk associated with clinical calcineurin inhibitor (CNI) use. Collectively, our findings identify the PPP3CA-NF-κB axis as a pivotal regulator of macrophage plasticity and provide a high-value translational basis for targeting this pathway to remodel the TME in lung cancer immunotherapy.

papers.abstract_en: OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the efficacy and safety of tislelizumab combined with nab-paclitaxel plus nedaplatin for advanced esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC), and its effects on serum tumor markers and inflammatory cytokines. METHODS: A total of 228 advanced ESCC patients were retrospectively enrolled and divided into an observation group (tislelizumab combined with nab-paclitaxel plus nedaplatin, n=114) and a control group (chemotherapy alone: nab-paclitaxel plus nedaplatin, n=114). Related serological indicators, T lymphocyte subsets, quality of life, short-term efficacy, pathological response, survival outcomes and adverse reactions were compared. Independent prognostic factors were analyzed via univariate and multivariate Cox regression. RESULTS: After treatment, both groups exhibited decreased levels of tumor markers, inflammatory cytokines, soluble PD-1, PD-L1, VEGF and MMP-9, with lower levels in the observation group (all P<0.05). The observation group had improved immune function, higher SF-36 scores, as well as higher objective response rate, disease control rate, and pathological response indexes (all P<0.05). Moreover, patients in the observation group had longer progression-free survival and overall survival (both P<0.05). Advanced TNM stage was an adverse prognostic factor, while combined immunochemotherapy reduced mortality risk. CONCLUSION: Tislelizumab plus the dual chemotherapy regimen can effectively reduce serum tumor markers and alleviate tumor-related inflammation, improve immune status, quality of life and survival of patients with advanced ESCC with acceptable safety, supporting its potential for broader clinical application.

papers.abstract_en: Non-SMC condensin I complex subunit G (NCAPG) is implicated in tumor progression and TGF-β pathway activation, yet its roles in oncogenesis and immune modulation within the lung squamous cell carcinoma (LUSC) microenvironment remain largely unexplored. Here, we used bioinformatics analysis to identify key upregulated genes in LUSC and assessed the effects of NCAPG and its upstream regulator E2F transcription factor 8 (E2F8) on malignant phenotypes via gain- and loss-of-function assays in NCI-H226 and NCI-H1703 LUSC cell lines, with in vivo efficacy validated using KLN205 cell isografts and NTCU-induced primary LUSC mouse models. Neutrophil polarization, neutrophil extracellular trap (NET) formation, and CD8⁺ T cell cytotoxicity was analyzed in co-culture systems and tumor tissues. Arundanine was identified as a potential NCAPG inhibitor via molecular docking and tested as monotherapy or in combination with anti-PD-1 therapy. We found that NCAPG was significantly upregulated in LUSC, and NCAPG depletion markedly impaired LUSC cell proliferation, migration, and invasion while promoting apoptosis. Mechanistically, NCAPG activated TGF-β signaling, which drove pro-tumor N2 neutrophil polarization and induced NETosis; these NETs upregulated PD-L1 expression on tumor cells and suppressed the expansion and cytotoxic function of CD8⁺ T cells. E2F8 was found to transcriptionally activate NCAPG by directly binding to its promoter. Furthermore, Arundanine destabilized NCAPG protein, suppressed TGF-β-mediated NET formation, and potentiated anti-PD-1 therapy to significantly prolong survival in LUSC models. Collectively, the E2F8/NCAPG axis promotes LUSC progression by orchestrating a TGF-β-driven immunosuppressive microenvironment, and targeting NCAPG with Arundanine represents a promising therapeutic strategy to overcome immune evasion and sensitize LUSC to PD-1 blockade.

papers.abstract_en: OBJECTIVES: The aim of this study is to evaluate the application, methodology and consistency of utility values used in National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE) single technology appraisals (STAs) of targeted therapies for advanced or metastatic non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC) over the past decade. METHODS: A review was conducted of NICE STAs of NSCLC targeted therapies from 2012 to 2022, focusing on four key aspects: (1) utility values per health state as defined by the economic model structure; 2) the primary sources of these utility values; (3) the methods used to derive utilities for quality of life, and 4) the application of disutilities or utility decrements. RESULTS: In the included 16 appraisals for targeted therapies, substantial variation was identified in the application, methodology, and consistency of utility values used in CUAs appraised by NICE over the past decade. Most appraisals used health state-specific utilities, with progression free values primarily derived from clinical trials and progressed disease values more often derived from external literature. Disutilities for adverse events were applied in an inconsistent way and no stratification by age was reported. CONCLUSION: Enhancing methodological consistency and incorporating up-to-date, representative utility data, particularly for progressed disease and adverse events, would strengthen the robustness, transparency and comparability of NICE technology appraisals of targeted therapies in NSCLC.

papers.abstract_en: Anti-angiogenic therapies provide clinically meaningful benefit in selected treatment settings for advanced non-small cell lung cancer, but durable responses are limited by heterogeneous and adaptive resistance. This resistance is not solely tumor-intrinsic; it emerges from interactions among tumor plasticity, compensatory angiogenic signaling, hypoxia, stromal and immune remodeling, vascular recovery, and alternative blood-supply mechanisms. These processes require different biological variables and therefore cannot be adequately interrogated by a single experimental model. Patient-derived lung cancer organoids preserve patient-specific tumor features and are useful for studying tumor-intrinsic responses, but tumor-only organoids do not reproduce perfusion-dependent vascular physiology, permeability, or drug-delivery dynamics. Microenvironment-integrated co-culture, vascularization, and microfluidic or perfusion engineering can extend these capabilities, although model complexity alone does not establish stronger evidence. This review integrates the clinical and mechanistic basis of anti-angiogenic resistance with the capabilities and limitations of current lung cancer organoid models and other three-dimensional systems. We propose a mechanism-matched framework linking the resistance mechanism to the required variable, the minimum set of model capabilities, and claim-matched readouts. Particular emphasis is placed on distinguishing structural from functional vascularization, tumor drug response from anti-angiogenic resistance, and acute treatment effects from acquired resistance. Current lung cancer organoid systems can model tumor-intrinsic and selected microenvironment-mediated responses and, increasingly, vascular responses, but direct longitudinal evidence of acquired anti-angiogenic resistance remains limited. Future progress will depend on fit-for-purpose standardization, functional qualification, longitudinal modeling, and prospective alignment with clinically observed resistance trajectories.

papers.abstract_en: This study examined the association of surgical approach with operative and postoperative outcomes as well as margin and nodal outcomes after complex segmentectomy, comparing mini-thoracotomy (MT) with multiportal minimally invasive thoracic surgery (mMITS) and, within mMITS, video-assisted thoracic surgery (mVATS) with multiportal robot-assisted thoracic surgery (mRATS), using propensity score matching (PSM). The study cohort comprised 808 consecutive patients treated with complex segmentectomy for suspected malignant pulmonary tumors from January 2015 through July 2026. Of these, 138 underwent MT and 670 mMITS, including 605 mVATS and 65 mRATS. PSM (1:2) was performed for MT versus mMITS (n = 126 vs. 252) and mVATS versus mRATS (n = 126 vs. 63). We assessed operative outcomes, postoperative complications, pain-related outcomes only for the mVATS-mRATS comparison, and margin and nodal outcomes. Blood loss was lower with mMITS than with MT (5 vs. 20 mL, p < 0.001), and chest tube duration was shorter (p = 0.002). Margin and nodal outcomes did not differ significantly between MT and mMITS. mRATS was associated with less blood loss than mVATS (3 vs. 5 mL, p = 0.006), a shorter duration of regular oral analgesic use (20 vs. 31 days, p = 0.007), and greater hilar and mediastinal lymph node yields (hilar, p = 0.037; mediastinal, p = 0.025). For complex segmentectomy, mMITS was associated with less blood loss and shorter chest tube duration than MT, without significant differences in margin and nodal outcomes. Within mMITS, mRATS was associated with shorter regular oral analgesic use and greater hilar and mediastinal lymph node yields than mVATS.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Ambient temperature has been associated with acute exacerbations of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (AECOPD), but evidence on seasonal lag patterns and susceptible populations remains limited. We characterized lag-specific and cumulative temperature-AECOPD associations during cold and warm seasons. METHODS: Using the Korean National Health Insurance Service-National Sample Cohort (2006-2019), we conducted a time-stratified case-crossover study with referent days matched by year, season, and day of the week. Cold-season exposure was defined as 2-m air temperature (November-April), and warm-season exposure as wet-bulb globe temperature (WBGT; May-October). Conditional quasi-Poisson distributed lag non-linear models estimated lag-specific and cumulative relative risks (RRs) over 0-28 days, adjusting for season-specific meteorological variables, PM10, PM2.5, and public holidays. Effect modification by age, sex, smoking, and body mass index (BMI) was examined. RESULTS: Among 5981 AECOPD events, lower cold-season temperatures were associated with delayed, sustained risk increases over lag days 6-23, peaking at lag 14-18 (RR = 1.23; 95% confidence interval (CI) 1.04-1.46). Higher warm-season WBGTs were associated with an immediate increase, peaking at lag 0-1 (RR = 1.06; 95% CI 1.02-1.10), which attenuated within 1 week. Cumulative exposure-response curves were monotonic for cold-season temperature and inverted U-shaped for warm-season WBGT. Associations were stronger in men, older adults, smokers, and those with a BMI ≥25. CONCLUSION: Cold- and warm-season ambient temperature metrics showed distinct temporal associations with AECOPD, delayed in the cold season and immediate in the warm season. Associations appeared relatively stronger among older adults, men, smokers, and individuals with higher BMI.

papers.abstract_en: OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the efficacy and safety of first-line third-generation EGFR-tyrosine kinase inhibitor (EGFR-TKI) combined with pemetrexed-platinum chemotherapy in patients with EGFR-mutant advanced lung adenocarcinoma and brain parenchymal metastases. METHODS: A bicenter retrospective cohort study was conducted. A total of 150 eligible patients were enrolled and balanced by 1:1 propensity score matching. Tumor response, survival outcomes, and treatment-related adverse events were compared between groups. RESULTS: After matching, 60 patients were assigned to each group. The intracranial objective response rate was 78.3% in the combination group versus 61.7% in the monotherapy group (P = 0.046). The median intracranial progression-free survival was 28.3 months in the combination group (hazard ratio = 0.536, 95% confidence interval: 0.350-0.820, P = 0.002). Systemic progression-free survival and overall survival were also significantly prolonged in the combination arm. Adverse events were predominantly chemotherapy-related toxicities and were generally manageable. CONCLUSION: First-line third-generation EGFR-TKI plus pemetrexed-platinum chemotherapy is associated with superior intracranial and systemic survival benefits in EGFR-mutant lung adenocarcinoma patients with brain parenchymal metastases, with a favorable safety profile. This study provides real-world evidence to support clinical treatment decision-making.

papers.abstract_en: Antibody-drug conjugates (ADCs) are emerging therapeutic options for epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR)-mutant non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) after the development of resistance to EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitors (EGFR-TKIs). However, the founding EGFR alteration alone does not guide ADC selection. At progression, actionable resistance mechanisms, altered antigen expression, central nervous system (CNS) involvement, spatial heterogeneity, and histological transformation may shift treatment priorities. This narrative review links agent-specific evidence boundaries to an eight-domain assessment of the post-progression disease state and distinguishes ADC eligibility from therapeutic priority. The framework first identifies clinical scenarios requiring immediate local, CNS-directed, or lineage-specific treatment. It then evaluates resistance-directed therapy and other systemic options in the context of prior treatment. Finally, each ADC is assessed according to its evidence base, biomarkers, construct fit, disease distribution, availability, and patient-specific safety. Currently, selected TROP2-directed ADCs have the most mature evidence. HER3-directed therapy remains under investigation, whereas c-Met- and human epidermal growth factor receptor 2-directed ADCs may be relevant in biomarker-defined settings. Tissue biopsy, plasma circulating tumor DNA analysis, and selected cerebrospinal fluid testing should be considered when the findings could alter clinical management. Accordingly, ADCs should be positioned relative to competing local and systemic strategies rather than considered a uniform post-osimertinib class. Prospective validation is required to determine whether this framework improves treatment outcomes.

ROS1 fusions are oncogenic drivers in a range of cancers and are identified in approximately 1-2% of NSCLCs. Zidesamtinib potently inhibits diverse ROS1 fusion proteins and clinically relevant ROS1 resistance mutations. Further, zidesamtinib has been shown to induce intracranial tumour regression in xenograft models. This article summarises the milestones in the development of zidesamtinib leading to this first approval for advanced ROS1-positive NSCLC.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: The acute inpatient symptom state following oesophagectomy is multidimensional and heterogeneous. However, the structure, between-patient heterogeneity, and network features of symptoms remain incompletely characterised. METHOD: We analysed 1047 postoperative patients with oesophageal cancer from four hospitals in Anhui Province, China, in the "Be Resilient to Oesophageal Cancer" program. We applied principal component analysis to summarise symptom dimensions and latent profile analysis to derive patient groups of symptom burden. Symptom networks were estimated and centrality computed to identify candidate targets. We then performed in silico node-perturbation simulations to estimate potential system-level effects of alleviating versus aggravating individual symptoms. RESULTS: Four symptom dimensions emerged from the principal component analysis: somatic discomfort and fatigue, psychological distress, social functioning impairment, and gastrointestinal/appetite-related symptoms. A low-burden group (80.2%) and a high-burden group (19.8%) were identified. The overall network's most central symptom was "reduced social interaction" (r = 2.52). Within groups, "worry" was most central in the low-burden group (r = 2.08), whereas "incision pain" was most central in the high-burden group (r=2.56). Computer simulations revealed that, within alleviating interventions, somatic symptoms accounted for the highest proportion across all symptom types (incision pain: -20.68% to -9.17%). Conversely, within aggravating interventions, psychosocial symptoms constituted the largest share in both the overall symptom network and the low-burden group (helplessness: 24.13% to 30.27%), whereas somatic symptoms dominated the high-burden group (incision pain: 9.17%). CONCLUSION: A multimethod pipeline identified reduced social interaction, worry, and incision pain as profile-specific, structurally prominent symptoms within the postoperative day 3 symptom networks. These findings highlight distinct psychosocial and somatic features across symptom-burden profiles and provide hypotheses for subsequent longitudinal and interventional studies.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Thymic epithelial tumors (TETs) are rare mediastinal tumors classified according to the WHO classification system. Classification can be challenging due to overlapping histological features. Subtyping on biopsy specimens is often inaccurate due to tumor heterogeneity and sampling effect. Since 2012 an international thymic tumor pathology expert panel is available in the Netherlands. This study evaluates the added value of this panel by assessing the discrepancies in diagnosis, inter-observer agreement and concordance on diagnosis between biopsy and the subsequent resection specimen. METHODS: All pathology excerpts from 2012 until 2024 for patients diagnosed with a thymic tumor were extracted from the national PALGA database and evaluated for histological subtype, assessment and the thymoma panel result. RESULTS: In total 1163 resection and 304 biopsy specimens were included, of which 36.1% were submitted to the thymoma panel. The diagnosis changed in 15.7% of cases after assessment. The subtypes AB and Bmix were most often submitted to the thymoma panel and the diagnosis changed most often for subtype A, B3 or Bmix. In 72.8% the concordance between the panel members exceeded 90%. The biopsy diagnosis varied from the resection diagnosis in 46.8%, but the differentiation between thymoma and thymic carcinoma was accurate on biopsy. CONCLUSION: A panel of dedicated pathologists with experience in thymic abnormalities contributed substantially to a more accurate classification of TETs, thereby guiding optimal treatment planning and prognostic evaluation. Despite the discrepancies between biopsy and resection specimens, distinguishing thymoma from thymic carcinoma was accurate on biopsy.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) has a spatially heterogeneous immune microenvironment, but the compartment-specific distribution of tumor-associated neutrophils (TANs) and its relationship with systemic inflammation remain incompletely defined. This study characterized CD177-defined neutrophil populations and other immune components across HCC tissue compartments and examined their associations with peripheral neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR). METHODS: Paired tumor center (TC), tumor margin/interface (IM), and adjacent non-neoplastic liver (NNL) specimens from 28 patients with HCC were analyzed using immunofluorescence microscopy and quantitative immunohistochemistry. Total neutrophil elastase-positive (NE+) and CD177+NE+ neutrophils, CD8+ lymphocytes, CD68+ and CD163+ macrophages, and CD34+ microvascular density were quantified. RESULTS: Total NE+ neutrophil density differed across compartments and was higher in both tumor-associated compartments than in NNL (median: TC, 46.40 cells/mm²; IM, 39.65 cells/mm²; NNL, 8.80 cells/mm²; P < 0.001). CD177+NE+ density showed a modest compartmental effect and was higher in the TC than at the IM (RR 2.68, 95% CI 1.20-6.02; Holm-adjusted P = 0.050). In contrast, the CD177+ fraction among total NE+ neutrophils was markedly lower in both tumor-associated compartments than in NNL (median: TC, 17.63%; IM, 10.90%; NNL, 88.08%; P < 0.001)among, accompanied by substantial enrichment of estimated NE+CD177- neutrophils. CD8+ lymphocytes preferentially accumulated at the IM, whereas CD34+ microvascular density followed a TC>IM>NNL gradient. CD68+ macrophages were more abundant in NNL, while CD163+ macrophage density showed a modest overall compartment effect (mixed-effects P = 0.037), and the CD163/CD68 macrophage-polarization index was higher in the TC than at the IM (P = 0.009). In exploratory analyses, higher preoperative NLR was associated with the CD163/CD68 macrophage-polarization index specifically in the TC (ρ = 0.451, P = 0.016; q = 0.048), but not with neutrophil abundance, CD177-defined distribution, or patient-level neutrophil spatial-distribution indices. CONCLUSIONS: HCC exhibits marked spatial myeloid heterogeneity, characterized by neutrophil enrichment in tumor-associated compartments, compartmental differences in CD177-defined populations, and compartment-specific macrophage polarization. These findings, generated using a practical tissue-based immunophenotyping approach applicable to routinely processed specimens, warrant validation in larger mechanistic studies.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Myelin oligodendrocyte glycoprotein antibody-associated disease (MOGAD) is an autoimmune inflammatory demyelinating disorder of the central nervous system with a broad clinical spectrum that includes brainstem syndromes. Evidence supporting neonatal Fc receptor (FcRn) inhibition in MOGAD remains limited. CASE PRESENTATION: A 37-year-old woman presented with a MOGAD-associated brainstem syndrome characterized by diplopia, ocular-motor abnormalities, right facial weakness, and gait instability. Brain MRI demonstrated a lesion in the right middle cerebellar peduncle near the fourth ventricle. CSF analysis showed 2 leukocytes/µL, 0 erythrocytes/µL, normal protein (0.328 g/L), a type II oligoclonal-band pattern, and an elevated IgG index of 1.8 (reference value, <0.7), supporting intrathecal IgG synthesis. Serum MOG-IgG was positive by live cell-based assay. High-dose corticosteroids were discussed, but the patient declined them because of concerns regarding adverse effects. IVIG was subject to intermittent local shortage and substantial financial burden, while PLEX was considered disproportionate to the clinical severity. The patient received individualized off-label intravenous efgartigimod (20 mg/kg on Days 1 and 5) and improved clinically. After the second relapse, the same efgartigimod regimen was repeated, and low-dose oral prednisone and MMF were initiated for relapse prevention. Prednisone was discontinued approximately 5 months after initiation, whereas MMF was continued as maintenance therapy. At follow-up approximately 18 months after discharge, the patient was clinically asymptomatic. DISCUSSION: This case documents a recognized brainstem MOGAD presentation with clinical improvement temporally associated with individualized off-label FcRn inhibition. Interpretation should consider the single-case design, absence of a comparator, rehabilitation, low-dose prednisone and MMF initiated for relapse prevention, and the natural course of the disease. This observation provides preliminary clinical context for prospective evaluation of FcRn inhibition but is insufficient to establish efficacy.

This study identified MAN1B1 as a key driving factor for chemotherapy resistance and malignant progression in BC. GSEA analysis is used to explore pathways associated with key genes. Perform single-cell analysis using Seurat, SingleR, Monocle 2, CellChat, and scTenifoldKnk, including cell annotation, pseudo time trajectory, intercellular communication, and virtual knockout. Carry out functional experiments in bladder cancer cell lines, including cell viability, wound healing Transwell, Colony formation and Western blot analysis. RESULTS: Through comprehensive transcriptome analysis and single-cell sequencing, we found that elevated levels of MAN1B1 are associated with poorer clinical outcomes. Computational molecular docking and molecular dynamics simulations indicate the potential binding interaction between MAN1B1 and GEM.This enzyme orchestrates a dual microenvironmental reprogramming by hyperactivating metabolic cascades while simultaneously dampening anti-tumor immune surveillance, predominantly originating from the epithelial compartment to modulate intercellular crosstalk. Functional disturbance experiments showed that knockout of MAN1B1 was associated with decreased cell survival, migration, and invasion, as well as increased sensitivity to GEM, while ectopic expression of MAN1B1 increased cell survival and was associated with enhanced PI3K/AKT/mTOR pathway activity. CONCLUSIONS: Our findings uncover the multifaceted regulatory network governing MAN1B1, establishing its utility as an innovative prognostic indicator and an actionable therapeutic vulnerability for overcoming GEM insensitivity in urological oncology.

papers.abstract_en: Antibody fusion proteins incorporating immunomodulatory molecules, such as cytokines of the common γ-chain receptor family and costimulatory members of the TNF superfamily, hold great potential for cancer immunotherapy, with many candidates already advancing into clinical studies. However, the efficacy as single agent with one payload is limited and combinatorial approaches are required to fully exploit their immunomodulatory potential. Here, we describe a novel format of a trifunctional antibody fusion protein, composed of a tumor-directed Fab antibody fragment, specific for the fibroblast activation protein (FAP), fused to single-chain 4-1BBL in combination with either IL-15 connected to an IL-15Rα fragment or IL-21. Binding to target cells was confirmed, and activity was assessed on activated PBMCs either bound to target cells or in an untargeted setting. Combinatorial effects enhancing IFN-γ release were found to be targeting-dependent for both trifunctional antibody fusion proteins and superior to the activity observed with combined bifunctional antibody-fusion proteins carrying single payloads. In contrast, significant combined activity enhancing granzyme B expression was observed only for the trifunctional fusion protein containing sc4-1BBL/IL-21 and appeared to be targeting-independent. In 3D coculture settings of fibroblast spheroids and PBMCs, both trifunctional fusion proteins enhanced the cytotoxic effect of an EGFR-directed T cell engager (TCE) and cetuximab (CTX), whereby sc4-1BBL/IL-15 was more effective than sc4-1BBL/IL-21, and comparable effects were obtained by the respective bifunctional antibody-cytokines. The activity of antibody fusion proteins containing IL-15 was associated with strong activation of CD8+T cells, CD3+CD56+ T cells and NK cells, as well as enhanced proliferation, particularly in combination with TCE, expanding CD8+ T cells and NKT-like cells. Activation by fusion proteins containing IL-21 became mainly apparent in combination with TCE on CD8+ T cells and with CTX on NK cells, while proliferation was restricted to NK cells. Thus, the trifunctional antibody fusion proteins presenting sc4-1BBL/IL-15 and sc4-1BBL/IL-21 exhibit distinct patterns of combined activity and immune cell stimulation, both demonstrating combinatorial potential with TCE and CTX.

papers.abstract_en: INTRODUCTION: Serous ovarian cancer (SOC) is characterized by tumour heterogeneity, cellular plasticity, and immune suppression, contributing to limited therapeutic responses. Understanding tumour -immune dynamics at the cellular level is essential for developing personalized treatment strategies. METHODS: We established a patient-derived microtumour (MT) platform from solid tumour tissue and malignant ascites of 18 treatment-naïve SOC patients. Using multiparametric flow cytometry, we analysed plasticity-associated markers (CD10, CD24, CD44, CD90, CD133), immunoregulatory molecules (PD-L1, PVR, PVRL2, CD47, Calreticulin, CD39, CD73), and antigen presentation molecules (HLA-A/B/C, HLA-DR/DP/DQ) during short-term culture. RESULTS: Plasticity-associated marker expression was largely conserved across compartments, with substantial interpatient heterogeneity and only modest differences in an exploratory composite plasticity score. Compared with tumour-derived MTs, ascites-derived MTs exhibited significantly higher calreticulin expression and lower expression of the ectonucleotidase CD39. Short-term culture induced CD44 upregulation and CD90 downregulation as well as dynamic modulation of immune markers, such as increased PVR and PVRL2 expression. HLA expression showed substantial interindividual heterogeneity rather than clear compartment-specific differences. Co-expression analyses revealed associations between plasticity-associated and immunoregulatory features, such as CD10/CD24 with PD-L1 and CD47. Finally, exploratory autologous co-cultures demonstrated the feasibility of combining patient-derived MTs with matched immune cells. Two of five samples showed moderate responses to anti-PD-L1 and anti-TIGIT, reflected by increased granzyme B expression and accompanied by compensatory changes in TIGIT and PD-L1 expression. DISCUSSION: Taken together, these findings indicate an association between tumour cell plasticity and an immune-evasive phenotype in ovarian cancer and support patient-derived MTs as an exploratory short-term platform for capturing patient-specific tumour -immune interactions, while highlighting dynamic immune checkpoint molecule expression during cultivation.

papers.abstract_en: Spring viremia of carp virus (SVCV) severely threatens cyprinid aquaculture, yet the role of autophagy in SVCV infection remains unclear. Here, SVCV infection was associated with enhanced autophagic activity and autophagic flux in common carp and EPC cells. Pharmacological perturbation of autophagy revealed that rapamycin treatment increased SVCV gene expression and aggravated SVCV-induced cytopathic effects, whereas chloroquine blocked autophagic flux, suppressed viral gene expression, and mitigated virus-induced cellular damage. Transcriptomic analysis identified 1,868 differentially expressed genes after chloroquine treatment, with major changes in lysosome/autophagy-related pathways, glycan degradation, ion transport, cell cycle, DNA replication, and DNA repair. Metabolomic and integrated multi-omics analyses revealed changes in amino sugar and nucleotide sugar metabolism, steroid biosynthesis, riboflavin metabolism, and amino acid metabolism. Functional validation showed that diflorasone and all-trans-retinal reduced SVCV-G expression, alleviated cytopathic effects, and improved survival after SVCV infection. These findings suggest that SVCV infection is associated with enhanced autophagic flux, whereas chloroquine treatment blocks autophagic flux and is accompanied by reduced SVCV gene expression.

papers.abstract_en: Lentivirus (LV)-based manipulation of immune cells is a commonly used approach in cell therapies. However, the most frequently used Vesicular Stomatitis Virus Glycoprotein (VSV-G) pseudotyping approach is inefficient to support LV gene delivery of mouse immune cells due to the lack of an optimal entry receptor. Here, we present a transgenic mouse model with Cre recombinase-inducible expression of the human Low Density Lipoprotein Receptor (hLDLR), the natural entry receptor of VSV-G LV. Surprisingly, we found that Cre induces robust hLDLR expression across multiple immune cells only under activation conditions. Induction of hLDLR expression by genetic crossing with Cre-transgenic mice or exposure to Cre mRNA-lipid nanoparticles (LNPs) potently sensitized murine immune cells, especially T cells, to VSV-G LV-mediated gene delivery. This novel transgenic mouse model serves as a valuable tool for investigating immune cell function and engineered cell therapies for cancer in syngeneic mouse models.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Rabies remains a devastating zoonotic disease, with prevention measures relying heavily on post-exposure prophylaxis (PEP). Evaluating rabies vaccine potency traditionally relies on the in vivo National Institutes of Health (NIH) mouse challenge assay, which is limited by long testing cycles, low reproducibility, and high animal consumption. Developing broad-spectrum monoclonal antibodies (mAbs) and alternative in vitro assays is essential to advance rabies prevention and improve vaccine quality control. METHODS: In this study, we characterized three human-mouse chimeric mAbs (05-2F10, 06-2A12, and 07-4D8-1C1) with broad-spectrum neutralizing activity. Leveraging in vitro pseudovirus neutralization assays, we evaluated candidate mAbs for high neutralizing capacity and low sensitivity to variation to select optimal pairs for assay development. Using these selected mAbs, a double-antibody sandwich ELISA was established to quantify glycoprotein (G) antigen content in human rabies vaccines. RESULTS: The three chimeric mAbs exhibited exceptional in vitro neutralization potency and breadth. The established double-antibody sandwich ELISA successfully quantified G antigen content in human rabies vaccines. Importantly, a high correlation was demonstrated between the antigen content quantified by this ELISA and the potency data generated via the traditional in vivo NIH mouse challenge test. CONCLUSION: Collectively, these findings provide a robust technical framework for replacing the traditional NIH potency assay with a reliable in vitro method, fully aligning with the 3Rs principles of animal welfare.

papers.abstract_en: Radioresistance severely compromises radiotherapy efficacy for lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD), yet the intrinsic heterogeneity of cellular radioresponses among isogenic tumor cells remains poorly characterized. Here, we integrated single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) and single-cell assay for transposase-accessible chromatin with high-throughput sequencing (scATAC-seq) to dissect the transcriptional and regulatory landscape underlying heterogeneous radioresponses in single-cell-derived LUAD cells following 6 Gy γ-ray irradiation. We found that isogenic LUAD cells harbored intrinsic molecular determinants for divergent radiosensitivity and displayed heterogeneous radioresponsiveness upon irradiation. A radiation-associated transcriptional cell state, coupled with DNA damage repair, apoptosis, and cell cycle regulation, emerged at 6 h post-irradiation. Inhibition of lysine demethylase 4B (KDM4B) enhanced LUAD radiosensitivity by intensifying DNA damage, whereas reduced expression of cyclin B1 (CCNB1) and DNA topoisomerase IIα (TOP2A) potentially contributed to radiation-triggered G2/M arrest. Notably, the radiation-associated regulatory cell state emerged earlier than radiation-induced transcriptional cell state. RNA polymerase II subunit A (POLR2A) functioned as a core regulator in high-responsive LUAD cells. Based on these findings, we proposed a hypothesis for the radiosensitization of LUAD cells. Collectively, this study provides multilayer mechanistic insights into LUAD radioresponse heterogeneity and yields actionable molecular candidates for developing improved radiosensitization strategies to advance precise radiotherapy for LUAD.

papers.abstract_en: Transcriptomic measurement technologies provide powerful approaches to understand biology but are limited to providing either a high-resolution snapshot at a moment in time or a low-resolution history of transcription constrained to a few genes over a narrow time range. Here, we introduce the 'recordanelle', a single-component synthetic organelle capable of recording the transcriptome in human cells. Recordanelles are composed of a mitochondrial membrane anchor, a condensate assembler and a poly(A)-binding protein. We demonstrate that the recordanelle can be engineered to recruit engineered RNAs or a sampling of up to 90% of all endogenous mRNAs and protect them over several days. We further show that transient and dynamic transcriptional responses resulting from inducible promoters or interferon signaling are preserved throughout time within the recordanelle at the single-cell level. This work provides a nondisruptive and unbiased transcriptome-wide single-cell RNA recording technology to enable a deeper understanding of biology.

papers.abstract_en: Here we present DynaVelo, a generative neural ordinary differential equation model that learns the joint dynamics of gene expression and transcription factor (TF) motif activity from single-cell multiome data. DynaVelo learns a functional form of the vector field, such that the model can be perturbed in silico and not only used to draw trajectories. We show that DynaVelo recovers the bifurcating in vivo dynamics of wild-type murine germinal center (GC) B cells and reveals how these dynamics change under heterozygous loss of epigenetic regulators Arid1a and Ctcf. In silico perturbation yields dynamic and cell-state-specific gene regulatory networks (GRNs) that recover known TF-to-gene edges in the wild-type GC GRN and predicts those that are disrupted in mutants. Perturbing Arid1aHet GCs in silico identified Ctcf, Stat3 and Bcl6 as rescue targets for Arid1a loss. In vivo experiments in double-heterozygous mice confirmed rescue of the Arid1aHet dark-zone phenotype in all three cases, and multiome profiling of Arid1aHet;CtcfHet GCs validated the predicted shift toward wild-type dynamics.

papers.abstract_en: Mast cells (MCs) display phenotypic heterogeneity across tissues and disease contexts, yet their relevance in melanoma remains unclear. Here, we investigated MC phenotypic programs associated with melanoma progression using high-dimensional phenotyping of MCs co-cultured with melanoma spheroids, trajectory inference, and transcriptomic analyzes. Human melanoma tissues showed differences in MC phenotypic composition despite comparable abundance between outcome groups, with metastatic melanomas enriched for Tryptase⁺ Chymase- MCs. Melanoma exposure induced MC phenotypic remodeling, characterized by loss of lineage- and effector-associated features and increased PD-1 expression, with more pronounced changes following metastatic melanoma co-culture. Trajectory analysis was consistent with a continuum toward a PD-1⁺ Chymase- phenotype, which was detected in melanoma tissues and enriched within intratumoral regions of metastatic melanomas. Experimentally defined protein changes were used to derive two MC-associated transcriptomic signatures with opposing clinical associations, reflecting lineage- and effector-enriched versus melanoma-remodeled programs. The MC-LE signature was associated with favorable survival and interferon-responsive pathways, whereas the MC-MR signature was associated with poorer survival and tumor-associated pathways. These transcriptomic associations extended beyond melanoma across multiple TCGA cancer cohorts, and independent analysis of MCs from healthy skin, basal cell carcinoma, and melanoma showed corresponding differences in MC-LE-related features. Together, these findings support distinct mast cell phenotypic programs associated with melanoma progression and identify a PD-1⁺ Chymase- MC phenotype enriched in metastatic disease and linked to transcriptomic features of poor survival.

papers.abstract_en: Although genome-wide association studies (GWAS) now routinely reveal genetic associations and biological insights in millions of individuals, underrepresentation of global populations, such as those from Polynesia, continue to persist. These exclusions, often driven by logistical challenges and lack of data, prevent systematic identification of population-enriched associations, such as the association of the missense variant at the CREBRF locus to BMI and type 2 diabetes discovered commonly occurring in Polynesian populations due to its rarity in global populations. Armed with the recently updated TOPMed imputation panel that could benefit studies in diverse populations that previously had poorer imputation performance, we performed the first GWAS of Native Hawaiians and Samoans, the largest to date of Polynesian-ancestry populations (combined N up to 8,461) to identify population-enriched associations for 13 adiposity and cardiometabolic traits available across both cohorts: BMI, fasting glucose, fasting insulin, HDL, height, hip circumference, HOMA-IR, LDL, T2D, total cholesterol, triglycerides, waist circumference, and waist-hip ratio. We found 25 trait-loci associations that met genome-wide significance: 20 previously reported or known associations and 5 putatively new associations via meta-analysis. In particular, with improved statistical power, we were able to confirm the previously suggestive association between the missense CREBRF variant with fasting glucose levels. The remaining 4 potentially novel loci-trait associations for BMI, LDL, and waist-hip ratio, however, were not replicated in All-of-Us. The lack of Polynesian-enriched findings outside of the CREBRF locus informs the bounds of the effect sizes or frequencies of any enriched variants and suggests that further expansion of cohort sizes from this region of the world and improved imputation references specific to these populations are needed to identify more population-enriched associations.

papers.abstract_en: Condition-responsive growth is a common feature of multicellular development, during which organisms integrate genetic and environmental signals to adjust their phenotype. However, the molecular properties shaping condition-responsive diversification remain poorly understood. The beetle genus Onthophagus offers promising opportunities to investigate this question, given its diversity of sex- and nutrition-responsive phenotypes, including horns - novel, secondary sexual weapons used in reproductive competition. We compared the gene regulatory properties of horns in two closely related species exhibiting highly specialized sex- and nutrition-biased phenotypes. We found a dynamic cis-regulatory landscape in developing horn tissue, shaped by mutational accumulation across species, condition-specific changes in chromatin accessibility within species, and the acquisition of lineage-specific regulatory elements. Many of these putative regulatory regions include binding site motifs of critical developmental regulatory genes, including members of the bone morphogenetic protein signaling pathway. We provide functional evidence that two proteins in this pathway have been co-opted for horn development, influencing the shape and size of this trait across species, sexes, and nutritional states. These findings provide evidence that evolutionarily labile cis-regulatory interactions may evolve alongside diversification of condition-specific traits, potentially modifying the activity of conserved developmental pathways over short evolutionary timescales.

papers.abstract_en: OBJECTIVE: To identify distinct cancer pain subgroups using integrated circadian, physiological and psychosocial data and assess subgroup-specific analgesic responses. METHODS: This explanatory sequential mixed-methods study included 191 adult inpatients with cancer pain from a tertiary care hospital. Quantitative measures included 24-h blood pressure, salivary melatonin, pain beliefs, coping styles, social support, and clinical variables. Mixed-type cluster analysis (K-prototypes) identified subgroups. Analgesic efficacy was evaluated using multiple linear regression, with changes in mean pain intensity and pain variability as the outcomes. The qualitative phase involved semi-structured interviews analyzed thematically. RESULTS: Four distinct patient subgroups (Cluster 0-3) were identified. Cluster 0 (elderly reverse-dipper, n = 44) showed moderate pain, poor sleep quality, emotional lability, and social withdrawal. Analgesics exerted no significant effect on mean pain intensity (coefficient = 0.063, 95% confidence interval [CI]: -0.585 to 0.711, p = 0.856) or pain variability (coefficient = -1.466, 95% CI: -4.178 to 1.246, p = 0.335). Cluster 1 (non-dipper severe pain, n = 54) exhibited disrupted circadian rhythm, negative pain cognition, and avoidant coping. Analgesics significantly reduced pain variability (coefficient = -2.333, 95% CI: -4.001 to -0.665, p = 0.008) but not mean pain intensity (coefficient = 0.072, 95% CI: -0.300 to 0.444, p = 0.712). Cluster 2 (dipper mild pain, n = 74) maintained normal circadian rhythm, positive mental status, and active social interaction. Analgesics significantly decreased pain variability (coefficient = -3.427, 95% CI: -5.391 to -1.463, p = 0.002) but not mean pain intensity (coefficient = -0.248, 95% CI: -0.682 to 0.186, p = 0.274). Cluster 3 (high-melatonin, n = 19) achieved significant reductions in mean pain intensity (coefficient = -1.259, 95% CI: -2.031 to -0.487, p = 0.001) and pain variability (coefficient = -5.602, 95% CI: -8.664 to -2.540, p = 0.001), with passive coping and emotional suppression. CONCLUSIONS: Patients with cancer pain exhibit marked heterogeneity in circadian rhythm, endocrine function, and psychosocial profiles. Interactions among these factors may contribute to distinct pain mechanisms and variable analgesic responses. Comprehensive multidimensional assessment may facilitate more accurate patient subtyping and support individualized pain management. REGISTRATION: This study was registered with the Chinese Clinical Trial Registry (ChiCTR) under registration number ChiCTR2500096806.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Locoregional recurrence (LRR) in oropharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma (OPSCC) patients treated with radiotherapy (RT) most often occurs within the high-dose target volume. Anatomical changes during RT may potentially lead to unintended target underdosage, which could contribute to the risk of treatment failure. This study aimed to quantify differences between planned and accumulated dose in the regions of later LRR. METHODS: Patients treated with curatively intended RT for OPSCC between 2009 and 2017 at Rigshospitalet with biopsy-proven LRR were identified. Recurrence volumes were delineated on follow up imaging and mapped to the planning CT. The point of origin (PO) of each recurrence was determined using the nidus method. Dose accumulation was performed using synthetic CTs based on daily cone beam CT, followed by recalculation and summation of daily dose distributions. Planned and accumulated doses at the PO were compared. Additional analyses evaluated effect of deformable registration methods. RESULTS: Forty patients with 54 recurrence volumes were included. The accumulated dose was higher than the planned dose in 57% of recurrences. The mean difference between accumulated and planned dose at the PO was - 0.04 Gy (SD: 0.81; 95% CI: -0.26 to 0.18 Gy; p = 0.72). Neither PO localization nor the dose accumulation process was sensitive to the use of an alternative deformation software CONCLUSIONS: Within the evaluated setting, no evidence was found that regions of later LRR were systematically underdosed. Dose differences were small and within clinically acceptable limits. This suggests that anatomical changes during RT were unlikely to cause clinically relevant compromised target dose coverage.

papers.results: 吡非尼酮与尼达尼布较安慰剂一致减少FVC下降；吸入曲前列尼尔在TETON-1/2合并证据中显示有利的FVC信号，多为背景抗纤维化治疗基础上的添加治疗。尼达尼布全因治疗终止OR 1.39（95% CI 1.02-1.88），吸入曲前列尼尔OR 1.39（95% CI 1.08-1.78）。吡非尼酮是唯一与较低全因死亡 odds 相关的治疗（OR 0.50；95% CI 0.31-0.83），基于已发表的ASCEND/CAPACITY合并死亡数据及日本3期试验。
papers.authors_conclusion: FVC下降仍是核心但可能不足以区分IPF各抗纤维化导向治疗；综合FVC效应、背景治疗、治疗持续性与死亡率，可为解读不断扩展的3期证据提供一个谨慎、依赖具体情境的框架。
papers.ai_note: FVC终点仅作“描述性汇总”，未给出合并效应量、置信区间或等效性检验，所谓“一致减缓”“有利信号”缺乏可量化支撑；“无等效性证据”被表述为治疗间差异的依据，逻辑上属不确定性。吡非尼酮死亡OR 0.50并非本研究统一提取的试验级合并结果，而是引用已发表ASCEND/CAPACITY合并数据加日本3期试验，来源异质、缺乏预设分析方案，存在选择性纳入与事后汇总风险。标题与结论以“Beyond FVC”为卖点，实质将次要终点（治疗终止、死亡）置于与主要终点同等甚至更高的解释权重，且无头对头或校正后的间接比较，不能支持治疗间排序。吸入曲前列尼尔“有利FVC信号”未报告数值，无法核验。

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Phase 3 evidence for antifibrotic-directed therapies in idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF) has expanded, but direct head-to-head trials are lacking. Forced vital capacity (FVC) decline remains the principal trial outcome, although it may not fully capture clinically relevant differences among therapies. METHODS: We systematically reviewed phase 3 randomized placebo-controlled trials of antifibrotic-directed therapies in IPF. FVC effects versus placebo were descriptively summarized using standardized 48-52-week estimates. All-cause treatment discontinuation and all-cause mortality were analyzed using placebo-controlled odds ratios. Sensitivity analyses assessed follow-up duration, background antifibrotic therapy, and trial-level consistency. RESULTS: Ten trials including 5,386 randomized participants were included. Pirfenidone and nintedanib showed consistent reductions in FVC decline versus placebo. Inhaled treprostinil showed a favorable FVC signal in the combined TETON-1/2 evidence, largely as add-on therapy with background antifibrotic treatment. Without background antifibrotic therapy, several therapies showed directionally favorable but imprecise FVC effects, without evidence of equivalence. Nintedanib and inhaled treprostinil were associated with higher odds of all-cause treatment discontinuation versus placebo: OR 1.39 (95% CI, 1.02-1.88) and OR 1.39 (95% CI, 1.08-1.78), respectively. Pirfenidone was the only therapy associated with lower odds of all-cause mortality (OR, 0.50; 95% CI, 0.31-0.83), based on published pooled ASCEND/CAPACITY mortality data and the Japanese phase 3 trial. CONCLUSIONS: FVC decline remains essential but may not fully distinguish antifibrotic-directed therapies in IPF. Integrating FVC effects, background therapy, treatment continuation, and mortality provides a cautious, context-dependent framework for interpreting expanding phase 3 evidence.

papers.abstract_en: The efficacy of immune checkpoint blockers in solid tumors remains limited by the physical and biological barriers posed by the tumor microenvironment, which restrict antibody transport and suppress anti-tumor immune responses. Focused ultrasound has emerged as a promising strategy to transiently enhance tumor perfusion, thereby improving the intratumoral delivery of immunotherapeutic agents. Despite encouraging experimental findings, a quantitative understanding of the coupled transport and immune mechanisms underlying focused ultrasound-enhanced immunotherapy remains incomplete. Here, we developed a multiphysics computational model to investigate how focused ultrasound modulates the tumor microenvironment, enhances the delivery of immune checkpoint blockers and influences innate and adaptive immune responses in solid tumors. Model predictions were validated against published in vivo experimental data, demonstrating good agreement with tumor growth and immune response measurements. Parametric analysis identified both tumor microenvironment and therapy-related parameters as key determinants of treatment efficacy. Stromal normalization and increased vessel wall pore radius enhanced antibody delivery, immune cell accumulation and tumor control, while focused ultrasound further amplified these effects. Moreover, increasing the anti-PD-1/PD-1 binding affinity and antibody administration dose enhanced immune checkpoint inhibition and tumor suppression, with focused ultrasound broadening the range of antibody characteristics associated with favorable therapeutic outcomes. Overall, the proposed computational framework provides a predictive platform for investigating and optimizing focused ultrasound-assisted immune checkpoint blockade, offering mechanistic insight into how focused ultrasound-induced modulation of the tumor microenvironment enhances antibody transport, promotes anti-tumor immune responses and improves therapeutic response.

papers.abstract_en: Chemoresistance remains a major obstacle to effective treatment of non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), yet the epigenetic mechanisms underlying platinum resistance remain incompletely understood. Here, we show that Jumonji C domain-containing protein 5 (JMJD5) promotes platinum resistance in NSCLC cells and xenograft tumors while inducing a slow-proliferative, mesenchymal-like phenotype characterized by enhanced migration, invasion, spheroid formation, and epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT). Mechanistically, JMJD5 interacted with RCC1 domain-containing protein 1 (RCCD1), and cisplatin treatment promoted their nuclear accumulation concomitant with reduced H3K36me2 levels. RCCD1 depletion attenuated JMJD5-associated H3K36me2 demethylation and reversed EMT-associated phenotypes and cisplatin resistance, supporting RCCD1 as a functional cofactor of JMJD5-mediated chromatin remodeling. Fibronectin 1 (FN1) was further identified as a downstream effector of this pathway. Genetic or pharmacological inhibition of FN1 suppressed JMJD5-induced migration and invasion and restored cisplatin sensitivity. Notably, JMJD5-dependent FN1 protein accumulation required ongoing protein synthesis without a corresponding increase in FN1 mRNA, suggesting post-transcriptional regulation. Consistently, elevated FN1 expression was associated with unfavorable overall survival in patients with lung cancer. Collectively, these findings reveal a JMJD5-RCCD1-H3K36me2-FN1 regulatory axis linking chemotherapy-induced epigenetic remodeling to EMT-associated platinum resistance and suggest that disruption of this pathway may represent a potential strategy for overcoming chemoresistance in NSCLC.

papers.title_en: Beyond immune surveillance: IFN-γ and PD-L1 as shapers of tumor plasticity in Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer (NSCLC).
papers.authors: Angelicola S, Frascino M, Chillico IC, Michel PLS, Pistone D, Semprini MS, Pittino OM, Ardizzoni A et al.
papers.affiliation_highlight: IRCCS Azienda Ospedaliero-Universitaria di Bologna, Bologna, Italy.

papers.abstract_en: Immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) targeting the PD-1/PD-L1 axis have transformed the treatment of Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer (NSCLC), yet durable responses remain limited to a minority of patients. Tumor plasticity is increasingly recognized as a determinant of immunotherapy resistance, although the tumor-intrinsic contribution of immunomodulatory mediators such as IFN-γ and PD-L1 remains poorly understood. In this review, we examine emerging evidence that IFN-γ and PD-L1, beyond their established roles in tumor-immune interactions, may contribute to the regulation of NSCLC plasticity. IFN-γ can activate non-canonical programs involving dose-dependent ICAM1/PI3K/AKT/Notch1 signaling, BCAT1- and FGF2/β-catenin-mediated metabolic reprogramming, and a putative autocrine TBX21/IL-4 signaling circuit that may sustain stem-like properties. PD-L1, in turn, is functionally integrated into plasticity-associated pathways involving the TGF-β signaling axis, β-catenin stabilization, epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition-associated microRNA networks, YAP/TAZ, CD44 and ATM signaling, as well as TRAF6/BECN1/NF-κB-dependent regulation of autophagy. Collectively, these findings support a role for IFN-γ and PD-L1 as context-dependent modulators of NSCLC plasticity, with potential implications for immunotherapy resistance, and provide a rationale for further exploring combinatorial treatment strategies and patient stratification approaches.

papers.abstract_en: Golgin-45 (G45) is a coiled-coil protein that transits reversibly between the Golgi and nucleus. In the Golgi, G45 serves as a tether for effectors of a pro-tumorigenic secretory program, but its nuclear role remains unclear. Here, we report that, upon entering the nucleus, G45 functions as a basic leucine zipper transcription factor. From genomic mapping, RNA-sequencing, and functional validation studies, we identify G45-binding sites and show that nuclear G45 can function as a transcriptional activator or repressor, a versatility enabled by phase separation into nuclear bodies enriched in transcriptional co-regulators. In lung cancer models, Golgi-docking reinforces, whereas nuclear translocation opposes, pro-tumorigenic activity of G45. Nuclear G45 incorporates into dimeric transcription factors that silence pro-tumorigenic secreted cargos. Epigenetic events in lung cancer degrade nuclear G45 and sequester G45 in the Golgi, which unleashes malignant secretion. Thus, inter-organelle transitions govern a G45-dependent secretory axis that drives lung cancer progression.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE: Spatially fractionated radiation therapy (SFRT) intentionally delivers nonuniform dose distributions characterized by alternating high-dose peaks and low-dose valleys, with therapeutic potential for complex, inoperable bulky tumors. Although clinical adoption is expanding, clinical implementation and practices remain heterogeneous across institutions. This consensus aims to identify system-level barriers to harmonized clinical implementation of SFRT and formulate consensus-based recommendations to enable reproducible multi-institutional integration. METHODS: The 2025 ESTRO Physics Workshop convened multidisciplinary international experts to evaluate current implementation practices and develop harmonization priorities through structured consensus discussions. Twenty-eight delegates participated, representing centers across Europe, the United States, China, and Australia. Core domains included dose recording and reporting specifications, commissioning and quality assurance (QA), motion management, registry infrastructure, and governance. RESULTS: Five principal domains were identified as barriers to harmonized implementation: (1) inconsistent dose recording and reporting conventions; (2) variability in commissioning and QA practices for heterogeneous small-field dose distributions; (3) uncertainty in motion management and geometric robustness evaluation in the presence of anatomical changes; (4) fragmented data infrastructure limiting multi-institutional outcome analysis; and (5) limited coordinated governance and standardization infrastructure. Consensus recommendations and a phased roadmap with measurable milestones were formulated to address these domains. CONCLUSION: Harmonization of clinical implementation is essential to ensure reproducibility, support prospective multi-institutional trials, and safeguard consistent patient care across institutions. Coordinated international collaboration will be critical to establish standardized definitions, QA benchmarks, registry infrastructure, and governance frameworks for safe and effective clinical integration.

papers.abstract_en: To investigate the local control and safety of adding high-dose-rate intraluminal brachytherapy (HDR-ILBT) with novel balloon applicator (BRAXX) after concurrent chemoradiation (CCRT) for non-surgery patients with esophageal cancer. The study enrolled 178 patients with esophageal cancer. A total of 13 patients were prospectively recruited to receive HDR-ILBT after CCRT and compared with two standard-of-care cohorts treated between 2022 and 2024. Brachytherapy was delivered via the BRAXX balloon applicator (Taiwan Food and Drug Administration approval No. 006603) using an Iridium-192 Nucletron remote afterloading system (Elekta, Stockholm, Sweden). The primary endpoint was freedom from local tumor recurrence (FFLTR). Secondary endpoints included overall survival (OS), disease progression-free survival (DPFS), and toxicities. Sankey diagrams and swimmer plot were utilized to visualize the longitudinal tumor response dynamics and individual survival trajectories. The median follow-up was 25.2 months. The 1-year and 2-year FFLTR rates were 93.3% and 81.2% (nCCRT + surgery), 84.6% and 67.7% (CCRT + ILBT), and 62.5% and 52.9% (dCCRT alone), respectively (P < 0.001). Consistent survival improvements were observed in both OS and DPFS in CCRT + ILBT cohort. Sankey diagrams demonstrated a favorable dynamic evolution in treatment response within the CCRT + ILBT cohort, achieving a clinical complete response (cCR) rate of 61.5% and overall response rate (ORR) of 69.2% at the end of per-protocol 1-year follow-up. Swimmer plot illustrated that response conversion and consolidation translated into long-term survival. The addition of HDR-ILBT did not exacerbate treatment-related esophageal strictures or fistula formations necessitating intervention. The addition of HDR-ILBT utilizing BRAXX applicator following CCRT is a feasible and promising strategy to enhance local control and prolong survival for non-surgical patients with esophageal cancer. By leveraging its distinct dosimetric advantages and streamlined workflow, ILBT holds the potential to consolidate disease-free status and eradicate residual disease. Further validation through large-scale, prospective clinical trials is still warranted to confirm its clinical benefit and long-term safety. If further validated, this strategy could offer a meaningful addition to the current treatment paradigm.

papers.abstract_en: Although single-port video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery (VATS) lobectomy is increasingly adopted for non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), evidence comparing its long-term oncological efficacy with that of the two-port approach remains scarce. This propensity score-matched study evaluated perioperative outcomes, postoperative recovery, and 3-year survival following single-port versus two-port thoracoscopic lobectomy in patients with NSCLC. We retrospectively analyzed 167 consecutive patients (single-port, n = 82; two-port, n = 85); propensity score matching (1:1, caliper = 0.2) yielded 72 matched pairs. Perioperative outcomes, postoperative pain (VAS), inflammatory markers (CRP, PCT, IL-1β), pulmonary function, 30-day complications, 3-year overall survival (OS), disease-free survival (DFS), and multivariable Cox regression were compared. Following matching, the single-port group demonstrated significantly longer operative time (187.3 ± 56.4 vs. 142.2 ± 49.4 minutes; P<0.001) but reduced blood loss (96.5 ± 42.0 vs. 121.7 ± 48.1 mL; P<0.001) 24-hour chest drainage volume (632.3 ± 447.3 vs. 945.5 ± 501.3 mL; P<0.001), and incision length (3.57 ± 1.37 vs. 4.94 ± 1.52 cm; P<0.001). Lymph node yield did not differ significantly (17.3 ± 4.1 vs. 16.1 ± 3.6; P = 0.058). Postoperative VAS scores were significantly lower in the single-port group on days 3, 5, and 7 (all P<0.001), with attenuated inflammatory responses (lower CRP, PCT, and IL-1β; all P<0.001) and better pulmonary function recovery (higher PaO2, SpO2, FVC, and FEV1; all P<0.05). Thirty-day complication rates did not differ significantly (6.9% vs. 9.7%; P = 0.763). Over a median follow-up of 38 months, 3-year OS (86.5% vs. 84.4%; P = 0.572) and 3-year DFS (79.2% vs. 77.1%; P = 0.684) were comparable. Multivariable analysis identified pathological stage II (HR, 2.45; 95% CI, 1.35-4.43; P = 0.003) and lymphovascular invasion (HR, 2.10; 95% CI, 1.18-3.72; P = 0.012) as independent predictors of poorer DFS, whereas surgical approach was not associated with DFS or OS. In conclusion, single-port thoracoscopic lobectomy was associated with reduced surgical trauma, decreased postoperative pain and inflammation, and improved pulmonary function recovery, without compromising lymph node dissection, short-term safety, or 3-year oncological outcomes. These findings support the continued use and wider adoption of single-port VATS in appropriately selected patients with NSCLC, while acknowledging that Stage I disease predominance limits generalizability to more advanced stages.

papers.reason: 启发式模式收录（未接入语言模型精评）：按期刊层级与研究类型自动入选。
papers.abstract_en: Learning curves for robotic-assisted reverse shoulder arthroplasty (RSA) are typically described over a surgeon's first 20 to 30 cases. Whether operative efficiency continues to improve beyond that point, and whether mean operative time is the appropriate measure of it, is unknown. We evaluated 100 consecutive primary robotic-assisted RSA procedures performed by a single fellowship-trained surgeon using the Mako system (Stryker, Kalamazoo, MI) at an academic ambulatory surgery center. The first 30 cases comprise our previously reported cohort. Operative time, defined as incision to the start of closure, was modeled by segmented linear regression with a breakpoint at case 30. Variability was assessed by standard deviation and Levene's test, and the distribution of improvement by percentile comparison and by quantile regression at the 10th, 50th and 90th percentiles. Baseline characteristics were compared across case groups, and the influence of patient factors on operative time was assessed by multivariable regression. Mean operative time fell from 88.6 min (cases 1 to 30) to 75.4 min (cases 31 to 70) to 64.3 min (cases 71 to 100). Segmented regression demonstrated a steep initial decline of 1.85 min per case (P = 0.0001) followed by a shallower but significant decline of 0.26 min per case (P = 0.001), with a significant difference in slope between phases (P < 0.0001). Variability fell proportionally further than the mean, with standard deviation decreasing by 56.6% against a 27.5% decrease in mean operative time (P = 0.008). Improvement was greatest at the upper end of the distribution: the 90th percentile declined by 0.52 min per case compared with 0.30 min per case at the 10th, and percentile improvement increased from 17% at the 5th percentile to 35% at the 95th. The total range of operative time contracted from 115 to 42 min, and the proportion of cases exceeding 90 min fell from 40% to none. Baseline characteristics did not differ across case groups, and the case-number effect persisted after adjustment for age, sex, body mass index and glenoid deformity. Operative efficiency in robotic-assisted RSA continues to improve well beyond the initial 30-case learning period, but the way that improvement is expressed shifts from shortening the typical case to eliminating the prolonged outliers. Because operating room scheduling is driven by the tail of the distribution rather than its mean, case-to-case predictability of operative time may be a more informative marker of a mature robotic workflow than mean operative time alone.

papers.reason: 为胸外科机器人/胸腔镜术中AI（解剖识别、AR与ICG导航、事件预警）提供证据分层框架与'中间终点未转化为患者获益、无安全可问责的患者层面自主决策'的基线判断，可用于课题立项时界定可委托决策的边界与所需结局指标，并提示单中心影像组学/AI研究需补充跨机构泛化与成本评估。
papers.abstract_en: Robotic surgical platforms have improved instrument dexterity, tremor filtration, and ergonomic control, yet intraoperative decisions still depend on a surgeon interpreting a moving, partially observed field under time pressure. Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly used to close parts of this loop by recognizing anatomy, tracking instruments, anticipating events, and-experimentally-planning or executing selected actions. This review maps the computational technologies that support intraoperative decision-making in robotic surgery and appraises the clinical evidence for them.Because the direct robotic evidence base is still uneven, we explicitly distinguish three kinds of material: (i) studies conducted on robotic systems during surgery; (ii) non-robotic surgical evidence from laparoscopic and thoracoscopic procedures that use the same vision and workflow methods; and (iii) preclinical, preoperative, and perioperative work that is conceptually relevant but not intraoperative. Robotic and non-robotic settings are labeled throughout the tables and text. We further separate non-AI image guidance-indocyanine green (ICG) fluorescence and registered overlays-from AI-based inference, and we include image-guided endovascular robotics as a complementary setting in which fluoroscopic perception, vascular-topology reasoning, and closed-loop instrument control are particularly advanced.We organize the field into four computational layers: perception, anatomical and procedural reasoning, action planning, and control and execution. Augmented-reality and fluorescence navigation can improve orientation and selected intermediate outcomes, and several randomized trials now exist. Computer-vision systems can recognize anatomy, phases, instruments, and adverse events, and in endovascular work they can track guidewires and reason over vascular topology. Foundation models broaden language and multimodal capabilities but remain, in surgery, largely preclinical. Autonomous subtasks have shown promise in phantoms, animals, and a small number of carefully bounded tissue tasks; no system has demonstrated safe, accountable patient-level autonomous decision-making.Navigation and AI-assisted systems have improved orientation, reduced ischemia, and accelerated recognition of critical events in some studies. Whether these intermediate gains improve patient outcomes, generalize across institutions, or justify their cost remains unknown. The question is not whether AI can interpret surgical scenes, but which decisions can be delegated, with what evidence, uncertainty limits, oversight, and outcome measures.

papers.abstract_en: PURPOSE: To evaluate whether time from birth to arrival at a tertiary extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO)-capable center is independently associated with ECMO utilization among outborn neonates with congenital diaphragmatic hernia (CDH). We hypothesized that longer transfer intervals would be associated with greater ECMO utilization after adjustment for disease severity and anatomic characteristics. METHODS: We performed a retrospective cohort study of outborn neonates with CDH transferred to a tertiary neonatal intensive care unit with ECMO capability. Transfer interval was analyzed using multivariable logistic regression adjusting for CDHSG postnatal score and anatomic characteristics. RESULTS: Among 46 neonates, 21 (45.7%) required ECMO and 25 (54.3%) did not. Infants requiring ECMO had greater CDHSG postnatal scores and more frequent intrathoracic liver herniation. After adjustment, transfer time was not independently associated with ECMO utilization (aOR 0.79, 95% CI 0.50-1.23). Intrathoracic liver herniation remained independently associated (aOR 8.65, 95% CI 1.52-49.38), whereas CDHSG score did not reach statistical significance. CONCLUSION: Within the transfer intervals observed, transfer time was not independently associated with ECMO utilization. These findings suggest that transport duration alone may be less informative than underlying disease characteristics in this cohort.

papers.abstract_en: PURPOSE: International protocols for paediatric renal tumours are largely based on Western data with Wilms tumour (WT) accounting for more than 90% of cases. We aimed to evaluate the relative frequency of WT and Non-Wilms Renal Tumours (NWRTs) in a diverse Asian cohort in Malaysia. METHODS: A retrospective review was conducted of all primary paediatric renal tumours treated at a national tertiary referral centre from 2015 to 2024. Diagnosis was confirmed via post-operative histopathology. RESULTS: Of 95 children (median age 29 months), all were Asian descent (73.7% Malay, 9.5% Chinese, 6.3% Indian). WT accounted for only 68.4% of cases, while NWRTs accounted for 31.6%. Among NWRTs, 63.3% were malignant, primarily clear cell sarcoma of the kidney (CCSK, n = 7) and renal cell carcinoma (RCC, n = 4). In the classic WT age range (6-84 months), WT prevalence was only 75.6%, with CCSK representing 9.0%. Congenital mesoblastic nephroma (CMN) predominated in infants < 6 months (71.4%), while RCC was exclusively seen in children > 84 months (40.0%). CONCLUSION: The substantial proportion of malignant NWRTs observed in this institutional cohort highlights potential risks of neoadjuvant chemotherapy without histological confirmation. Histopathological diagnosis via percutaneous core-needle biopsy or primary surgery may be highly considered in similar clinical settings.
