papers.abstract_en: Purpose To assess pulmonary gas exchange in participants with cystic fibrosis (CF) relative to control participants, evaluate the effect of CF transmembrane conductance regulator (CFTR) modulator therapy, and assess subclinical lung disease using xenon 129 (129Xe) MRI. Materials and Methods Participants with CF and control participants were prospectively enrolled between October 2019 and February 2024 and underwent 129Xe MRI and spirometry. Images from gaseous xenon, xenon dissolved in pulmonary capillary red blood cells (RBCs), and dissolved in the gas-exchange membrane (interstitial tissue and capillary plasma) were binned into three compartments to generate maps of ventilation, RBC transfer, and membrane uptake. Spirometric and imaging differences between participants with CF and control participants were assessed using analysis of variance with Tukey post hoc corrections, and associations were analyzed using Kendall rank correlation. Results Sixty-one participants with CF (median age, 14.2 years; IQR, 10.0-19.7 years; 33 female) and 47 controls (median age, 24.9 years; IQR, 20.9-29.2 years; 25 males) were included. For participants with CF, spirometry (percent predicted) was normal: forced expiratory volume after 1 second (median, 98.2%; IQR, 87.2%-109%), forced vital capacity (median, 104%; IQR, 96.8%-112%), and forced expiratory flow between 25% and 75% forced vital capacity (median, 88.1%; IQR, 69.9%-108%). Participants with CF had a higher ventilation defect percentage (2.50% vs 1.40%; P < .001), RBC transfer (0.00354 vs 0.00325; P = .0104), and membrane uptake (0.0096 vs 0.0076; P < .001) than controls. Membrane uptake correlated with elevated RBC transfer (τ = 0.62; P < .001) for participants with CF on and off CFTR modulator therapy. Conclusion Participants with CF had higher RBC transfer and membrane uptake than control participants. Membrane uptake was elevated in participants with CF exhibiting normal spirometry and receiving highly effective CFTR modulator therapy. Keywords: Adults and Pediatrics, Lung, MR-Hyperpolarization, MR-Functional Lung Imaging Supplemental material is available for this article. © RSNA, 2026.

papers.abstract_en: OBJECTIVES: To compare low-attenuation analysis (LAA) with visual scoring and explore their application in the detection of emphysema in low-dose CT (LDCT) scans. METHODS: A random cohort of 352 CT examinations from health-check participants was selected from a lung cancer screening(LCS) dataset. Scans were evaluated for emphysema by four readers according to latest Fleischner criteria, and emphysema was quantified by LAA with thresholds from -900 HU to -980 HU. Fleiss' Kappa assessed inter-reader agreement on visual detection and severity classification. Cases with full agreement on emphysema presence were used to compare LAA quantification and visual detection. Spearman correlation test measured their correlation and Cohen's Kappa evaluated the agreement between LAA%-measured emphysema and visual detection. RESULTS: Agreement among four observers was found in 266 cases on emphysema presence based on visual evaluation (K = 0.738, 0.737-0.739). Concordance between emphysema presence using a LAA% cutoff of 6% and binary visual classification was 61.3% (163/266, Cohen's Kappa:0.173. Spearman analysis showed a correlation between LAA% and visual scores (P < 0.05). CONCLUSIONS: LAA emphysema quantification shows in comparison with visual scoring limited performance for discrimination of normal and emphysematous lung parenchyma in a Low dose CT Lung cancer screening dataset. ADVANCES IN KNOWLEDGE: Full agreement among four readers regarding visual emphysema classification was achieved in only three-quarters of cases. Limited concordance was found between LAA%-measured emphysema and visual detection.

papers.abstract_en: Although multi-hit TP53 mutations correlate with rapid disease progression, treatment resistance, recurrence, and poor survival, their occurrence within an individual TP53 gene molecule (cbTP53) remains unexplored. Consequently, the impact of cbTP53 on protein conformation, transcriptional architecture, and oncogenicity is unknown. We show that cbTP53 with combined mutations (Y220C+R248Q+R282Q) does not drastically alter local stability or structural conformation, but significantly affects TP53 binding to DNA promoters comparing it to a single Y220C mutation. Functionally, cbTP53 promotes divergent cellular phenotypes, characterized by enhanced cell proliferation, increased formation of multicellular tumor spheroids (MCTS) and spheroids, altered responses to chemotherapeutic drugs (e.g., cisplatin, carboplatin) and p53 inhibitors (e.g., MB710, PK11007), and increased resistance to carboplatin-induced DNA damage. Furthermore, cbTP53 is linked to distinct immune cell profiles (e.g., CD4+ and CD8+ T cells, nature killer cells, dendritic cells), more circulating tumor cells, a higher rate of tumor engraftment, and an increased number of lung tumor nodules. Mechanistically, introduction of R248Q/R282Q mutations changes 42.7% of Y220C-regulated gene expression, and cbTP53 (vs Y220C) owns a distinctive transcriptomic signature with 1,004 up- and 1,747 down-regulated genes. cbTP53 shows the enhanced binding affinity in the promoters of inflammatory cytokines, leading to their increased production. This study establishes causative and mechanistic links of cbTP53 to lung aggressive cancer metastasis and disease progression, providing a novel perspective on the genetics of TP53 mutations in cancer.

papers.abstract_en: INTRODUCTION: This study aimed to estimate the incidence, mortality, and overall survival (OS) of esophageal cancer (EC) and to evaluate the association of clinicopathological characteristics and treatment modality with OS. METHODS: A retrospective observational cohort study was conducted using data from the Population-Based Cancer Registry (PBCR) in rural central India. The dataset included 545 incident EC cases registered between 2010 and 2019, of which 476 were eligible for OS analysis. Incidence and mortality rates were estimated, OS was analyzed using the Kaplan-Meier method, and Cox proportional hazards regression was used to identify prognostic factors. Prespecified sensitivity analyses, including metastasis-adjusted and age-stratified Cox regression models, were performed to assess the robustness of the primary multivariable findings. RESULTS: The age-standardized incidence rate (ASIR) of overall EC cases was 3.99 per 100,000 population (95% CI: 3.50-4.47), while the age-standardized mortality rate (ASMR) was 3.29 per 100,000 population (95% CI: 2.94-3.64). The overall median survival was 178.33 days (95% CI: 115.49-234.48). The OS rates at 1, 3, 5, and 10 years were 31.3%, 19.7%, 17.4%, and 14.6%, respectively. OS differed significantly according to tumor site (χ² = 5.24, p = 0.043), treatment modality (χ² = 15.42, p = 0.031), and metastatic status (χ² = 162.64, p < 0.001) on Kaplan-Meier analysis. Median survival was 232 days (95% CI: 159.59-304.41) for localized disease, 199 days (95% CI: 166.38-231.61) for regional disease, 68 days (95% CI: 54.21-81.79) for distant disease, and 28 days (95% CI: 15.56-40.44) for advanced disease. On univariable Cox regression, patients with middle-third tumors had a lower hazard of death than those with upper-third tumors (HR: 0.74, 95% CI: 0.56-0.98; p = 0.036), and this remained significant after adjustment for metastatic status and in the age-stratified sensitivity model, while metastatic disease was associated with progressively higher mortality. Radiotherapy plus chemotherapy and surgery plus chemotherapy were independently associated with lower mortality after multivariable adjustment (HR: 0.48, 95% CI: 0.28-0.85, p = 0.011; HR: 0.45, 95% CI: 0.21-0.94, p = 0.035, respectively). Age, sex, and histological type were not significantly associated with OS. CONCLUSION: EC demonstrated a substantial mortality burden and poor OS in this population-based cohort. Metastatic status was the strongest associated prognostic factor, while tumor site and treatment modality were associated with survival on Kaplan-Meier analysis. Radiotherapy plus chemotherapy and surgery plus chemotherapy remained independently associated with lower mortality after multivariable adjustment. These findings highlight the importance of early diagnosis, accurate assessment of disease extent, and appropriate multimodal management of EC.

papers.abstract_en: INTRODUCTION: Pleural effusion remains diagnostically challenging when standard thoracentesis does not establish an aetiology. This pilot analysis described sequential biomarker measurements in patients proceeding to medical thoracoscopy and explored their associations and discrimination across final diagnostic classifications. METHODS: Prospectively collected data from a single-centre tertiary referral cohort were analysed. Pleural-fluid adenosine deaminase (ADA) and serum complement components 3 and 4 (C3 and C4) were obtained on day 1, whereas pleural-fluid cancer antigen 125 (CA125) and lactate dehydrogenase (LDH) were obtained at the day 7/thoracoscopy evaluation. Final classifications were based on a composite reference standard integrating thoracoscopy, histopathology, microbiology, cytology, imaging, and clinical follow-up. Analyses were exploratory. RESULTS: Amongst 75 patients, 6 (8.0%) were classified as tuberculous pleural effusion (TB-PE), 33 (44.0%) as malignant pleural effusion (MPE) and 36 (48.0%) as other non-tuberculous, non-malignant pleural effusions. ADA differed across groups (Kruskal-Wallis P = 0.002; Benjamini-Hochberg q = 0.010) and showed exploratory discrimination for TB-PE (area under the curve [AUC] 0.934; bootstrap 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.855-0.995). At the conventional ≥ 40 U/L threshold, sensitivity was 83.3%, specificity 93.4%, positive predictive value (PPV) 55.6%, negative predictive value (NPV) 98.3%, positive likelihood ratio (LR+) 12.7, and negative likelihood ratio (LR-) 0.18. CA125, LDH, C3 and C4 did not show significant omnibus group differences after reanalysis. In a post hoc sensitivity analysis excluding 26 patients retained as non-specific pleuritis (n = 49), ADA remained significantly different across groups (P = 0.004; q = 0.022). CONCLUSIONS: In this selected thoracoscopy cohort, day 1 pleural-fluid ADA showed the clearest exploratory signal, including after exclusion of non-specific pleuritis, but estimates were based on only six TB-PE cases and do not establish stand-alone utility or a role in avoiding thoracoscopy. The remaining biomarkers showed no robust aetiology-specific signal. TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov NCT06159179.

papers.abstract_en: Lung cancer remains a major cause of cancer-related mortality, including among patients diagnosed with potentially curable disease. Current decisions regarding perioperative treatment and follow-up rely on a limited number of established prognostic factors. Further knowledge is needed regarding the clinical, histopathological, and molecular factors associated with subsequent metastatic disease, particularly brain metastasis (BM), which is associated with poor prognosis. We investigated these factors in a large cohort of patients with surgically resected stage I-III lung cancer followed for more than five years. BM was associated with higher pathological tumour and lymph-node stage and younger age at surgery. Lung adenocarcinoma was associated with a higher risk of BM than lung squamous cell carcinoma. Several molecular alterations were associated with metastatic disease or BM, including KRAS mutations in lung adenocarcinoma and NFE2L2 mutations in lung squamous cell carcinoma. Additional associations involving specific EGFR and KRAS mutation subtypes and rarer alterations were observed, but were based on small numbers of cases and should be considered exploratory. Several of the associated genes are involved in the RAS/MAPK, PI3K/AKT/mTOR, or NRF2-related pathways. However, pathway activation and causality could not be established in this observational study. These findings support further investigation of clinical, histopathological, and molecular factors associated with metastatic progression after surgical resection. Validation in larger, independent, stage-stratified and contemporary cohorts with comprehensive treatment data is required before the identified molecular alterations can be considered for clinical risk stratification or surveillance.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Underweight is a well-established risk factor for cancer mortality, yet its impact relative to obesity remains unclear in individuals with type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM), where current guidelines focus primarily on obesity management with limited guidance on underweight-related risks. We evaluated the association between body mass index (BMI) and gastrointestinal (GI) cancer mortality across the full BMI spectrum in individuals with T2DM. METHODS: This nationwide population-based cohort study utilized the Korean National Health Insurance Service database. We included 2 507 976 adults with T2DM screened in 2015-2016 and followed through 2022, with a 1-year lag period applied to minimize reverse causality. BMI was categorized into eight groups: severe underweight (< 16.0 kg/m2), moderate underweight (16.0-16.9 kg/m2), mild underweight (17.0-18.4 kg/m2), normal weight (18.5-22.9 kg/m2), overweight (23.0-24.9 kg/m2), Class I obesity (25.0-29.9 kg/m2), Class II obesity (30.0-34.9 kg/m2) and Class III obesity (≥ 35.0 kg/m2). Multivariable-adjusted hazard ratios (aHRs) for GI cancer mortality were estimated using Cox proportional hazards models adjusting for clinical variables. RESULTS: During 5.75-year mean follow-up, 10 978 GI cancer deaths occurred (975 oesophageal, 4391 gastric, 5317 colorectal and 295 other GI cancers including small intestine and anal cancer). A reverse J-shaped association was observed with mortality nadir at BMI 25.0-29.9 kg/m2, which served as the reference group. Underweight was consistently associated with increased mortality across all severity categories: mild underweight aHR 2.54 (95% CI 2.26-2.85), moderate underweight aHR 2.51 (95% CI 1.96-3.20) and severe underweight aHR 2.96 (95% CI 2.14-4.09), with the highest risk observed in severe underweight. Notably, all underweight categories were associated with substantially higher mortality risk than Class III obesity (aHR 1.35, 95% CI 1.05-1.73). Cancer-specific analyses revealed that underweight was associated with the highest mortality risk for oesophageal cancer (aHR 13.23 [95% CI 6.77-25.85] for severe underweight), followed by gastric and colorectal cancers, whereas obesity significantly increased mortality only for colorectal cancer (aHR 1.52 [95% CI 1.10-2.08] for Class III obesity). Underweight was not significantly associated with GI cancer incidence after adjustment, and associations remained largely robust in 2-, 3-, and 4-year lag and competing risk analyses, except for colorectal cancer. CONCLUSIONS: In individuals with T2DM, underweight status is associated with substantially higher GI cancer mortality risk than obesity, with severe underweight showing nearly threefold higher risk compared to the reference group (BMI 25.0-29.9 kg/m2). These findings suggest that underweight, rather than obesity alone, warrants greater clinical attention as a determinant of GI cancer mortality in this population.

papers.abstract_en: The 2026 American Society of Clinical Oncology (ASCO) Annual Meeting presented substantial new data on antibody-drug conjugates (ADCs) in lung cancer, highlighting the ongoing expansion of ADC-based strategies from later-line treatment toward first-line combination regimens. This focused narrative review summarizes and discusses the efficacy and safety findings of ADCs targeting TROP2, HER2, Nectin-4, PD-L1, c-Met, B7-H3, DLL3, SEZ6, and other emerging targets in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) and small cell lung cancer (SCLC), with particular attention to emerging ADC plus immune checkpoint inhibitor combinations in the first-line setting. Taken together, these findings highlight an expanding ADC landscape in lung cancer. However, many of the emerging strategies remain supported primarily by preliminary conference-reported or early-phase data and therefore require confirmation in mature peer-reviewed studies and adequately powered randomized clinical trials.

papers.abstract_en: INTRODUCTION: Urinary toxicities are common following prostate radiotherapy and can impair quality of life. New biomarkers are needed that can predict the risk of urinary toxicity following MRI guided stereotactic body radiotherapy (MR-SBRT) to assist with selection of the most appropriate radiotherapy treatment approach. We aimed to identify urine miRNA biomarkers of radiation-induced urinary toxicities. METHODS: Ten patients undergoing MR-SBRT were enrolled on a prospective biorepository protocol and urine specimens were collected before, at the final fraction and 2-4 months following radiotherapy. RNA was isolated and microRNA sequencing was performed followed by qPCR for confirmation of microRNA expression changes. Differences in microRNA expression were assessed with regard to timepoint, cancer risk category and urinary toxicity. RESULTS: Both sequencing and qPCR showed that expressions of miR-26a-5p and miR-95-3p decrease during MR-SBRT and increase during early follow up. miR-204-3p and miR-192-5p changed differently in patients with and without urinary radiation toxicity. Expression of miR-375-3p was lower in patients with higher risk category (NCCN unfavorable intermediate to high risk or recurrent/metastatic) at all timepoints and decreased during and after MR-SBRT, especially in patients with a lower risk category (NCCN low to favorable intermediate risk) of prostate cancer. DISCUSSION: Urine microRNA analysis is feasible and may identify biomarkers linked to radiation-induced urinary toxicity and prostate cancer severity. The findings of this pilot study are limited by the sample size and should be prospectively validated.

papers.abstract_en: OBJECTIVE: To analyze the correlation between inflammation, nutrition and metabolic indicators and the risk of papillary thyroid carcinoma (PTC), and to construct and validate a nomogram for predicting PTC risk among patients with thyroid nodules undergoing surgery, to assist clinicians in making more individualized clinical decisions. STUDY DESIGN: Retrospective population-based cohort study. METHODS: A retrospective study was conducted on the clinical medical records of patients with thyroid masses who underwent surgical treatment at Hebei General Hospital from 2020 to 2024. Independent risk factors for the onset of PTC were screened through Logistic regression analysis. A risk prediction model for the onset of PTC based on inflammatory, nutritional and metabolic indicators was constructed using R4.3.3 software and externally validated. RESULTS: A total of 1727 patients who underwent thyroidectomy for thyroid nodules were enrolled, among whom 1167 patients (67.6%) were pathologically-confirmed papillary thyroid carcinoma (PTC), and 560 patients (32.4%) had benign thyroid nodules after surgery. Multivariate logistic regression analysis demonstrated combined Hashimoto's thyroiditis (HT) (OR = 1.887, 95%CI: 1.174-3.031, P = 0.009), combined metabolic syndrome (MetS) (OR = 2.157, 95%CI: 1.449-3.211, P < 0.001), and elevated uric acid (UA) (OR = 1.640, 95%CI: 1.112-2.417, P = 0.013) were independent risk factors for PTC onset. Age ≥ 55 years (OR = 0.318, 95%CI: 0.238-0.424, P < 0.001), other marital status (OR = 0.067, 95%CI: 0.012-0.392, P = 0.003), and increased prognostic nutritional index (PNI) (OR = 0.934, 95%CI: 0.902-0.966, P < 0.001) were independent protective factors against PTC onset. Based on the above independent risk factors, a nomogram for PTC was constructed. The AUC of the ROC curve in the modeling group was 0.702, and that in the external validation group was 0.721, indicating that the nomogram has good predictive performance. The calibration curve and decision analysis curve also indicate that the nomogram has good predictive performance and clinical application efficacy. CONCLUSION: Combined HT, combined MetS, and elevated UA are independent risk factors for PTC onset, whereas age ≥ 55 years, other marital status, and PNI level represent independent protective factors.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Frailty is associated with poor short-term surgical outcomes, but whether the Fried frailty phenotype is associated with long-term mortality after curative colorectal cancer (CRC) surgery, independently of age and tumor stage, is uncertain. We examined this association using restricted mean survival time (RMST), which does not require proportional hazards. METHODS: This retrospective multicenter cohort study included 304 patients aged ≥60 years who underwent curative CRC surgery at three centers in China in 2018-2019. The preoperative Fried phenotype was analyzed as robust (n=131), pre-frail (n=57), or frail (n=116); binary (robust versus non-robust) and ordinal codings were secondary. The primary outcome was 5-year all-cause mortality. Because proportional hazards were violated (Schoenfeld test P = 0.011), the RMST difference at 60 months was the primary effect measure, adjusted by pseudo-observation regression for age, sex, and TNM stage, the minimal adjustment set from a directed acyclic graph. Stage-specific and time-varying-effect analyses were also performed. RESULTS: Over a median follow-up of 60 months, 27 patients (8.9%) died. Five-year survival was 96.2%, 84.2%, and 88.8% in robust, pre-frail, and frail patients (log-rank P = 0.015). Unadjusted RMST differences versus robust patients were -2.38 months (95% CI -4.45 to -0.78) for pre-frail and -2.73 months (-4.58 to -1.09) for frail patients. After adjustment for age, sex, and TNM stage they were -1.48 months (-3.42 to 0.45; P = 0.13) and -0.81 months (-2.56 to 0.93; P = 0.36); for non-robust versus robust patients, -1.16 months (-2.50 to 0.19; P = 0.092). Estimates were in the same direction within every stage but imprecise. The hazard ratio for non-robust patients appeared higher in the first 36 months than later, but period-specific estimates were unstable and did not differ significantly (P = 0.15). CONCLUSIONS: The Fried frailty phenotype identified older patients with lower 5-year survival after curative CRC surgery. After adjustment for age and tumor stage the association was attenuated and imprecise, so an independent effect could not be established with 27 deaths. The apparent early concentration of excess mortality in non-robust patients is hypothesis-generating and requires confirmation in larger cohorts with treatment and cause-of-death data.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Mixed-grade glioma surgical cohorts exhibit highly variable low-grade glioma (LGG) proportions across studies. This meta-analysis quantifies pooled LGG proportions to provide cohort-level epidemiological benchmarks for researchers, with applications in clinical trial design, health economics, and institutional benchmarking. METHODS: A single-arm meta-analysis of 191 cohort studies (25,847 patients) with Grade II numerators and denominators from Embase, MEDLINE, PubMed, and Scopus (PRISMA 2020) used Freeman-Tukey random-effects synthesis with Cochrane risk-of-bias assessments; subgroup analyses examined study design, geography, era, molecular specificity, and interventions; sensitivity analyses tested robustness. RESULTS: The pooled LGG proportion was 57% (95% CI: 52%-61%; I²=99%; n=191). Mixed LGG/high-grade gliomas (HGG) cohorts showed 41% (32%-50%; 45 studies, 6,847 patients) versus 82% (77%-88%) in pure WHO Grade II cohorts (25 studies). Surgery-only cohorts demonstrated 46% (33%-59%) versus 86% (74%-98%) with targeted therapies, and 93% (90%-96%) in randomized controlled trials. Sensitivity analyses confirmed stability (50%-62%). CONCLUSION: In mixed-grade glioma cohorts, an LGG proportion approaching 60% may serve as a cohort-level epidemiological reference for understanding the historical grade composition of mixed surgical series. This meta-analysis primary value lies in applications such as clinical trial design, health economics and epidemiological modeling, and institutional benchmarking. papers.abstract_en: Lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD), a major subtype of non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), remains a leading cause of cancer-related mortality despite major therapeutic advances. Precision oncology has revolutionized the management of LUAD by identifying actionable molecular biomarkers and developing targeted therapies. In this review, we summarize the major predictive biomarkers in LUAD, including EGFR, KRAS, ALK, ROS1, MET, RET, BRAF, HER2, NTRK, and PD-L1, and describe the currently approved targeted therapies and emerging therapeutic strategies. Recent advances in selective inhibitors, antibody-drug conjugates, and immune checkpoint inhibitors that have improved clinical outcomes in molecularly defined patient populations are highlighted. The review also discusses the molecular basis of acquired resistance, such as on-target mutations, bypass signalling activation, histological transformation, and epithelial-mesenchymal transition that continue to limit long-term therapeutic efficacy. We also discuss emerging strategies to overcome resistance, including combination therapies, next-generation inhibitors, liquid biopsy-guided monitoring, and artificial intelligence-assisted precision medicine. Collectively, these findings highlight the need for comprehensive molecular characterization and integrated biomarker-guided treatment strategies to improve therapeutic decision-making and clinical outcomes in LUAD.

papers.title_zh: 帕博利珠单抗相关暴发性1型糖尿病：1例肾透明细胞癌患者病例报告及32例文献汇总分析
papers.title_en: Pembrolizumab-induced fulminant type 1 diabetes mellitus: a case report and literature review.
papers.authors: Sun S, Su L, Ma X, Dou J
papers.affiliation_highlight: Weifang People's Hospital, Shandong Second Medical University, Weifang, China.
papers.results: 本例患者HbA1c 6.7%，血糖显著升高、C肽极低，经补液及胰岛素治疗后好转出院；继续同药治疗3周期后永久停药。文献汇总32例中，FT1DM发病时间为治疗1至24个周期；GADA阳性者发病倾向更早；90%病例在FT1DM前或同时存在甲状腺功能异常；垂体功能异常1例、肾上腺功能异常1例均发生于FT1DM之后。
papers.authors_conclusion: 提示帕博利珠单抗治疗全程应持续代谢监测，FT1DM后应监测后续内分泌功能障碍；帕博利珠单抗相关FT1DM需长期胰岛素治疗；是否继续或重启帕博利珠单抗应在DKA纠正、血糖稳定后个体化决定。
papers.ai_note: 证据层级仅为个案加病例报告汇总，无对照、无系统检索策略与筛选流程描述，存在发表/回忆偏倚；'GADA阳性者发病更早'仅以'倾向'表述，未给出统计量；90%等比例均基于病例报告分母，缺乏总体用药人群基数，无法推算真实发生率；本例患者在确诊FT1DM后仍继续同药3周期，与随后'个体化决定'的结论之间存在张力，摘要未交代该决策依据与期间血糖管理细节。

pico.p: 1例接受帕博利珠单抗治疗的年轻男性ccRCC（可疑肺转移、既往甲状腺功能减退）患者；文献部分纳入32例确诊帕博利珠单抗相关暴发性1型糖尿病病例（以肺癌和黑色素瘤为主）
pico.ic: 帕博利珠单抗暴露（含继续用药3周期后永久停药）；无对照组

papers.reason: 提醒胸部肿瘤/免疫治疗随访中对罕见但致命的暴发性1型糖尿病及合并内分泌功能异常的识别与长期代谢监测，为免疫治疗安全性随访流程与患者教育提供病例级参照。
papers.abstract_en: As pembrolizumab has been widely used in the immunotherapy of various solid tumors such as melanoma and lung cancer, reports of pembrolizumab-related adverse drug events have gradually attracted attention; however, cases of pembrolizumab-induced fulminant type 1 diabetes mellitus (FT1DM) remain rare. This article reports a case of a young male patient with clear cell renal cell carcinoma (ccRCC) and suspected pulmonary metastases, who had a prior history of hypothyroidism and no family history of diabetes. After 22 cycles of pembrolizumab treatment, the patient developed lethargy and marked metabolic acidosis. The patient had markedly elevated blood glucose with an HbA1c of 6.7% and extremely low C-peptide levels. Given the history of pembrolizumab treatment, the patient was diagnosed with immune checkpoint inhibitor-associated FT1DM. His condition improved after fluid resuscitation and insulin therapy, and he was subsequently discharged. The patient continued treatment with the same agent for another three cycles before permanent discontinuation. Given the rarity of pembrolizumab-associated FT1DM, we further reviewed the literature. A literature search identified 32 confirmed cases of pembrolizumab-associated FT1DM, which were included in the analysis. The 32 reported cases mainly involved lung cancer and melanoma, with FT1DM onset ranging from 1 to 24 treatment cycles. GADA-positive patients tended to develop FT1DM earlier. Thyroid dysfunction occurred before or concurrently with FT1DM in 90% of cases. One case of pituitary dysfunction and one case of adrenal dysfunction both occurred after FT1DM onset. These findings suggest that metabolic monitoring should continue throughout pembrolizumab therapy, and that subsequent endocrine dysfunction should be monitored after FT1DM. Pembrolizumab-associated FT1DM requires long-term insulin therapy. Whether to continue or resume pembrolizumab should be decided individually after DKA resolution and glycemic stabilization.

papers.title_zh: 黑人乳腺癌女性财务毒性与抑郁症状的纵向相互预测关系：整体强相关但无前瞻性预测效应
papers.title_en: Examination of Longitudinal Interdependence Between Financial Toxicity and Depressive Symptoms in Black Women With Breast Cancer.
papers.authors: Thompson T, Rodebaugh TL, Carlton-Brown D, Margenthaler JA, Glover-Collins K, Charlot M, Troester M, Sargent E et al.
papers.affiliation_highlight: School of Social Work, University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill, Chapel Hill, North Carolina, USA.
papers.results: n=107；基线COST均值24.1（SD=9.9）；基线CES-D均值15.0（SD=10.9）；抑郁症状与财务毒性整体关联r=-0.63，p<0.001；两构念随时间未相互预测（摘要未报告交叉滞后系数及P值）
papers.authors_conclusion: 财务毒性与抑郁症状强相关，但未发现前瞻性效应；研究结果说明纵向财务毒性研究对于理解随时间变化模式的重要性。
papers.ai_note: ①主要假设之一（交叉滞后相互预测）为阴性，摘要仅以文字表述“did not predict each other over time”，未给出交叉滞后系数、置信区间或P值，无法判断是真实无效应还是样本量（n=107）不足以检出中小效应；②未报告检验效能或缺失数据处理细节；③抑郁以CES-D筛查量表评估，非临床诊断；④样本为单一族裔非转移性乳腺癌女性，外推受限；⑤横断面强相关被突出呈现，易被误读为因果或可干预路径；⑥该主题属乳腺心理社会肿瘤学，与胸部肿瘤临床决策无直接关联。

pico.p: 非转移性乳腺癌黑人女性，n=107，诊断后2个月内入组
pico.ic: 无干预与对照组设置；基线、2个月、4个月、18个月重复测量财务毒性（COST）与抑郁症状（CES-D）

papers.reason: 提供纵向设计的阴性证据：横断面强相关不等于随时间的前瞻性预测，为胸外科肿瘤患者报告结局（财务毒性、抑郁）队列的随访间隔设定与因果推断假设提供方法学对照基线，避免将相关误作预测。
papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Financial toxicity, or the negative economic effect of cancer treatment, has been cross-sectionally associated with poorer psychosocial outcomes in patients with breast cancer. Few studies have examined financial toxicity longitudinally or in Black women with cancer in particular. METHODS: Black women with non-metastatic breast cancer enrolled in this prospective study within 2 months of diagnosis. Participants completed the Comprehensive Score for Financial Toxicity (COST) and the Center for Epidemiologic Studies Depression (CES-D) at baseline, 2 months, 4 months, and 18 months. We used a random-intercept cross-lagged panel model to examine two components of the relationship between financial toxicity and depressive symptoms: the overall association (correlation of the intercepts) and the association over time. We hypothesized that financial toxicity would be associated with greater depressive symptoms (i.e., intercepts would be correlated). We further hypothesized that financial toxicity and depressive symptoms would predict each other over time (i.e., greater financial toxicity at one timepoint would be associated with greater depressive symptoms at the next timepoint, and vice versa). RESULTS: In 107 participants, mean baseline COST score was 24.1 (SD = 9.9); mean baseline CES-D score was 15.0 (SD = 10.9). We found a strong overall association between depressive symptoms and financial toxicity (r = -0.63, p < 0.001), but the constructs did not predict each other over time. CONCLUSIONS: Financial toxicity and depressive symptoms were strongly correlated, but we did not find prospective effects. Findings speak to the importance of longitudinal financial toxicity research in understanding patterns over time.

papers.title_zh: 职业与环境致癌物暴露与肺类癌的关联：范围综述提示暴露者中不典型类癌比例升高，但证据受研究数量与诊断标准限制
papers.title_en: Carcinoids of the lung caused by exogenous noxious agents: a scoping review.
papers.authors: Kilo S, Schröder C, Frei-Stuber L, Jöckel KH, Jonigk D, Länger F, Nowak D
papers.affiliation_highlight: Federal Institute for Occupational Safety and Health, BAuA, Berlin, Germany kilo.sonja@baua.bund.de.
papers.results: 世贸中心倒塌后暴露于粉尘人群中，类癌占肺癌病例的 6%（女性 9%，男性 3%）；类癌中不典型类癌比例由对照的 9.3% 升至吸烟者的 16.3%，石棉可能暴露者约 25% 升至确定暴露者 45%
papers.authors_conclusion: 基于这些发现，致癌物质（尤其是石棉和香烟烟雾）与类癌之间存在关联似乎是合理的（seems plausible）；需要在流行病学调查中开展更严格的分析，以进一步阐明肺类癌的发病机制。
papers.ai_note: 全文为叙事性汇总，未提供任何合并效应量、风险比或置信区间，无法判断关联强度与精确度；突出的均为比例变化（不典型类癌占比），属无对照匹配的构成比比较，易受诊断强度、监测偏倚、吸烟与石棉共暴露混杂影响；世贸中心 6%（9%/3%）数据缺少分母定义、对照人群与筛查方式说明，难以外推；纳入研究仅 14 项正式研究且多数肿瘤例数少、缺乏统一形态学与分子诊断标准，作者亦承认此局限；摘要以不典型类癌比例升高作为一致发现加以强调，但该终点并非预先设定的主要关联指标。

pico.p: 检索 1302 篇文献，最终纳入 27 篇原始研究及 7 篇会议论文，主题涉及吸烟暴露（n=23）与石棉暴露（n=6）及机制研究
pico.ic: 干预/暴露：职业或环境致癌物暴露（石棉、香烟烟雾、2001 年世贸中心倒塌粉尘）；对照：非暴露或暴露程度较低人群（用于比较不典型类癌占比）

papers.reason: 为肺类癌的病因学风险评估提供现有证据基线，提示石棉/吸烟暴露人群需关注不典型类癌比例升高这一假设；可用于设计后续带对照与统一病理复核的流行病学队列，而非直接改变当前手术或随访决策。
papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Approximately 2% of lung tumours are pulmonary carcinoids (PCs), divided into typical (90%) and atypical (AC) (10%). The link with external exposure to carcinogens remains controversial. OBJECTIVE: To investigate the association between occupational exposure to carcinogens and PC tumours. METHODS: A PRISMA-ScR-guided scoping review was performed. A systematic search was conducted in PubMed and Embase (January 2025). Studies were reviewed, data extracted, analysed and summarised narratively. RESULTS: 1302 studies were reviewed. 27 original studies and seven conference papers on topics including exposure to cigarette smoke (n=23) and asbestos (n=6), or mechanistic information, were included. Following the collapse of the World Trade Center in 2001, carcinoids accounted for 6% of lung cancer cases in people exposed to the resulting dust (9% in women, 3% in men). The proportion of ACs among carcinoids rose from 9.3% (controls) to 16.3% (smokers) and from ∼25% to 45% (probable versus definite asbestos exposure). Basic research has identified biological pathways linking harmful exposures (such as asbestos and cigarette smoke) to neuroendocrine cell proliferation and the potential progression of PCs to higher-grade lung tumours. DISCUSSION: The significance these of findings is limited due to 1) the limited number of studies, 2) the small number of tumours within those studies and 3) the lack of rigid diagnostic (morphological and molecular) criteria for PCs in most studies. Nevertheless, a consistent finding is a higher proportion of AC among carcinoids, particularly following asbestos exposure. CONCLUSIONS: Based on these findings, a link between carcinogenic substances (especially asbestos and cigarette smoke) and carcinoids seems plausible. More stringent analyses in epidemiological surveys are needed to further clarify the pathogenesis of PCs.

papers.title_en: GRP75-dependent SIMPA mediates inter-organellar quality control.
papers.authors: Yu F, Jiang L, Liu H, Yang S, Yuan Y, Jin H, Liu J, Liu X et al.
papers.affiliation_highlight: The State Key Laboratory of Medicinal Chemical Biology and Frontier of Science Center for Cell Response, College of Life…
papers.authors_conclusion: SIMPAs作为蛋白凝聚体，是线粒体质量控制的核心跨区室通讯枢纽，支持细胞与机体适应度；GRP75依赖的SIMPA信号级联在蛋白毒性应激下减弱线粒体应激并维护线粒体完整性。
papers.ai_note: 摘要通篇无样本量、无效应量、无统计量，全部为定性描述，无法评估可重复性与效应强度；证据仅来自细胞模型与肝病模型，未涉及肺/胸部肿瘤或任何患者队列，不能外推至胸外科临床；『支持细胞与机体适应度』属概括性推断，缺乏体内系统层面的量化终点；与六类分栏均不契合，归入advanced仅为形式归属，实际为纯基础细胞生物学。
papers.reason: 与胸外科及胸部肿瘤的诊疗决策无直接关联，不改变手术选择、随访或结节风险判断；仅在理解肿瘤细胞线粒体蛋白稳态与细胞器互作的应激适应机制层面提供背景参考，不构成本领域证据基础。
papers.abstract_en: Mitochondria are bound by a double membrane and are semiautonomous organelles, rendering them highly vulnerable to global and internal proteostatic stress1. Multiple surveillance mechanisms at proteostatic and inter-organellar levels have evolved to maintain mitochondrial integrity and cellular health2-7. However, the precise mechanisms by which proteostatic damage relays stress signals across organelles and how the quality surveillance machinery coordinates these functions remain unknown. Here we report that under proteostatic stress, damaged mitochondrial proteins are sequestered to form stress-induced mitochondrial protein aggregates (SIMPAs) that activate specific quality control mechanisms in a spatially confined manner without perturbing the mitochondrial network. Quantitative proteomic and correlative light-electron microscopy analysis revealed that SIMPA mediates inter-organellar communication via mitochondria-endoplasmic reticulum contact sites or mitochondrial-associated membranes. Mechanistically, GRP75 coordinates SIMPA biogenesis and focally activates endoplasmic reticulum unfolded protein response pathways via mitochondria-endoplasmic reticulum contact sites or mitochondrial-associated membranes for the targeted clearance of SIMPAs. Functionally, in both cellular and liver disease models, we found that a GRP75-dependent SIMPA signalling cascade attenuates mitochondrial stress and preserves mitochondrial integrity under proteotoxic stress. Overall, we show that SIMPAs, functioning as protein condensates, serve as a central cross-compartment communication hub for mitochondrial quality control, supporting cellular and organismal fitness.

papers.authors: Qian J, Bassiouni R, Jin Y, Rajpara S, Neuman M, Khetan VU, Salhia B, Craig DW et al.
papers.affiliation_highlight: Department of Cancer Biology, Keck School of Medicine, University of Southern California, Los Angeles, California, Unite…

papers.abstract_en: High-grade serous ovarian cancer (HGSOC) is characterized by remarkable intratumoral heterogeneity and variable tissue architectures, dictating differential therapeutic responses. Although BRCA1/2 mutations correlate with improved responses to DNA-damaging agents, how BRCA genotype shapes the tumor immune microenvironment (TIME) remains incompletely understood. Here, we integrated whole exome sequencing, total RNA sequencing and spatial transcriptomics to profile a cohort of BRCA-mutated (BRCA-MT) and non-BRCA-mutated (BRCA-WT) HGSOC tumors. While bulk transcriptomics highlighted global phenotypic shifts, suggesting a more pro-inflammatory milieu in BRCA-MT tumors, spatially resolved analysis revealed how these differences manifest within specific tissue architectures. Integrated clustering revealed recurrent spatial transcriptional states across genotypes. Specifically, we identified a transcriptionally distinct immune-enriched region (IC7) characterized by low tumor purity, interferon signaling, and antigen-presentation programs. Reference-based RCTD deconvolution provided orthogonal computational support that IC7 was enriched for T/NK and dendritic cells relative to non-IC7 regions. At the patient level, the functional state of IC7 was highly BRCA-dependent: BRCA-MT tumors exhibited stronger enrichment of interferon-α/γ responses and inflammatory signaling than BRCA-WT tumors. Exploratory CellChat analysis further suggested genotype-associated differences in predicted immune-related signaling. We also identify a conserved structural interface between CAF-like region (IC3) and macrophage-rich region (IC4), accompanied by a predicted CXCL12-CXCR4 chemokine recruitment axis. Taken together, these findings support a model in which BRCA mutation status is associated with functional differences within broadly conserved spatial regions, rather than extensive reorganization of the overall spatial architecture. This spatially resolved framework identifies BRCA-associated immune transcriptional patterns in HGSOC and provides a basis for future mechanistic validation.

papers.abstract_en: Epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) mutant-driven non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) frequently develops acquired resistance to third-generation tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKIs), particularly through the EGFR C797S mutation. Existing EGFR-targeting proteolysis-targeting chimeras (PROTACs) remain limited by unfavorable pharmacokinetics and suboptimal selectivity inherited from their parent TKIs. To address these limitations, we developed HQY1480, a next-generation PROTAC derived from the macrocyclic fourth-generation EGFR inhibitor BI-4020. Systematic linker and E3 ligase ligand optimization enabled potent and selective degradation of multiple clinically relevant EGFR mutants with single-digit nanomolar DC50 values. HQY1480 exhibited favorable pharmacokinetics, stronger suppression of oncogenic signaling than BI-4020, and no detectable off-target degradation in proteomic profiling. In xenograft models, HQY1480 outperformed BI-4020, overcame osimertinib resistance, and effectively inhibited tumor growth at low doses, while inducing robust EGFR degradation in patient-derived xenografts. These findings establish HQY1480 as an effective and well-tolerated lead PROTAC for EGFR-mutant NSCLC with acquired resistance to third-generation TKIs.

papers.abstract_en: Fatty acid (FA)-induced internalization of the FA transporter CD36 normally functions as an intrinsic brake on FA uptake and lipid overload, but cancer cells can bypass this checkpoint to sustain lipid-fueled growth. The mechanism underlying this failure remains unclear. Here, we identify a FA 2-hydroxylase (FA2H)-CD36 signaling axis that operates as an endogenous brake on lipid fueling in gastric cancer cells. FA2H-derived (R)-2-hydroxy palmitic acid ((R)-2-OHPA) disrupts CD36 interaction with its palmitoyltransferase DHHC4, thereby limiting CD36 palmitoylation and trafficking to the plasma membrane. Loss of FA2H permits CD36 palmitoylation and establishes a feed-forward loop that amplifies FA uptake, lipid accumulation, and tumor growth. Restoring FA2H expression or supplementing cells with exogenous (R)-2-OHPA reinstates the lipid-sensing checkpoint. Moreover, FA2H activation sensitizes gastric cancer cells to inhibition of endogenous FA synthesis through blockade of FA synthase (FASN) or stearoyl-CoA desaturase 1 (SCD1). In vivo, (R)-2-OHPA treatment or expression of the palmitoylation-deficient CD36 AASS mutant attenuates FA2H deficiency-driven lipid accumulation and tumor growth, positioning CD36 palmitoylation as the critical effector in this metabolic circuit. Together, these findings establish FA 2-hydroxylation as a metabolic checkpoint that links FA structure to CD36 trafficking and FA utilization in gastric cancer, revealing a targetable vulnerability in lipid-driven tumor growth.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Combined pulmonary fibrosis and emphysema-associated pulmonary hypertension (CPFE-PH) has emerged as a distinct third category of PH, yet its detailed clinical-hemodynamic profile, pathological features, and comparative outcomes remain poorly defined. This study aims to characterize the phenotype of CPFE-PH and compare it with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease-related PH (COPD-PH) and idiopathic interstitial pneumonia-related PH (IIP-PH). METHODS: In this multicenter cohort study, we analyzed 113 patients with CPFE-PH, 277 with COPD-PH, and 78 with IIP-PH, all diagnosed by right heart catheterization. Clinical, physiological, imaging, pathological, treatment response, and survival data were statistically compared across groups. RESULTS: CPFE-PH patients were older, predominantly male smokers, and exhibited preserved ventilatory function but severely reduced diffusing capacity (DLCO 31.6% predicted, IQR 24.8-37.8). They had the most severe hemodynamic compromise (mean pulmonary arterial pressure 41 mmHg, pulmonary vascular resistance 7.4 Wood units), a high prevalence of mediastinal lymphadenopathy (81.4%), and universal capillary hemangiomatosis-like remodeling, a pathological feature absent in COPD-PH and rarely observed in IIP-PH. Pulmonary arterial hypertension-targeted therapy failed to improve functional or biomarker outcomes, and transplant-free survival was shortest in CPFE-PH (median 32 months) compared with COPD-PH and IIP-PH (P < 0.05). CONCLUSIONS: CPFE-PH appears to represent a severe phenotype within Group 3 PH, in which prominent capillary remodeling, including hemangiomatosis-like changes, may contribute to its clinical, radiological, and functional manifestations, distinguish it from other Group 3 PH types. CLINICAL TRIAL: Chinese Clinical Study.org, No: ChiCTR2000032212, Registration Date: 2020-04-23; URL: http://www.chictr.org.cn/ .

papers.abstract_en: This study aimed to develop and validate a nomogram based on clinical and computed tomography (CT) features for the preoperative prediction of invasiveness in patients with solitary pulmonary ground-glass nodules (GGNs). We retrospectively analyzed 846 patients with solitary GGNs who underwent surgical resection at the Lung Cancer Center of West China Hospital between November 2022 and January 2024. All nodules were pathologically confirmed as atypical adenomatous hyperplasia (AAH), adenocarcinoma in situ (AIS), minimally invasive adenocarcinoma (MIA), or invasive adenocarcinoma (IAC). Patients were classified into a non-invasive group (including AAH, AIS, and MIA) and an IAC group based on postoperative pathological results. Clinical data and CT features before surgery were collected. Patients were randomly assigned to a training cohort (n = 592) and a validation cohort (n = 254) in a ratio of 7:3. Least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression was used for feature selection, followed by multivariate logistic regression to identify independent predictors and construct a nomogram model. The variance inflation factor (VIF) was used to evaluate multicollinearity among the candidate predictors. Model performance was assessed using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), calibration curves, and decision curve analysis (DCA). Multivariate logistic regression analysis revealed that the maximum tumor diameter (OR = 39.82, 95% CI: 16.29-97.32), consolidation-to-tumor ratio (0.5<CTR<1, OR = 2.51, 95% CI: 1.36-4.63), vacuole sign (OR = 2.29, 95% CI: 1.29-4.07), pleura traction sign (OR = 3.03, 95% CI: 1.66-5.53), and the presence of solid component on the mediastinal window (OR = 3.27, 95% CI: 1.46-7.28) were independent risk factors for IAC. The nomogram constructed based on these variables demonstrated good discriminative ability, with AUC values of 0.930 and 0.913 in the training and validation cohorts, respectively. Calibration curves demonstrated good agreement between the predicted and observed probabilities, and DCA indicated favorable clinical utility. Consequently, this nomogram based on the maximum tumor diameter, CTR, vacuole sign, pleura traction sign, and the presence of solid component on the mediastinal window, provides an effective and noninvasive tool for preoperative prediction of the invasiveness of solitary GGNs.

papers.abstract_en: AIMS: To summarize the clinical features, treatment patterns and survival outcomes of patients with non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) combined with connective tissue disease (CTD), and to determine whether CTD independently influences prognosis and treatment-related toxicity in this special patient population. METHODS: In this retrospective study, we enrolled 200 consecutive patients with pathologically confirmed NSCLC. Among them, 95 patients met the diagnostic criteria for CTD were set as the CTD group, and the remaining 105 patients with simple NSCLC as the control group. The primary endpoint was overall survival (OS). Secondary endpoints included progression-free survival (PFS), baseline tumor characteristics, metastatic patterns, first-line treatment patterns and delivery, and treatment-related adverse events (AEs). We adopted Kaplan-Meier method for survival analysis and Cox proportional hazards regression model for prognostic analysis. Prespecified subgroup analyses were performed to evaluate the prognostic effect of CTD and identify independent survival predictors. RESULTS: The CTD group presented more severe intrathoracic tumor dissemination, including higher incidence of bilateral pulmonary lesions (P = 0.042) and pleural effusion (P = 0.011). Compared with controls, the CTD group were less likely to receive platinum-based doublet chemotherapy (P = 0.035), cisplatin-based chemotherapy (P = 0.017), immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI)-containing therapy (P = 0.009) and thoracic radiotherapy (P = 0.029). Meanwhile, the CTD group had higher risks of chemotherapy dose reduction (P = 0.011), treatment delay longer than 7 days (P = 0.015) and early treatment discontinuation (P = 0.002). In survival outcomes, the median PFS was 5.4 vs 7.8 months (HR, 1.58; 95% CI, 1.17-2.13; P = 0.003), and the median OS was 9.7 vs 14.6 months (HR, 1.76; 95% CI, 1.29-2.40; P<0.001). The incidence of grade 3-4 treatment-related AEs was significantly higher in the CTD group (P = 0.010). Multivariate regression analysis confirmed that CTD was an independent adverse prognostic factor for poor OS (HR, 1.41; 95% CI, 1.01-1.97; P = 0.044). CONCLUSION: For patients diagnosed with NSCLC, comorbid CTD is correlated with aggravated intrathoracic tumor dissemination, reduced treatment intensity and treatment tolerance, increased severe toxicity, and dismal long-term survival.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: ORCHARD (NCT03944772) was a biomarker-directed, phase II, platform study conducted to characterize resistance mechanisms and evaluate novel treatment combinations in patients with epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR)-mutated non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) following progression on first-line osimertinib. We report results from the module evaluating osimertinib plus platinum-based chemotherapy. METHODS: Patients received osimertinib (80 mg once daily) plus ≤ 4 cycles of platinum-based doublet chemotherapy (pemetrexed 500 mg/m2 plus carboplatin AUC5) on day 1 of every 21-day cycle, followed by pemetrexed maintenance until disease progression, unacceptable toxicity, or another discontinuation criterion. The primary endpoint was objective response rate (ORR) using Response Evaluation Criteria in Solid Tumors v1.1. Secondary endpoints were progression-free survival (PFS), duration of response (DoR), overall survival (OS), and safety. RESULTS: Thirty-one patients received study treatment. Eight patients had a confirmed partial response (ORR 26%; 80% CI, 16-39). Median DoR was 7.6 months (95% CI, 4.2-not calculable). Median PFS was 5.6 months (95% CI, 4.0-7.5); PFS events were reported in 29 (94%) patients. Median OS was 10.9 months (95% CI, 8.5-15.0); 20 (65%) patients had died at data cut-off. Grade ≥ 3 adverse events (AEs) occurred in 20 (65%) patients; AEs leading to discontinuation of any treatment occurred in 7 (23%) patients. CONCLUSION: In patients with EGFR-mutated advanced NSCLC who had progressed on first-line osimertinib, osimertinib plus platinum-based chemotherapy demonstrated a modest clinical benefit and manageable safety profile, consistent with the individual drug profiles.

At 4 weeks, OCT showed no significant differences in EP and LP thicknesses between groups, although both remained different from the healthy contralateral mucosa. CONCLUSIONS: Both laser modalities provided favorable clinical outcomes and specimens suitable for histopathological diagnosis. The 1064-nm nanosecond-pulsed Nd:YAG laser resulted in significantly lower thermal alteration than the 980-nm diode laser, while OCT showed comparable tissue morphology at 4 weeks. These findings suggest a potential advantage of the nanosecond-pulsed Nd:YAG laser when minimizing thermal damage is a priority.

papers.abstract_en: PURPOSE: Virtual-assisted lung mapping (VAL-MAP) is a safe and useful procedure for identifying suitable lines for sublobar lung resections. Nonetheless, the current VAL-MAP technique using a thin bronchoscope limits access to peripheral lung regions, including the upper lobes or the S6 region. METHODS: To overcome this limitation, we developed a new technique utilizing an ultrathin bronchoscope (UTB), termed 'UTB VAL-MAP', enabling precise dye marking of the visceral pleura which is difficult to access with a thin bronchoscope. RESULTS: Overall, 178 preoperative markings (75 patients) were included: 74 markings in 35 patients in the UTB VAL-MAP group and 104 markings in 40 patients in the conventional VAL-MAP group. The overall detection rate in the UTB VAL-MAP group was significantly higher than that in the conventional VAL-MAP group [97.3% (72/74) vs. 84.6% (88/104); P = 0.005]. Furthermore, the marking success rate using indigo carmine in the UTB VAL-MAP group was higher for lesions located in the upper lobe and S6 region than that in the conventional VAL-MAP group (P < 0.001). In multivariate generalized estimating equations models, UTB use (odds ratio = 7.390, P = 0.015) was significantly associated with overall detection rate. No severe procedure-related complications occurred in either group. CONCLUSION: UTB VAL-MAP appears useful for increasing the rate of successful visceral pleura marking, particularly in the upper lobes or S6 areas, which the conventional VAL-MAP technique has difficulty reaching, without increasing complications.

papers.abstract_en: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) imposes substantial risk to all infants, but its impact on youth with SCD (Y-SCD) is underexplored. With newer, highly effective RSV monoclonal antibodies (RSV-mAb), research is needed to inform their use in Y-SCD. This single-center study of Y-SCD aged 0-21 years identified 667 hospitalizations that included RSV testing. Of these, 5% were positive for RSV, and 68% occurred in Y-SCD beyond their first RSV season. Intensive care, positive pressure ventilation, and transfusion were required in 21%, 32%, and 21% of hospitalizations, respectively. Findings indicate that multicenter studies are warranted to determine if RSV-mAbs improve outcomes in Y-SCD.

papers.abstract_en: Intrathecal methotrexate (MTX) remains a critical component in multiagent chemotherapy regimens for acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL). However, MTX-induced neurotoxicity (MIN) can cause significant morbidity. Aminophylline can be a treatment for MIN, mitigating neurotoxicity, but its use has been restricted to case reports and small patient series. In this report, we present treatment outcomes of seven patients who developed MIN and received aminophylline. The median time-to-improvement after aminophylline was 9 h, and the median time to full resolution of symptoms was 36 h. All patients developed full symptom resolution, advocating aminophylline as treatment of MIN in patients with ALL.

papers.abstract_en: In the literature, shear-wave elastography (SWE) is most often described for evaluating the elasticity of internal organs; nevertheless, it has also been increasingly used to assess the musculoskeletal system. In clinical and research settings, changes in the mechanical properties of musculoskeletal tissues can be observed in conditions related to overuse, sports injuries, congenital anomalies, neurological disorders, and other musculoskeletal conditions. SWE enables the assessment of these changes and may facilitate monitoring of disease-related alterations, therapeutic effects, and adaptations associated with physical training. The aim of this systematic review was to identify and synthesize all studies using SWE to assess the musculoskeletal system in the paediatric population. A total of 67 studies involving 2,558 children aged 1 day to 18 years were included. SWE was applied to a wide range of musculoskeletal structures and clinical populations, with substantial heterogeneity in study designs, ultrasound systems, measurement protocols, anatomical positioning, and reported outcomes. Twenty two studies assessed the reliability of SWE measurements, with reliability varying according to the examined structure and measurement conditions. Due to the substantial methodological and clinical heterogeneity of the included studies, a quantitative meta-analysis was not performed. Overall, the available evidence demonstrates a broad range of potential applications of SWE in paediatric musculoskeletal assessment, while also highlighting the need for greater methodological standardization and further research to establish robust reference values and clinically applicable protocols.

papers.abstract_en: Understanding how scientific datasets are accessed and reused is essential for resource planning and impact assessment. Here we present the PRIDE Archive download tracking infrastructure and a comprehensive analysis of 159.3 million download records from the PRIDE proteomics database (2021-2025), spanning 35,528 datasets accessed from 235 locations. The infrastructure includes nf-downloadstats, a scalable Nextflow pipeline for processing download logs, and DeepLogBot, a machine-learning framework that classifies traffic into bots, institutional download hubs, and independent user downloads. DeepLogBot combines heuristic seed selection with multi-LLM annotation (Claude and Qwen3) to produce LLM-assisted consensus labels, achieving 92.2% bot classification accuracy on a held-out test set. After separating bot traffic, analysis reveals downloads from 214 countries/regions, 249 institutional download hubs, and a concentrated reuse distribution, with the top five countries (United States, United Kingdom, Germany, China, and Canada) accounting for over 54% of independent user downloads. These findings provide actionable insights for repository infrastructure planning and highlight the importance of distinguishing automated from individual access in scientific data resources.

Results Of an estimated 2,970 hospitalizations (594 sampled), 36.5% involved PDT. Annual volumes declined for PDT (215 to 115; P-trend=0.023) and OST (480 to 165; P-trend=0.003). Conclusions Both OST and PDT volumes declined. No significant association was detected between approach and short-term outcomes, although estimates were imprecise. The mortality increase within OST hospitalizations, concentrated in the pandemic period, warrants cautious interpretation given potential changes in case mix, treatment selection, pandemic-related practice, and unmeasured severity.

papers.abstract_en: Stimuli-responsive supramolecular nanocarriers capable of controlled drug release have emerged as promising alternatives to conventional chemotherapy; however, the development of structurally defined small-molecule systems exhibiting thermo-responsive behavior within biologically relevant temperature ranges remains challenging. Herein, we report a series of ionizable xanthone-based bolaamphiphiles (X1-X3) engineered to undergo temperature-triggered self-assembly in aqueous media. Systematic modulation of oxyethylene-chain density revealed that X3 exhibits a sharp and reversible lower critical solution temperature (LCST) transition within the physiological temperature window (35-40 °C), leading to the formation of stable nanovesicular assemblies. The resulting X3 nanovesicles accommodate doxorubicin (DOX) with an encapsulation efficiency of ∼25% and a drug-loading content of 11% while maintaining good colloidal stability under physiologically relevant conditions. X3-DOX nanovesicles exhibit progressive thermoresponsive drug release near physiological temperature, which is further enhanced under mild hyperthermia, together with an additional acid-responsive release behavior associated with protonation of the piperazine units (apparent pKa ≈ 4.5). Cellular studies performed in 4T1 breast cancer and A549 lung cancer cells demonstrated enhanced intracellular drug accumulation, superior cytotoxicity, and effective suppression of multicellular tumor spheroids compared with free DOX. Furthermore, the nanoformulation exhibited excellent hemocompatibility, favorable biodistribution characteristics, and efficient systemic clearance. In a 4T1 tumor-bearing mouse model, X3-DOX induced remarkable tumor-growth inhibition with minimal systemic toxicity. These findings establish thermo-responsive xanthone-based nanovesicles as a versatile supramolecular platform for controlled anticancer drug delivery and provide a molecularly defined strategy for developing stimuli-responsive nanomedicines.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: De novo malignancies are a major cause of late death following lung transplantation (LTx). Although previous reports from Japan have identified post-transplant lymphoproliferative disorder (PTLD) as the most common de novo malignancy, comprehensive long-term data on the spectrum, treatment, and outcomes of de novo malignancies remain limited. METHODS: We retrospectively reviewed the medical records of 413 patients who underwent LTx at our institution between April 2002 and December 2025 and analyzed the incidence, characteristics, and outcomes of de novo malignancies. RESULTS: De novo malignancy was diagnosed in 53 patients (12.8%), comprising 18 cases of PTLD and 37 cases of solid tumors (42 tumors in total). The cumulative incidence of PTLD was 3.1% at 1 year and remained stable thereafter, whereas the incidence of solid tumors increased steadily over time, reaching 16.8% at 10 years after LTx. PTLD and solid tumors showed distinct temporal patterns, with median times to onset of 8.0 months and 64.0 months, respectively. Regarding post-LTx lung cancer, five of the six cases (83.3%) originated in the native lung after single LTx. The 2-year overall survival after malignancy diagnosis was significantly higher in the curative treatment group than in the non-curative group (87.9% vs. 16.7%, p < 0.001). CONCLUSIONS: Our findings demonstrate that the risk of solid malignancies continues to increase during long-term follow-up after LTx. The favorable outcomes observed among patients receiving curative treatment are considered to reflect earlier detection and better baseline patients' condition, underscoring the importance of post-transplant cancer surveillance.

papers.abstract_en: INTRODUCTION: In September 2021, the eruption of the Tajogaite volcano on La Palma (Spain) released large amounts of toxic gases and particulate matter over three months. This study, part of the ASHES Project, analyses the serum cytokine profile and its relationship with exposure to these pollutants in general population, asthma patients, and occupationally exposed workers. MATERIALS AND METHODS: In this cross-sectional study, 102 participants (69 women; median age 50 years) were included. Structured interviews were conducted, and serum samples were collected to quantify 48 biomarkers related to TH1, TH2, and TH17 inflammatory responses (Olink®). Participants were classified into three groups: healthy population (n = 66), occupationally exposed workers (n = 13), and asthmatic patients (n = 23). Comparisons were performed between healthy population vs. asthmatics and healthy population vs. occupational group. RESULTS: Occupationally exposed workers showed the highest exposure (median 10 h), compared with 6 h in the healthy population and 5 h in asthmatics (p = 0.006). This group, with highest exposure, had increased levels of IL-2, IL-7, IL-17A, and IL-17F compared with the general population. Asthmatic patients showed higher levels of IL-2, IL-7, TNFSF12, CXCL10, IL-17C, CCL3, and CCL4, and lower levels of IL-15 and MMP12 (p < 0.05). A strong positive correlation between IL-4 and exposure time (r = 0.7935, p < 0.0001), and negative correlations with CCL8, CXCL11, and TNF-α were observed in asthmatics. CONCLUSIONS: Volcanic emissions are associated with exposure- and disease-dependent immune responses. Asthmatics show heightened TH1/TH2/TH17 activation, while highly exposed workers display a TH17-skewed profile, with the general population maintaining a balanced response, suggesting greater vulnerability in asthma patients.

METHODS: The participants of this study are 283 male miners in a tin mine in China. A targeted research design was adopted to conduct a questionnaire survey, physical examination, blood sample analysis coupled with radon concentration measurements, statistical analysis was performed to investigate the impact of varying levels of radon exposure on hematological and biochemical parameters among the participants. RESULTS: Mean platelet volume (MPV), plateletcrit (PCT), and platelet-large cell ratio (P-LCR) decreased significantly across the working-level month (WLM) groups (Bonferroni-corrected P < 0.003), as did albumin (ALB) and the albumin-to-globulin (A/G) ratio (Bonferroni-corrected P < 0.0045). All values remained within clinically normal reference ranges. CONCLUSION: Cumulative occupational radon exposure was independently associated with decreased platelet volume indices and elevated urea levels in miners, suggesting subclinical hematological changes and altered renal-related parameters. These findings contribute to occupational health surveillance frameworks for populations chronically exposed to radon in mining environments.

papers.abstract_en: Metastasis represents a major cause of chemotherapy failure in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). To explore the role of CYP1B1 enzymatic activity in NSCLC metastasis, we established A549 and H460 cells overexpressing wild-type CYP1B1, an activity-enhanced variant (L432V), and an activity-reduced variant (N203S). CYP1B1 did not affect cell proliferation but promoted migration and invasion, with the extent of these effects being associated with CYP1B1 enzymatic activity. We then designed and synthesized a series of CYP1B1 inhibitors. Compound G26 exhibited high selectivity over other CYP isoforms (IC50 = 5.33 nM), showed favorable microsomal metabolic stability with species differences, significantly inhibited migration and invasion in A549 and H460 cells, exhibited moderate oral bioavailability in SD rats (F = 20.7%), and showed a favorable safety profile in mice.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Thoracic cancers during pregnancy are rare but increasingly encountered because of delayed childbearing and the rising incidence of cancer in younger individuals. Despite guideline recommendations, exposure to targeted small-molecule therapies occurs across all trimesters, but safety data remain limited. OBJECTIVE: To investigate the safety of targeted small-molecule therapies for thoracic cancers during pregnancy by combining VigiBase data with a systematic review. PATIENTS AND METHODS: We performed a pharmacovigilance disproportionality analysis based on the reporting odds ratio (ROR) and a systematic review. Individual case safety reports from VigiBase (January 1, 2006-February 24, 2026) were analysed. A systematic review of PubMed, EMBASE, and Scopus through June 25, 2026 included case reports and case series. RESULTS: The VigiBase analysis included 15,023 reports of anticancer exposure during pregnancy, of which 162 involved small molecules currently used on- and off-label for thoracic cancers, including 75 with approved agents for non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC). Compared with other anticancer agents, including cytotoxic drugs, immune checkpoint inhibitors, other immunotherapies, antibody-drug conjugates, molecularly targeted therapies (including biologics and small molecules other than those of interest), and anticancer agents not further specified, the small molecules of interest were associated with disproportionate reporting of premature labor (ROR: 2.64; 95% confidence interval [CI]: 1.21-5.75), foetal growth restriction (ROR: 2.10; 95% CI 1.15-3.84), neonatal respiratory distress syndrome (ROR: 3.78; 95% CI 1.50-9.57), and low birth weight (ROR: 2.27; 95% CI 1.18-4.37). Among approved small molecules for NSCLC, signals were observed for premature labor (ROR: 4.17; 95% CI 1.65-10.53), neonatal respiratory complications (ROR: 2.56; 95% CI 1.02-6.42), and low birth weight (ROR: 3.55; 95% CI 1.61-7.83). Of note, anaplastic lymphoma kinase (ALK) inhibitor ICSRs were fewer, and 14/18 alectinib reports described pregnancy exposure without pregnancy-related ADRs of interest, precluding alectinib-specific disproportionality analysis. The systematic review included 26 women (27 pregnancies) with oncogene-driven metastatic NSCLC. Live births occurred in 96.3% of pregnancies, with 53.8% preterm deliveries, 33.3% pregnancy complications, and 19.2% neonatal complications. Maternal outcomes were favourable (objective response rate 80.8%). There were no clinically significant pregnancy complications reported in the 10 cases involving alectinib exposure alone. CONCLUSIONS: Exposure during pregnancy to small molecules currently used on- and off-label for thoracic cancers was associated with disproportionate reporting signals for selected adverse foetal outcomes. The available clinical evidence remains limited, and although no clinically significant pregnancy complications were reported with alectinib exposure, the current data are insufficient to establish its safety. Treatment decisions should therefore be individualised and made within a multidisciplinary expert setting.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: DNA methylation alterations are stable, biologically informative, and detectable in tissue and circulating DNA, making them promising biomarkers for non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). However, few methylation biomarkers have entered routine clinical practice. We aimed to characterize the evolution and translational challenges of this field. METHODS: Publications on NSCLC, DNA methylation, and biomarker applications were retrieved from the Web of Science Core Collection through 31 December 2025. After PRISMA-based screening, bibliometric and knowledge-map analyses were performed. RESULTS: A total of 1,910 publications were included. Annual output increased after 2010 and peaked in 2022. Lung Cancer was the most productive journal, whereas Cancer Research had the highest citation impact. China contributed the largest publication volume, while the United States had the highest citation impact. Foundational studies focused on promoter hypermethylation, methylation-specific PCR, and methylated DNA detection in accessible biospecimens. Research priorities shifted from candidate-gene studies toward methylation signatures, liquid biopsy, multi-omics integration, immunotherapy-related applications, and computational modeling. CONCLUSION: NSCLC methylation biomarker research has evolved toward integrated translational frameworks. Future progress requires multicenter validation, standardized platforms, clinically defined methylation panels, and AI-assisted integration. papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Occupational epidemiological analyses typically focus on a priori hypotheses relating disease to specific exposures or occupations. We used regularized regression models to agnostically identify occupations associated with lung cancer while accounting for known lung carcinogens. METHODS: We pooled data from 14 European and Canadian lung cancer case-control studies. The main analysis included 13 587 cases and 16 410 controls for men and 3199 cases and 4408 controls for women. Associations between ever-employment in various occupations and lung cancer risks were evaluated using two selection approaches: a least absolute shrinkage and selection operator regression and a two-stage Bayesian hierarchical horseshoe model accounting for age, study, smoking, and occupational exposure to known lung carcinogens. Unconditional logistic regression models were used to estimate odds ratios (ORs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) for selected occupations. RESULTS: For men, occupations consistently identified as positively associated with lung cancer included miners (OR = 1.28, 95% CI: 1.06-1.54) and bricklayers (OR = 1.30, 95% CI: 1.12-1.52), while secondary education teachers (OR = 0.37, 95% CI: 0.22-0.60), production managers (OR = 0.66, 95% CI: 0.54-0.81), and government executive officials (OR = 0.72, 95% CI: 0.62-0.83) were negatively associated. For women, secondary language and literature teachers (OR = 0.39, 95% CI: 0.20-0.72) and government executive officials (OR = 0.63, 95% CI: 0.48-0.81) showed negative associations. CONCLUSION: Two agnostic, data-driven models identified several occupations associated with both increased and decreased lung cancer risks. These associations persisted after accounting for known exposures and covariates, highlighting the need to investigate unidentified occupational factors.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE: High-dose-rate endobronchial brachytherapy (HDR-BTE) is an effective technique for the treatment of malignant tracheobronchial tumors. Although two-dimensional (2D) planning provides limited dosimetric information and does not accurately assess the relationship between the catheter and the tumor or the dose delivered to organs at risk (OARs), it continues to be used because it ensures adequate PTV coverage, is associated with low toxicity, and minimizes the risk of catheter displacement by avoiding patient transfer to the CT simulation room. PATIENT AND METHODS: An 83-year-old patient with 2D HDR-BTE for tracheal recurrence of previously resected lung adenocarcinoma was analyzed and compared with four simulated 3D plans based on catheter position relative to the tumor volume, while keeping the active length and prescribed dose constant. RESULTS: The favorable oblique scenario achieved the best PTV coverage (D90: 9.05 Gy; V100: 100%), although with highest V150 (96.47%) and homogeneity index (IH: 5.14). The unfavorable oblique and posterior positions significantly reduced coverage (V100: 51.4% and 61.29%, respectively). The esophagus was the most sensitive organ, showing the highest doses in the posterior orientation of the catheter. The contralateral lung and heart received low doses; while the aorta showed higher doses in the favorable oblique scenario due to the location of the PTV. CONCLUSIONS: Catheter orientation in HDR-BTE has a significant impact on PTV coverage and the dose delivered to critical organs. Despite the trend toward 3D planning, there is no direct clinical evidence comparing the two techniques.

papers.abstract_en: RATIONALE: Immune checkpoint inhibition (ICI) targeting programmed death-1 or its ligand (PD-1/PD-L1) is being explored as an addition to standard treatment for esophageal cancer (EC) to improve response rates, yet robust methods for patient selection are lacking. The predictive value of PD-L1 expression in biopsies is inconsistent due to intra- and intertumoral heterogeneity, and the impact of neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy (CRT) on ICI response is unclear. Improving patient selection for receiving ICI therapies in patients with EC requires a better understanding of the drug's distribution and target binding. Here, we investigated the distribution of fluorescently labelled durvalumab (durvalumab-680LT) using ultrasound-guided quantitative fluorescence molecular endoscopy (US-qFME) before and after CRT in 20 patients with EC. METHODS: US-qFME included in vivo mucosal fluorescence imaging, spectroscopic quantification, and biopsy sampling of the tumor and healthy tissue. For dose optimization, 0, 4.5, 15, and 25 mg durvalumab-680LT were used pre-CRT. RESULTS: Quantifying in vivo fluorescence revealed a dose-dependent increase in the durvalumab-680LT signal in tumor tissues pre-CRT, with the highest fluorescence intensity and highest interpatient variability in the 25-mg group (ranges: 4.5 mg: 0.0101-0.0202 mm⁻¹, 15 mg: 0.01295-0.03225 mm⁻¹, 25 mg: 0.01720-0.0514 mm⁻¹). Sixty percent of patients (n = 3 in both dose cohorts) in the 15 mg and 25 mg cohorts exhibited high durvalumab-680LT signals with a tumor-to-healthy tissue ratio ≥2. Lower fluorescence signals were measured post-CRT compared to pre-CRT. Finally, durvalumab-680LT binding to tumor cells was confirmed using fluorescence microscopy. CONCLUSIONS: US-qFME combined with durvalumab-680LT enables the visualization of durvalumab uptake in EC and reveals interpatient variability, supporting its potential future role in selecting patients for ICI therapy.

papers.abstract_en: INTRODUCTION: Atrial fibrillation (AF) is associated with a significantly increased risk of thromboembolic complications, including ischaemic stroke. Despite the dominant role of oral anticoagulants, low-molecular-weight heparins (LMWHs) are still used in selected clinical scenarios. AIM: The aim of this review was to summarise the current clinical role of LMWHs in atrial fibrillation, with particular emphasis on available evidence, practical limitations and selected complex clinical scenarios. METHODS: A review based on the analysis of available clinical trials, guidelines, and pharmacological data. RESULTS: Low-molecular-weight heparins are used primarily for bridging therapy and in situations where oral anticoagulation is temporarily contraindicated or not feasible. However, robust evidence supporting the long-term use of LMWHs for stroke prevention in atrial fibrillation remains limited. CONCLUSION: Low-molecular-weight heparins should not be considered standard chronic therapy for atrial fibrillation. Further studies are needed to better define optimal anticoagulation strategies in patients with atrial fibrillation, particularly in complex clinical settings such as active cancer and thrombocytopenia.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: In patients receiving immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs), central nervous system (CNS) infections may mimic or coexist with neurological immune-related adverse events (irAEs). ICI-driven immune dysregulation has been proposed to amplify inflammation against latent pathogens ("immunotherapy infections due to dysregulated immunity", ITI-DI), but this remains a hypothesis-generating framework rather than a validated diagnosis. CASE PRESENTATION: A 54-year-old man with stage IIIC lung adenocarcinoma developed a herpes zoster eruption and lumbosacral pain 7 days after the first infusion of pembrolizumab-containing chemoimmunotherapy, followed by rapidly progressive flaccid paraplegia, urinary incontinence, and declining consciousness. Intravenous acyclovir was not initiated until 20 days after rash onset. The first cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) sample was xanthochromic and coagulated spontaneously in the collection tube (Froin-like CSF), precluding protein measurement. A second lumbar puncture showed mild pleocytosis (8 cells/ μ  L; 70% neutrophils) and undetectable glucose; varicella-zoster virus (VZV) DNA was detected in CSF by post-mortem targeted polymerase chain reaction. Spinal Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) showed diffuse meningeal enhancement; follow-up cranial imaging showed acute hydrocephalus. Despite intravenous acyclovir, corticosteroids, and intravenous immunoglobulin, the patient died 43 days after pembrolizumab initiation. CONCLUSION: This case highlights VZV CNS infection as an important diagnostic consideration in ICI-treated patients who develop herpes zoster and neurological symptoms, because infection may mimic or coexist with a neurological irAE. The temporal relationship with pembrolizumab raises, but does not establish, the possibility that PD-1 blockade modified the inflammatory response. Prompt virological testing and adequately dosed antiviral therapy are central to management; the role of adjunctive immunomodulation remains uncertain and should be individualized.
