papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: To assess the trends in the global disease burden of early-onset female tracheal, bronchus, and lung cancer (TBL) from 1990 to 2021. METHODS: The estimates of age-standardized incidence rate (ASIR), age-standardized death rate (ASDR), age-standardized disability-adjusted life years (DALY) rate, and estimated annual percentage change (EAPC) were extracted, with subsequent analysis of attributable risk factors. RESULTS: From 1990 to 2021, the global disease burden of early-onset female TBL showed a decreasing trend, as reflected by negative EAPCs for the age-standardized DALY rate, ASDR, and ASIR (all EAPCs < 0). Among different socio-demographic index (SDI) regions, low-middle SDI regions saw the fastest growth in age-standardized DALY rates (EAPC = 0.66), ASDR (EAPC = 0.68), and ASIR (EAPC = 0.75). The age distribution showed that the 15-19 and 20-24 age groups in low SDI regions had the highest EAPC (both 1.12). Regional analysis shows that South Asia shows the fastest rising trends in all indicators (DALY rate EAPC = 1.42, ASDR EAPC = 1.44, ASIR EAPC = 1.53). Ambient particulate matter pollution shows the fastest growth (DALY rate EAPC = 1.22, ASDR EAPC = 1.27). CONCLUSIONS: The global disease burden of early-onset female TBL continues to increase in younger populations in low SDI regions. Ambient particulate matter pollution is the primary growth factor. High-burden areas and South Asia face rapidly growing crises.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Multidisciplinary team (MDT) review is essential for individualized treatment planning in lung cancer, where decisions often require integration of staging, pathology, molecular findings, performance status, and multimodal treatment options. However, the effective implementation of MDT review remains constrained by limited specialist availability in resource-limited hospitals and by high patient volume, heavy physician workload, and tight clinical schedules in tertiary care centers. Large language models (LLMs) may support MDT workflows by synthesizing clinical information and generating preliminary treatment recommendations for clinician review. This study compared GPT-5 and Gemini-2.5-Pro with expert MDT recommendations in real-world lung cancer cases and evaluated how information completeness and input format influenced LLM-generated treatment recommendations. METHODS: We conducted a head-to-head evaluation of GPT-5 and Gemini-2.5-Pro for lung-cancer multidisciplinary team decision support. For each of 150 consecutively collected cases, structured vignettes were entered using three information-completeness levels in both natural-language and isomorphic JavaScript Object Notation (JSON) formats. Each model produced a single-sentence recommendation. Outputs were compared with the expert multidisciplinary team plan, which was treated as a clinical reference standard for concordance analysis rather than an objective guideline-only gold standard, using predefined plan-level categories. To better quantify model performance, we applied keyword extraction and semantic matching to normalize both multidisciplinary team recommendations and model outputs into ten treatment categories with subsequent manual review and correction. RESULTS: Stratifying by information level and format, Information Level III produced the best overall performance for Gemini-2.5-Pro under natural-language input, with F1 0.7603, accuracy 0.8647, precision 0.7031, and recall 0.8278. GPT-5 achieved its highest recall under Information Level III with JSON input (recall 0.9132), but this was accompanied by lower precision and F1. Under the same natural-language Information Level III, GPT-5 reached recall 0.8770 with F1 0.6826 and accuracy 0.7967. CONCLUSIONS: Gemini-2.5-Pro show promise as adjuncts to MDT decision-making in lung cancer, offering high agreement with expert plans under controlled conditions. With appropriate clinician oversight, LLM-based tools may help expand access to standardized, high-quality recommendations where specialist availability is limited.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: The creation of synthetic data in healthcare research has emerged as a compelling solution to address challenges related to data privacy, in case of data-sharing and data scarceness for training machine learning models. OBJECTIVE: The current paper aims to provide a critical landscape analysis of synthetic data quality metrics used in healthcare, mapping the state of the field, examining how current fidelity and utility scores often fail to capture weaknesses that appear in specific patient subgroups, and illustrating these blind spots with a lung-cancer case study. We specifically set out to highlight the need for assessing synthetic datasets not only at the aggregate level but also across clinically meaningful subgroups, to ensure reliability and fairness in downstream applications. METHODS: By examining the landscape of synthetic data adoption in healthcare, we highlight the methodological and utility considerations that shape its integration into the research ecosystem. We elucidate how synthetic data can expedite research initiatives, support data-driven decision-making, and facilitate innovative methodologies while safeguarding sensitive patient information. Conversely, while many papers focus solely on the advantages of synthetic data, we aim to highlight also the potential constraints of using synthetic data in a real-world case involving lung cancer patient level data. Our analysis centers on identifying situations where synthetic data might introduce biases or inaccuracies that hinder the generation of meaningful clinical insights. RESULTS: We demonstrate the limitations of using synthetic data in a lung cancer case study, especially when dealing with small subgroups from the original dataset. While high values for fidelity and utility metrics are achieved when considering the entire synthetic dataset, significant discrepancies arise in cross-classification performance when examining subsets. Additionally, visual inspection reveals spurious correlations in the synthetic data that are not present in the real data. CONCLUSION: Global realism scores can give a false sense of security: in our case study, metrics that rate the full dataset as "high quality" overlook errors which appear once we zoom in on specific subgroups. We argue that future work must (i) design subgroup-aware fidelity and utility metrics, (ii) favor conditional generators that model rare strata explicitly, and (iii) report metric panels alongside qualitative, clinical sanity checks. Until such standards mature, our analysis highlights that researchers and regulators should treat synthetic data with caution.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Physical functioning has emerged as a potentially valuable prognostic indicator in patients with nonsmall cell lung cancer (NSCLC). This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to evaluate the prognostic value of objectively measured components of physical functioning on survival outcomes across treatment modalities. METHODS: Medline, Web of Science and Scopus were searched up to May 2025. Eligible studies included adult patients with NSCLC and assessed at least one objectively measured physical functioning indicator in relation to survival outcomes. Indicators were categorised using the International Classification of Functioning, Disability and Health (ICF) framework into "body functions and structures", "activities" and "participation" and studies were stratified into "surgery" and "nonsurgery" groups. Meta-analyses were conducted when data permitted it. RESULTS: 58 studies (19 436 patients) were included. Most assessments were performed before treatment. In the surgical group, only "activities"-based measures were evaluated. A meta-analysis restricted to this group showed that survivors had substantially higher (functional) exercise capacity, measured through cardiopulmonary exercise testing and field tests (standardised mean difference 0.79). In nonsurgical cohorts, prognostic value extended across all ICF domains, with low handgrip strength (hazard ratio (HR) 1.27), low (functional) exercise capacity (HR 2.11) and physical inactivity (HR 2.86) associated with significantly higher mortality. Notably, no studies in surgical cohorts evaluated "body functions" or "participation". Heterogeneity and varying thresholds were noted across studies. CONCLUSIONS: Objectively measured physical functioning is a significant prognostic indicator of survival in NSCLC. Routine assessment could enhance risk stratification and guide personalised care. Future research should address longitudinal changes, standardisation of measures and targeted interventions.

papers.abstract_en: INTRODUCTION: We aimed to systematically review and meta-analyse the effectiveness of interventions in increasing informed choice and participation in lung cancer screening based on low-dose computed tomography (LDCT). METHODS: Five electronic databases, Medline (PubMed version), Embase, Cinahl (Ebsco version), Scopus and Cochrane CENTRAL, were searched for randomised controlled trials, nonrandomised controlled trials and before-after studies published from 2000 until 15 March 2023. A random-effects meta-analysis was conducted to assess the effectiveness of interventions to increase rates of LDCT completion. RESULTS: Out of 3483 studies identified, 14 completed and 21 ongoing studies were included in the review. Shared-decision making (SDM)+navigation (OR 4.34, 95% CI 2.50-7.54) and outreach+navigation (OR 2.20, 95% CI 1.70-2.84) resulted in a higher proportion of LDCT performed compared to the control group. Educational/informational interventions (OR 1.03, 95% CI 0.89-1.19) as well as SDM alone (OR 1.15, 95% CI 0.57-2.32) did not improve LDCT uptake, despite the second improving decisional outcomes in both intervention and control groups. Multicomponent interventions showed significantly higher LDCT uptake (OR 2.64, 95% CI 1.79-3.90), compared to unicomponent interventions (OR 1.00, 95% CI 0.87-1.14). The vast majority of interventions, including those in ongoing trials, are patient-oriented, while community-based, provider-level and system-level interventions remain rare. CONCLUSIONS: Combining high-intensity patient-oriented interventions, such as patient navigation, active outreach and SDM, appears to be the most promising strategy to increase lung cancer screening uptake (low certainty of evidence). However, implementation studies are needed to evaluate interventions targeting both provider and healthcare systems level.

papers.abstract_en: Lung cancer is one of the deadliest forms of cancer, with a significantly high mortality rate. Consequently, early diagnosis is crucial for effective treatment and improved survival outcomes. The cytokeratin 19 fragment, CYFRA 21-1, is a key biomarker for lung cancer detection and is strongly associated with non-small cell lung cancer, particularly squamous cell carcinoma. Accordingly, establishing a sensitive and reliable method for early lung cancer diagnosis based on CYFRA 21-1 detection is critical to improving clinical outcomes. This study introduces a new highly sensitive competitive electrochemical platform capable of detecting CYFRA 21-1using gold nanoparticles (AuNPs)/graphene oxide (GO)/MoO3-MoS2 nanocomposite and gold (Au) nanotags. The sensing platform is constructed by depositing CYFRA 21-1 on a AuNPs/GO/MoO3-MoS2 nanocomposite-modified screen-printed electrode (SPE). In the detection process, the electrode specifically captures unbound anti-CYFRA 21-1 on hydroquinone (HQ)@Au nanotags after competitive binding to the target CYFRA 21-1 in the sample. Our strategy for signal amplification uses the electrochemical response of HQ, anchored to nanotags, as a redox probe. The combination of three nanomaterials enhances electrode reactivity by increasing surface area and conductivity, while maintaining sufficient CYFRA 21-1 bioactivity due to the materials' biocompatibility. Quantitative analysis is achieved by the signal-off HQ peak current, which is inversely proportional to CYFRA 21-1 concentration, with two linear ranges of 0.010-5.0 and 5.0-25 ng mL-1 on a logarithmic concentration scale and a detection limit of 3.0 pg mL-1. Moreover, the sensor exhibits high specificity, reliable reproducibility, and exceptional stability. Simultaneously, the proposed competitive immunosensor can effectively detect CYFRA 21-1 in human serum samples, demonstrating good recovery. The implementation of this electrochemical biosensor offers an opportunity to develop an accurate, cost-effective, and user-friendly diagnostic tool for detecting this type of cancer.

papers.abstract_en: We investigated whether carbon nanoparticles (CNPs), a shared core component of coal dust, ambient PM2.5, and tobacco smoke, drive non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) progression. In an experimental mouse model of CNP‑induced pulmonary fibrosis (intranasal instillation, 200 µg/kg every other day for 90 days), we used transcriptomic screening to identify aryl hydrocarbon receptor nuclear translocator 2 (ARNT2) as a key upregulated transcription factor. In an ectopic xenograft model (nude mice pre‑exposed to 15 µg/kg CNPs for 1 week, subsequently inoculated with A549/A427 cells with or without ARNT2 silencing, with CNP administration continued for a total of 40 days), CNP exposure increased tumor volume at day 36 (A549, 194 ± 17-308 ± 22 mm³; A427, 245 ± 31-417 ± 42 mm³), proliferation (Ki‑67/PCNA: A549, 2.93‑/3.33-fold; A427, 1.94‑/3.55-fold), and levels of epithelial-mesenchymal transition markers (N‑cadherin/Vimentin: A549, 1.61‑/3.17-fold; A427, 2.44‑/1.98-fold), while ARNT2 knockdown reversed these effects. In vitro, CNP treatment (2 µg/mL, 48 h) enhanced proliferation (A549, 2.01‑fold; A427, 1.43-fold), migration (A549, 1.83‑fold; A427, 3.61‑fold), invasion (A549, 2.50‑fold; A427, 2.40‑fold), levels of stemness markers (CD133/SOX2/Oct4: A549, 2.38-/1.93-/2.02-fold; A427, 2.44-/1.44-/1.60-fold), and concentrations of inflammatory cytokines (TNF‑α/IL‑1β/IL‑6: A549, 5.39‑/6.41-/13.70-fold; A427, 3.59‑/10.02-/9.66-fold), reduced apoptosis (A549, 0.47‑fold; A427, 0.36-fold) and senescence (A549, 0.61-fold; A427, 0.37-fold), and increased reactive oxygen species levels (A549, 2.32‑fold; A427, 2.01‑fold); all these changes were attenuated by ARNT2 silencing. Transcriptomic and bioinformatic analyses identified ADP-ribosylation factor-like protein 14 (ARL14) as a downstream effector of ARNT2; ARL14 overexpression in ARNT2‑silenced cells restored proliferation and invasion and reduced apoptosis. Overall, experimental CNP exposure promotes NSCLC progression in an ARNT2-dependent manner, with ARL14 as a downstream mediator, which suggests potential targets for intervention in particulate-associated lung cancer.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Climate mitigation can deliver substantial air quality co-benefits, yet these remain poorly quantified across pathways ranging from sufficiency-to technology-driven transitions. This study compares four French energy-transition scenarios for 2030 and 2050 against a 2019 baseline under fixed meteorology, evaluating annual PM2.5 and NO2 concentration changes and health and economic co-benefits. METHODS: PM2.5 and NO2 concentrations for 2030 and 2050 were estimated with the CHIMERE chemistry-transport model using scenario-specific emission projections. Health impacts relative to 2019 were assessed via disease-specific lag assumptions, covering yearly premature mortality, morbidity, DALYs, and economic benefits across nine cardiometabolic and respiratory outcomes (hypertension, lung cancer, acute myocardial infarction, stroke, COPD, type-2 diabetes, respiratory infections, asthma in children and adults). FINDINGS: Annual population-weighted exposure in continental France is projected to fall by 24% (PM2.5) and 45% (NO2) by 2030, and by 40% (PM2.5) and 75% (NO2) by 2050, relative to 2019 consistently under all four 2050 transition scenarios. Health gains, assessed over each period under delayed-impact assumptions, were substantial and broadly consistent across the four scenarios. Annual avoided premature deaths are projected to reach 8,800-9,300 (PM2.5) and 11,000-12,800 (NO2) by 2030, rising to 21,300-22,100 (PM2.5) and 24,500-26,200 (NO2) by 2050. Avoided morbidity cases reached nearly 40,000 (PM2.5) and 15,000 (NO2) by 2030 to 68,000 (PM2.5) and 20,300 (NO2) by 2050, with DALYs averted increasing from nearly 150,000 in 2030 to 230,000 by 2050 across the pollutants. By 2050, direct lifetime medical cost savings reached approximately €780-810 (S4-S1) million/year for PM2.5 and were markedly smaller for NO2, at approximately €60-64 million/year (S4-S1). Annual intangible cost savings (discounted to present value) totalled approximately €19-20 billion for PM2.5 and €17-18 billion for NO2 across S1-S4. CONCLUSION: Net-Zero transition can deliver substantial health and economic co-benefits across diverse policy pathways. These findings support integrating co-benefits into climate policy frameworks to strengthen the evidence base for ambitious mitigation action.

papers.abstract_en: Lung cancer remains a leading cause of cancer mortality. We developed a dual-targeting nanocomposite FU@TPP/BSA@MnO/UA that induces mitochondrial dysfunction and activates the cGAS-STING pathway. The nanocomposite features a BSA-Mn2 + core, a FU@TPP shell for sequential, dual-stage targeting-first recognizing P-selectin on the tumor vascular endothelium, followed by triphenylphosphine (TPP)-directed mitochondrial localization-and encapsulated ursolic acid (UA). Mechanistically, FU@TPP/BSA@MnO/UA internalizes into lung cancer cells, causing mitochondrial swelling, membrane potential loss, elevated mtROS, and an increased Bax/Bcl-2 ratio. These events trigger autophagic flux and mtDNA release into the cytoplasm, activating the cGAS-STING pathway, which leads to nuclear translocation of IRF3 and p65, upregulation of cGAS/STING, and production of IFN-γ, TNF-α, IL-1β, and IL-6. In a murine LLC xenograft model, the nanocomposite significantly suppresses tumor growth, promotes intratumoral CD8⁺ T cell infiltration, and enhances dendritic cell maturation. Notably, combination with the PD-1 inhibitor sintilimab produces synergistic antitumor efficacy without observable systemic toxicity. Collectively, FU@TPP/BSA@MnO/UA bridges mitochondrial disruption with innate immune activation, offering a promising dual-mechanism strategy for lung cancer treatment and checkpoint immunotherapy enhancement.

papers.abstract_en: B7-H3 is widely expressed in multiple solid tumors but shows minimal expression in normal tissues, making it an ideal target for molecular imaging; however, its systematic investigation remains limited. In this study, we utilized the clinically investigated B7-H3-targeted antibody-drug conjugate (ADC) HS-20093 to develop and evaluate a novel immuno-positron emission tomography (immuno-PET) tracer, [89Zr]Zr-DFO-HS-20093, for accurate imaging of B7-H3 expression in lung cancer and triple-negative breast cancer models. [89Zr]Zr-DFO-HS-20093 was synthesized with high radiochemical purity (98.2 ± 0.6%). Cellular uptake assays revealed significantly higher tracer uptake in A549 cells than in 4T1 cells at 1, 2, and 4 h (all P < 0.0001), which was markedly reduced by blocking with excess unlabeled antibody. Immunofluorescence revealed predominant membrane localization of B7-H3 in 4T1 cells, whereas A549 cells exhibited pronounced intracellular distribution, suggesting enhanced internalization. In tumor-bearing mice, [89Zr]Zr-DFO-HS-20093 positron emission tomography (PET)/CT enabled clear tumor visualization, with peak uptake at 24 h post-injection in both A549 and 4T1 xenografts (9.63 ± 1.97 and 7.15 ± 3.14 μCi/mL, respectively), supporting its potential for tumor imaging. Ex vivo biodistribution data corroborated the PET findings, showing significantly higher tracer uptake in A549 tumors (5.01 ± 1.19 % ID/g) than in blocked tumors (2.89 ± 0.43 % ID/g) and 4T1 tumors (1.89 ± 0.47 % ID/g) (P = 0.034 and P = 0.003, respectively). Immunohistochemical analysis of A549 xenografts showed strong B7-H3 expression (3+), whereas 4T1 tumors exhibited lower expression levels (1-2+), further confirming that B7-H3 expression patterns were consistent with the imaging results. [89Zr]Zr-DFO-HS-20093 enables sensitive immuno-PET imaging of B7-H3 and reveals tumor-type-dependent differences in B7-H3 expression and intracellular behavior.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Accurate gross tumor volume (GTV) delineation is essential for esophageal cancer radiotherapy, but CT-only automatic delineation remains difficult because of indistinct tumor boundaries. PURPOSE: This study aimed to develop and validate a two-stage dual-prompt framework combining a spatial-mask prior with LLaMA3-encoded clinical-text conditioning for primary esophageal GTV delineation. METHODS: This multicenter study included 857 patients: 500 for development, 125 for internal validation, 50 for ablation analysis, and 182 for external validation. The proposed framework consists of two stages: (1) a CT-based automatic segmentation network generating an initial GTV as a spatial mask prompt, and (2) a refinement network that jointly incorporates spatial mask prompt and LLaMA3-encoded clinical text prompt derived from structured clinical information. Performance was evaluated using overlap, surface distance, and volumetric metrics, and compared with multiple state-of-the-art deep learning models. Ablation and radiomics analyses assessed component contributions and downstream consistency. RESULTS: In internal validation, the framework achieved a DSC of 80.32 ± 6.65%, an HD95 of 11.42 ± 8.90 mm, and an absolute volume difference of 9.99 ± 10.49 mL; all Holm-adjusted p values were <0.001 versus the comparison models. Mean DSCs were 78.60 ± 13.39% and 78.36 ± 15.54% in the external cohorts. Mean DSCs were 78.60 ± 13.39% and 78.36 ± 15.54% in the two external cohorts, respectively. In external cohort A, ContextUNETR showed a lower mean HD95 than the proposed model (10.93 ± 8.03 vs. 13.44 ± 18.90 mm), although the paired difference was not statistically significant after Holm correction (adjusted p = 0.906). Compared with the direct Stage-1 output, the complete framework consistently improved overlap, boundary-distance, and volumetric-agreement metrics across the internal and both external validation cohorts (all adjusted p < 0.001). LLaMA3 encoding improved DSC versus an MLP using the same variables (adjusted p = 0.009), whereas ASSD did not differ significantly. Automatic and manual GTVs showed high radiomic concordance and comparable prognostic performance. CONCLUSION: The framework improved overlap and volumetric agreement for CT-only primary esophageal GTV delineation across multicenter validation cohorts, although boundary-distance performance varied across external cohorts.

papers.abstract_en: To investigate the mechanism of the ethyl acetate extract of Tumor Vine (PT-EAE) in combination with cisplatin (DDP) for the treatment of non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), using network pharmacology prediction and validation through cellular experiments. The chemical components of PT-EAE were identified using Ultra-Performance Liquid Chromatography-Quadrupole-Orbitrap Mass Spectrometry (UPLC-Q-Exactive-Orbitrap-MS). Network pharmacology was employed to predict the potential active components of PT-EAE and their molecular targets affecting NSCLC cell functions. A "PT-EAE-active components-targets-disease" interaction network was constructed. Gene Ontology (GO) functional annotation and Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes (KEGG) pathway enrichment analysis were performed on the potential targets to identify core targets and signaling pathways closely related to the active components of PT-EAE. Subsequently, in A549 cells, the effects of PT-EAE alone, DDP alone, and their combination (PT-EAE & DDP) were evaluated. Cell Counting Kit-8 (CCK-8) assay, wound healing assay, transwell assay, and flow cytometry were used to detect cell proliferation, migration, invasion, and apoptosis, respectively. Finally, western blotting and quantitative reverse transcription polymerase chain reaction (RT-qPCR) were utilized to detect the expression levels and phosphorylation status of the predicted core molecular proteins following treatment with PT-EAE and DDP. PT-EAE inhibited the proliferation, migration, and invasion of A549 cells, while promoting apoptosis. Compared to the DDP monotherapy group, the PT-EAE & DDP combination group reduced the IC50 of DDP for inhibiting A549 cell proliferation. Network pharmacology analysis identified 12 active components in PT-EAE, which were mapped to 124 NSCLC-related targets and multiple key signaling pathways. Among these, EGFR, Src, and PI3K were identified as potential core nodes. At the molecular level, PT-EAE downregulated the protein expression levels of EGFR and Src in A549 cells, as well as the phosphorylation levels of downstream molecules in the Src signaling pathway-PI3K, Akt, and mTOR. It also suppressed the mRNA expression of EGFR, Src, PI3K, Akt, and mTOR. The ethyl acetate extract of Tumor Vine, when combined with cisplatin, shows promising anti-tumor activity through multi-component, multi-target, and multi-pathway actions, with the PI3K/Akt/mTOR signaling pathway likely representing one of its therapeutic routes.

papers.abstract_en: OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the predictive value of a nomogram incorporating ultrasound and clinical features for cervical lymph node metastasis (CLNM) in patients with thyroid cancer. METHODS: A retrospective analysis was conducted on patients pathologically diagnosed with papillary thyroid carcinoma (PTC) between April 2024 and January 2025. Radiomics features were extracted from two-dimensional thyroid ultrasound images, and feature selection was performed using the least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO). Five classifiers were compared, and logistic regression was selected to construct the radiomics model. A clinical-radiomics model integrating the radiomics score and clinical predictors, together with a standalone clinical model, was developed using multivariable logistic regression. Model discrimination, calibration, and clinical utility were evaluated in a held-out internal validation set. RESULTS: Sex, Radscore, age, and thyroid stimulating hormone (TSH) levels were identified as independent predictors of CLNM in patients with PTC. Based on these variables, radiomics, clinical, and clinical radiomics models were constructed; the models achieved area under the curve (AUC) values of 0.735, 0.792, and 0.867, respectively, in the validation set. DeLong's test and decision curve analysis (DCA) demonstrated that the clinical radiomics model outperformed the radiomics model in the validation set, offering a higher net clinical benefit. CONCLUSION: A nomogram integrating ultrasound imaging and clinical data effectively predicts the risk of CLNM in patients with PTC and may assist clinicians in developing individualized treatment strategies.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Current preoperative assessment of meningioma brain invasion (BI) demands imaging analytical frameworks that optimize computational efficiency while capturing multidimensional tumor-pathology correlations. Building upon the inherent advantages of 2.5D MRI in synthesizing multiplanar biological data with manageable processing loads, this study innovatively integrates deep transfer learning (DTL), a technique bridging pretrained network knowledge with target domain adaptation, to systematically identify tumor-invasive biological signatures and develop an optimized predictive system using preoperative contrast-enhanced T1-weighted imaging (CE-T1WI). METHODS: This retrospective study enrolled 674 patients with pathologically confirmed meningiomas, including 53 with BI and 621 without BI. The cohort was stratified into a training set and an independent test set. Tumor regions of interest (ROIs) were delineated on CE-T1WI, and radiomics and DTL features were extracted. Radiomics and DTL features were fused via early fusion, followed by feature selection. Within the training cohort, five-fold cross-validation was performed, with SMOTE applied exclusively to the training portion of each fold; validation folds and the independent test set retained their original class distributions. RESULTS: The effectiveness of the models was compared using the area under the ROC curve (AUC). In the training set, ComM achieved an AUC of 0.977, while in the test set, its AUC reached 0.935. ComM demonstrated the best performance (training set: AUCComM > AUCDTLRM > AUCRadM > AUCClinM > AUCDTLM; test set: AUCComM > AUCDTLRM > AUCRadM > AUCDTLM > AUCClinM), showing excellent preoperative predictive capability for meningioma BI. The Hosmer-Lemeshow test indicated good model fit, and the calibration curve revealed that ComM was closest to the ideal curve. CONCLUSION: ClinM, RadM, DTLM, DTLRM, and ComM based on 2.5D CE-T1WI all exhibited good performance in predicting meningioma BI. The clinical-radiomics-DTL fusion model (ComM) demonstrated the highest efficacy, suggesting that DTL provides additional features correlated with meningioma BI that differ from radiomics features. This model shows potential clinical utility for preoperative prediction; however, further external validation in larger multicenter cohorts is required before clinical implementation.

papers.abstract_en: OBJECTIVE: To investigate tumor vascular habitat parameters based on dynamic susceptibility contrast-enhanced perfusion-weighted imaging (DSC-PWI) for differentiating glioblastoma (GBM) from solitary brain metastasis (SBM). METHODS: In this single-center retrospective study, imaging data from 141 patients with pathologically or clinically confirmed malignant brain tumors (74 GBM, 67 SBM) were analyzed. The hemodynamic tissue signature (HTS) method was used to segment the lesions and construct four tumor vascular habitats: high angiogenic tumor (HAT), low angiogenic tumor (LAT), potentially infiltrated peripheral edema (IPE), and vasogenic peripheral edema (VPE). Pearson correlation analysis was used to quantify the correlations among habitat hemodynamic parameters. Habitat characteristic parameters were calculated, and ROC were plotted to evaluate the diagnostic performance. A nomogram model was constructed using logistic regression. RESULTS: GBM exhibited significantly higher median relative cerebral blood volume (rCBVmedian) and median relative cerebral blood flow (rCBFmedian) than SBM across all four habitat regions (all p < 0.001). In terms of volumetric parameters, the ratio of IPE volume to peritumoral volume (V (IPE)/V (P)) was significantly higher in the GBM group (p < 0.001). Among individual habitat parameters, LAT rCBFmedian showed the best diagnostic performance with an AUC of 0.786 (95% CI: 0.709-0.850). In the GBM group, the perfusion parameters of the IPE and VPE were significantly positively correlated with those of the HAT, whereas no such correlation was found in the SBM group. A nomogram incorporating lesion location, enhancement pattern, and LAT-rCBFmedian yielded an AUC of 0.857 (95% CI: 0.79-0.92) for distinguishing GBM from SBM, with good calibration. CONCLUSION: Tumor vascular habitat parameters based on DSC-PWI demonstrate significant differences between newly diagnosed GBM and SBM, and the nomogram shows certain value in differentiating between the two tumor types.

papers.abstract_en: OBJECTIVE: Accurate early diagnosis of Clinically Significant prostate cancer (csPCa) is crucial for improving patient survival rates. This study aimed to develop and validate an interpretable, confidence-based deep learning model for csPCa classification using biparametric MRI (bpMRI). METHODS: A retrospective analysis was conducted on bpMRI data from 410 patients. A classification model was constructed using the visual geometry group 16-layer (VGG-16) network, incorporating gradient-weighted class activation mapping (Grad-CAM) for visual interpretability, Monte Carlo Dropout (MC-Dropout) for uncertainty estimation, and a rejection mechanism. The model's performance was evaluated using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves and area under the ROC curve (AUC). RESULTS: Across all predictions, the confidence-based model achieved an overall accuracy of 79.3% before rejection. At a confidence threshold of 0.8, 80.8% of predictions were retained, among which the selective accuracy was 94.6%, with 99 false-positive and 2 false-negative predictions. Besides, the model's accuracy outperformed that of a senior radiologist (94.6% vs 90.8%). Qualitative Grad-CAM visualization demonstrated that the classifier frequently assigned high activation to MRI regions considered suspicious for csPCa; however, quantitative spatial agreement with lesion annotations was not assessed. CONCLUSION: This confidence-based model identifies csPCa lesions and provides reliable confidence scores without pixel-level annotations. By rejecting uncertain predictions, it enhances the transparency and safety of clinical decision-making.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Prostate cancer remains one of the most frequently diagnosed malignancies and a leading cause of cancer-related mortality among men globally. Its development is driven by a complex interaction of genetic susceptibility, molecular alterations, hormonal signaling, environmental exposures, and lifestyle-related factors. This systematic review synthesizes current evidence on the etiological mechanisms and evolving therapeutic landscape of prostate cancer. METHODS: A systematic review was conducted according to the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) 2020 guidelines. Literature published between January 2010 and December 2025 was searched in PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science databases. Eligible studies included original research, clinical studies, translational studies, and experimental investigations evaluating prostate cancer etiology, molecular mechanisms, risk factors, biomarkers, or therapeutic interventions. RESULTS: The review included 29 studies encompassing epidemiological cohorts, clinical studies, genomic analyses, tissue-based investigations, and preclinical experimental studies. Evidence demonstrated that prostate cancer etiology involves multiple interconnected pathways, including androgen receptor signaling, DNA repair alterations, genomic instability, chromatin remodeling, metabolic reprogramming, and inflammatory mechanisms. Genetic variants, including single nucleotide polymorphisms and polygenic risk scores, were associated with disease susceptibility, aggressiveness, treatment response, and toxicity outcomes. Therapeutic advances included optimization of androgen deprivation therapy, novel androgen receptor pathway inhibitors, chemotherapy, radiotherapy personalization, bone-targeted therapies, PSMA-directed radioligand therapy, and emerging immunotherapeutic approaches. Biomarker-driven strategies, including genomic classifiers and molecular signatures, showed potential for improving risk stratification and individualized treatment selection. CONCLUSION: Prostate cancer is a biologically heterogeneous disease requiring integrated approaches that combine molecular understanding with clinical decision-making. Recent advances in precision oncology have expanded therapeutic options beyond conventional treatment paradigms, enabling more personalized management strategies. However, further research is required to improve representation of diverse populations, validate biomarkers across different ethnic groups, and optimize the clinical implementation of emerging targeted and immune-based therapies. SYSTEMATIC REVIEW REGISTRATION: https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/, identifier CRD420261435105.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Stereotactic body radiotherapy (SBRT) combined with lenvatinib and tislelizumab has shown potential activity in advanced hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), but early treatment failure (ETF) remains common. We developed an exploratory model to estimate ETF, defined as radiologically confirmed progressive disease (PD) or all-cause death within 6 months after treatment initiation. METHODS: This single-center retrospective study included advanced HCC patients treated with the triple regimen from June 2021 to June 2024. Baseline clinical, imaging, and hematological variables were analyzed. LASSO regression with 10-fold cross-validation was used for feature selection. Restricted cubic splines assessed linearity, and λ.1se was examined as a sensitivity analysis. A multivariable logistic regression model was presented as a nomogram. Discrimination, calibration, and decision curve analysis (DCA) were evaluated, with 1000-resample bootstrap internal validation repeating the modeling pipeline. RESULTS: Among 118 patients, 33 (27.9%) experienced ETF; 28 had radiologically confirmed PD and 5 died without prior documented PD. At λ.min, LASSO selected maximum tumor diameter, Vp4 portal vein tumor thrombosis (PVTT), baseline systemic immune-inflammation index (SII), ALBI score, and log10-transformed alpha-fetoprotein (AFP). Under λ.1se, four predictors were retained, with SII excluded. The final model had an apparent ROC-AUC of 0.903 and an optimism-corrected ROC-AUC of 0.866. Calibration showed acceptable agreement between predicted and observed risks. DCA suggested net benefit over an exploratory threshold range of approximately 0.10-0.50, which should not be interpreted as a validated treatment-switching threshold. CONCLUSION: The nomogram showed promising internal discrimination for estimating 6-month ETF risk in advanced HCC patients receiving SBRT, lenvatinib, and tislelizumab. Given the modest sample size and single-center design, the model remains exploratory and hypothesis-generating. External multicenter validation is required before clinical implementation or use for treatment selection.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Immune-mediated liver injury caused by checkpoint inhibitors (ILICI) differs from chemotherapy- or targeted drug-related hepatotoxicity in pathogenesis and management. Biomarkers to distinguish ILICI from other anticancer agent-induced liver injuries are lacking. We compared the clinicopathological features, treatments, and outcomes of ILICI versus other anticancer agent-related liver injuries to identify distinguishing biomarkers. METHODS: We retrospectively included patients with liver injury during anticancer therapy at Fujian Cancer Hospital between June 2022 and November 2024. Cases were classified as ILICI or non-ILICI using the Common Terminology Criteria for Adverse Events v5.0 and the Roussel Uclaf Causality Assessment Method. RESULTS: Sixty-seven patients were enrolled, including 30 ILICI and 37 non-ILICI. ILICI was associated with more high-grade liver injury than non-ILICI (P = 0.001), with similar latency, recovery time, and prognosis. Corticosteroids were administered in 70% of ILICI vs. 5.4% of non-ILICI patients (P < 0.001). Among 29 liver biopsies (19 ILICI, 10 non-ILICI), ILICI showed a higher focal necrosis score (P = 0.031) and programmed death-ligand 1 (PD-L1) expression in liver sinusoidal endothelial cells (LSECs), lymphocytes, and Kupffer cells (KCs) (P = 0.007). Receiver operating characteristic analysis showed that a PD-L1 positivity cutoff of >30% in LSECs, lymphocytes, and KCs discriminated ILICI with an AUC of 0.811 (95%CI: 0.641-0.980). Sensitivity analyses and Firth penalized logistic regression confirmed that this finding remained robust after adjustment for confounders including pre-biopsy corticosteroid use and inactive HBV carrier status. CONCLUSIONS: ILICI was associated with more severe hepatic inflammatory necrosis and a greater need for immunosuppressive therapy than non-ILICI. The PD-L1 positivity rate >30% in LSECs, lymphocytes, and KCs may serve as a potential diagnostic biomarker for ILICI.

papers.abstract_en: OBJECTIVE: Four-dimensional computed tomography (4D-CT)-guided functional-avoidance radiotherapy reduces radiation pneumonitis, but the lack of patient selection criteria limits its adoption. This study aimed to identify clinical predictors of lung ventilation heterogeneity and determine which patients derive the greatest dosimetric benefit from functional-avoidance planning. METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 274 lung cancer patients. 4D-CT ventilation imaging was generated via deformable registration and a density-change algorithm, and the coefficient of variation (CoV) across six lung zones quantified heterogeneity. Clinical factors were assessed using Mann-Whitney U, Spearman, and multivariable logistic regression for three ventilation outcomes. Thirty-two patients were selected from CoV quartiles and re-planned with functional-avoidance plans; dosimetric parameters were compared using the Wilcoxon signed-rank test, with False Discovery Rate (FDR) correction applied to address multiple comparisons. RESULTS: Univariate analysis showed chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) and airway obstruction reduced bilateral mean ventilation, while central tumors impaired ipsilateral ventilation. Higher CoV was observed in stage III-IV versus I-II, central versus peripheral tumors, and patients with airway obstruction. Multivariable analysis identified airway obstruction as an independent predictor of elevated CoV (adjusted OR = 2.914, 95% CI: 1.315-6.454, P<0.05). Central location and advanced stage showed borderline significance, while COPD trended toward lower CoV. Dosimetrically, functional-avoidance plans reduced functional lung metrics in a heterogeneity-dependent manner. After FDR correction, key metrics (fMLD, fV10, fV20, fV30) remained significant in Group 1 (highest CoV; Q = 0.040-0.049), while significance diminished in lower CoV groups. Leave-one-out (LOO) sensitivity analysis confirmed fMLD and fV20 as robust endpoints. Furthermore, beam arrangement modifications were most frequent in Group 1 (5/8 patients) and absent in Group 4 (0/8), reflecting clinical optimization needs rather than confounding. CONCLUSIONS: Ventilation heterogeneity is driven by tumor burden and airway patency. Patients with advanced stage, central tumors, or airway obstruction exhibit the strongest heterogeneity and may represent appropriate candidates for functional-avoidance radiotherapy in future prospective trials. However, as this replanning study lacked clinical follow-up for radiation pneumonitis, these findings reflect dosimetric rather than confirmed clinical patient-level benefit. Notably, CoV quartiles were derived from internal median splits within this cohort and require external validation. This study provides a dosimetric basis for hypothesis-generating patient selection.

papers.abstract_en: Protein arginine methyltransferases (PRMTs) are promising anti-cancer targets, but their tumorigenic mechanisms remain incompletely understood. Here, we show that arginine methylation drives global 3'UTR shortening, thereby promoting oncogenic short isoforms. Inhibition of asymmetric dimethylation reverses this shift, with combined inhibition of asymmetric and symmetric dimethylation (DMAi) producing an even greater effect across human cancer cell lines, patient-derived organoids, and activated murine T cells, while also counteracting the shortening induced by reduced CFIm25 expression. Arginine methylation promotes PCF11 association with the cleavage and polyadenylation machinery, enabling efficient processing of weak proximal poly(A) sites within transcripts characterized by high GC content, large distances between alternative poly(A) sites, and a position-dependent sequence code. These findings establish physiologic roles of PRMTs in promoting 3'UTR shortening, which could be exploited for patient stratification of PRMT-targeting therapies in oncology and immune-related diseases.

papers.abstract_en: A 72-year-old woman with a history of resected lung adenocarcinoma presented with a pancreatic mass and multiple bilateral renal masses. Endoscopic ultrasound-guided tissue acquisition of the pancreatic lesion showed neuroendocrine morphology, synaptophysin positivity, focal chromogranin A positivity, and a Ki-67 labeling index of 2%, leading to an initial diagnosis of pancreatic neuroendocrine tumor grade 1. Renal biopsy also demonstrated neuroendocrine differentiation with a Ki-67 labeling index of 17%. However, the pancreatic lesion was hypovascular and poorly defined, and the multifocal bilateral renal involvement was atypical for a low-grade pancreatic neuroendocrine tumor. Re-evaluation of the resected lung specimen revealed a focal neuroendocrine component showing large cell neuroendocrine carcinoma-like features, although the strict diagnostic criteria for such a diagnosis were not fully met. Genomic analysis identified a KRAS G12V mutation shared by the renal and lung tumors, supporting the interpretation that the renal lesions represented metastatic recurrence of the previously resected lung tumor. Direct molecular confirmation was unavailable for the pancreatic lesion because of insufficient residual endoscopic ultrasound-guided tissue acquisition material; therefore, its origin remained diagnostically uncertain. Nevertheless, based on the overall clinicopathological context, the pancreatic lesion was interpreted as an accompanying neuroendocrine tumor-like lesion most consistent with metastatic recurrence. This case highlights the importance of integrating clinical history, imaging features, disease distribution, archival pathology, and molecular findings when evaluating neuroendocrine tumor-like lesions in patients with a prior malignancy.

papers.abstract_en: OBJECTIVE: Young adults with cancer (YACs) experience psychological and psychosocial challenges related to cancer. In this qualitative study, we identified self-conscious emotions of guilt, shame and pride associated with psychosocial challenges in a sample of recent cancer survivors. We aim to inform the adaptation of psychotherapy interventions to support psychological adjustment to cancer through the regulation of self-conscious emotions. METHODS: We recruited 35 YACs (English-speaking, age 18-39, completed treatment 2-5 years prior) through YA cancer advocacy organizations. Participants completed a virtual semi-structured interview focused on personal identity, self-conscious emotions, and close relationships. We coded and analyzed the data using reflexive thematic analysis guided by the theory of self-conscious emotions and a narrative identity framework. RESULTS: Participants endorsed guilt, shame, and pride related to cancer and described the motivational impact of each on their relationships. Themes included: (1) Guilt, encompassing imposter syndrome, survivors' guilt, and guilt for perceived burden on caregivers, financial toxicity, disrupted milestones, and self-care. Guilt undermined relational closeness through the perception of "falling behind" peers and coping through social withdrawal. (2) Shame, centering on worsened body image and loss of physical function, was exacerbated by "body positivity" pressures. Effects of shame included reluctance toward intimacy and disclosure. (3) Pride emerged as a key driver in rebuilding personal identity, arising from awareness of resilience, recommitment to goals, and expansion of survivors' personal identity through empathy and advocacy. CONCLUSIONS: Based on these findings, we offer adaptations of psychotherapy tools to address guilt and shame, and to optimize pride.

papers.abstract_en: Lung cancer remains the leading cause of cancer-related mortality worldwide. Although substantial progress has been made in defining the genetic, epigenetic, and molecular drivers of this heterogeneous disease, metabolic reprogramming has only recently emerged as a major determinant of tumour progression and therapeutic response. Cumulative evidence demonstrates that rather than relying on a single nutrient source or pathway, cancer cells integrate glucose and glutamine, fatty acid and one-carbon metabolism, as well as nucleotide biosynthesis, and redox-supporting circuits in a highly context-dependent manner. These programs vary across histological and molecular subtypes, reflecting the influence of lineage identity and oncogenic state on metabolic organisation. In both non-small cell lung cancer and small cell lung cancer, subtype-specific constraints shape distinct metabolic states, yet a common feature is the ability to rapidly shift between alternative nutrients and biosynthetic routes. This adaptability supports continued growth under nutrient limitation, maintains redox homeostasis, and contributes to resistance against conventional and targeted therapies. By summarising current mechanistic evidence, this review presents lung cancer metabolism as an integrated and adaptable system rather than a collection of isolated pathways, and identifies metabolic dependencies that may be leveraged for therapeutic intervention.

papers.abstract_en: Although climate change represents one of the greatest public health challenges of our time, its impacts on patients with interstitial lung disease (ILD) remain unclear. This Personal View synthesises the evidence surrounding established, emerging, and postulated climate change health effects on patients with ILD, who are especially vulnerable to disease due to older age, reduced lung function, and sensitivity to inhaled exposures. Established risk factors for ILD such as air pollution might worsen with climate change, whereas other exposures such as extreme heat, viral illnesses, residential water intrusion, pollen, natural disasters, and desertification could pose novel threats to this population. Knowledge gaps exist across multiple domains, including wildfire smoke effects, the effects of climate on occupational ILD, and disaster preparedness. The incorporation of multiple research modalities, including patient-centred approaches, is crucial to address these gaps. Clinicians, scientists, and professional societies can lead climate-health research, the adoption of mitigation and adaptation strategies, and drive global policy actions to address this growing challenge.

papers.abstract_en: INTRODUCTION: Achalasia is associated with an increased risk of esophageal squamous cell carcinoma even after definitive surgical treatment. Heller-Dor surgery is an established surgical treatment for achalasia; however, marked esophageal dilatation may persist despite successful symptom control and pose technical challenges during subsequent esophagectomy. CASE PRESENTATION: A 73-year-old man with a history of Heller-Dor surgery for achalasia and prior endoscopic submucosal dissection (ESD) for esophageal squamous cell carcinoma developed a metachronous lesion at a different esophageal site. Histopathological examination after ESD demonstrated deep submucosal and vascular invasion, warranting additional curative treatment. Preoperative imaging showed predominant upper thoracic esophageal dilatation with a maximum diameter of 56 mm, whereas gastric deformity was minimal. The patient underwent prone-position video-assisted thoracoscopic subtotal esophagectomy with 3-field lymphadenectomy and retrosternal gastric conduit reconstruction. Intraoperatively, venous engorgement required meticulous dissection, while marked upper thoracic esophageal dilatation restricted the operative workspace around the left recurrent laryngeal nerve. An internal organ retractor provided stable esophageal traction with flexible repositioning of the traction point, facilitating adequate exposure. Despite intra-abdominal adhesions from the previous surgery, gastric conduit reconstruction was successfully completed as anticipated from the preoperative assessment of gastric anatomy. Final histopathological examination revealed no residual carcinoma or lymph node metastasis. The postoperative course was uneventful, and the patient remained recurrence-free at 2 years. CONCLUSIONS: Long-term endoscopic surveillance remains important after surgical treatment for achalasia. In patients requiring subsequent esophagectomy, preoperative assessment of the degree and distribution of esophageal dilatation may help anticipate technical difficulty, while appropriate repositionable traction may facilitate operative exposure. Careful assessment of gastric anatomy may also help determine the feasibility of gastric conduit reconstruction after Heller-Dor surgery.

papers.authors: Lin J, Pang Z, Jiang Z, Li F

papers.authors_conclusion: 在此基础上，靶向脂质代谢重编程已成为NSCLC治疗有前景的新方向；本文梳理NSCLC脂质代谢改变、驱动基因突变改变脂质代谢的机制，并提供当前阶段靶向关键脂质代谢通路的可能治疗策略，旨在为开发针对NSCLC特定基因突变亚型的新疗法提供理论依据与前景。

papers.abstract_en: Non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) is among the leading causes of cancer-related deaths worldwide. Previous treatment regimens often have limited efficacy due to drug resistance and recurrence. Metabolic reprogramming participates in the initiation and progression of NSCLC, with prominent changes in lipid metabolism. Mutations in specific driver genes directly remodel lipid metabolic reprogramming in NSCLC by rewiring lipid synthesis, uptake, and catabolism, which confers cancer cells with enhanced proliferative and metastatic capacity. On this basis, targeted lipid metabolism reprogramming has become a promising new direction for the treatment of NSCLC. In this review, we examined the alterations in lipid metabolism in NSCLC, explored the mechanisms by which driver gene mutations change lipid metabolism in NSCLC, and provided possible therapeutic strategies targeting key lipid metabolism pathways at the current stage, aiming to offer a theoretical basis and prospects for the development of novel therapies targeting specific gene mutation subtypes of NSCLC.

papers.abstract_en: Protein delivery nanosystems must balance stable loading, barrier navigation, and targeted, controlled release. Herein, a pH/ROS dual-responsive nanogel (PRNG) was constructed by forming dynamic boronic ester crosslinkers between PEGylated hyaluronic acid bearing diethylenetriamine-grafted-catechol groups (PEG-HA-Dien-CA) and hyaluronic acid-conjugated phenylboronic acid (HA-PBA) for cytoplasmic cytochrome c (CC) delivery. This pioneering conceptual design not only facilitates the formation of stable nanocarriers with a high CC loading capacity, but also presents a distinctive mechanism for dual-responsive protein release. Confocal imaging confirmed that CC-loaded PRNG was efficiently internalized by A549 cells through CD44-dependent endocytosis, rapidly released from the endo/lysosomal compartments, and effectively delivered CC into the cytoplasm, and subsequently induced cell apoptosis in the acidic tumor microenvironment (TME) rich in H2O2. In mice bearing human lung tumors, CC-loaded PRNGs preferentially accumulate at tumor sites and effectively inhibit growth with minimal systemic toxicity, demonstrating a versatile nanoplatform for lung cancer therapy.

papers.abstract_en: Selective targeting of ULK1 represents a promising approach to overcome autophagy-mediated resistance in KRAS-driven cancers. However, achieving selectivity over the closely related ULK2 isoform with ATP-competitive inhibitors remains challenging due to the high sequence homology within their kinase domains. Here, we describe the design, synthesis, and structure-degradation relationship studies of two cereblon-recruiting ULK1 degraders, MR-9034 and MR-9036. Structure-guided optimization led to the discovery of MR-9036 as a potent and selective ULK1 PROTAC that degrades ULK1 without affecting ULK2 or IMiD neo-substrates. Cellular and biophysical studies confirm ternary complex formation and proteasome-dependent degradation. Compared with the clinical ULK1/2 inhibitor DCC-3116, MR-9036 produces sustained autophagy suppression following compound washout. In KRASG12C-mutant NSCLC models, ULK1 degradation enhances the antiproliferative activity of sotorasib. Pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamic (PK/PD) studies in mice support in vivo feasibility. These findings establish selective ULK1 degradation as a chemical strategy to interrogate ULK1 biology and enhance therapeutic response in KRAS-driven cancers.

papers.abstract_en: Ecto-5-nucleotidase (CD73), a rate-limiting enzyme in the adenosine pathway, plays a crucial role in mediating tumor immunosuppression and has emerged as an attractive target for cancer immunotherapy. A series of aryl alkyl ether-based CD73 inhibitors were designed and synthesized. Compound LB10 stood out as the most promising inhibitor from this series, with IC50 values of 8.1 nM and 2.7 nM in biochemical and cell-based assays, respectively. This compound was confirmed to be a competitive inhibitor by enzyme kinetic and co-crystallization experiments. The compound exhibited no apparent cytotoxicity and a favorable pharmacokinetic profile. In a syngeneic Lewis lung carcinoma mouse model, oral administration of LB10 significantly inhibited tumor growth and synergized with paclitaxel or an anti-PD-1 antibody via immune activation. Collectively, these results establish LB10 as a promising CD73 inhibitor warranting further development.

papers.abstract_en: GFPT1, the rate-limiting enzyme of the hexosamine biosynthesis pathway, promotes various cancers but its role in esophageal cancer is unclear. GFPT1 expression was assessed by public datasets, western blotting, and IHC. GFPT1-silenced cells were established via siRNA. Proliferation, migration, invasion, apoptosis, ER stress, and autophagy markers were evaluated by CCK-8, colony formation, Transwell, wound healing, flow cytometry, western blotting, and LC3 immunofluorescence. In addition, rescue experiments were performed using the ER stress inhibitor 4-PBA in GFPT1-knockdown cells, and O-GlcNAcylation levels were examined by western blot. GFPT1 was highly expressed in esophageal cancer tissues. Knockdown of GFPT1 suppressed proliferation, invasion, and migration, while enhancing apoptosis. GFPT1 depletion upregulated ER stress markers (GRP78, GRP94, p-PERK, p-eIF2α) and autophagy-related changes (increased LC3-II/LC3-I ratio, ATG5, ATG7, and reduced p62), and reduced overall O-GlcNAcylation. Importantly, treatment with 4-PBA significantly reversed the GFPT1 knockdown-induced suppression of proliferation, migration, and invasion, and rescued the alterations in ER stress markers, indicating that the phenotypic effects are causally mediated, at least in part, through the ER stress pathway. GFPT1 knockdown impedes esophageal cancer progression by reducing aggressive phenotypes and promoting apoptosis, potentially via ER stress and autophagy activation.

papers.title_zh: 膳食炎症指数与前列腺癌发病风险：大型前瞻性队列中未调整的负相关在年龄校正后消失，未见独立关联
papers.title_en: Dietary inflammatory index and incident prostate cancer.
papers.authors: Li S, Chen Y, Zhou L, Wu T, Xu J, Yin M, Long H, Cao L et al.
papers.affiliation_highlight: Department of Urology, The Affiliated Lihuili Hospital of Ningbo University, Ningbo, Zhejiang, China.
papers.results: 未调整分析：DII 每增加 1 单位 HR 0.951（95%CI 0.927-0.977）。完全调整年龄及其他协变量后：HR 0.986（95%CI 0.956-1.018；P=0.389）；Q4 vs Q1 HR 0.928（95%CI 0.788-1.093；P for trend=0.426）。次要 logistic 分析：每增加 1 单位 OR 0.982（95%CI 0.950-1.015；P=0.275）。DII 与修订版 18 营养素 MAR 呈负相关（Pearson r=-0.694；Spearman ρ=-0.756），但在年龄调整联合模型中两指数均与前列腺癌无关。
papers.authors_conclusion: 未调整分析中 DII 与前列腺癌的表面负相关主要由不同 DII 类别间的年龄差异解释；调整年龄及其他协变量后，logistic 与时间-事件分析均不支持独立关联，这些发现强调前列腺癌流行病学中严格年龄控制的必要性，不应作因果解读。
papers.ai_note: 未调整与调整后效应量方向一致但幅度显著衰减，提示残余/未测混杂（尤其年龄以外的生活行为因素）无法完全排除；DII 与 MAR 高度相关（|r|≈0.7），提示暴露存在共线性，联合模型结果解释受限；仅基于 Oxford WebQ 单次膳食评估，暴露错分可能为无差异性并趋向零；研究对象为特定志愿队列（可能健康志愿者偏倚），外推性受限；本文非胸部肿瘤研究，与本领域临床决策关联极弱。

pico.p: 基线无前列腺癌的男性 30,972 例；中位随访 13.8 年（IQR 13.5-14.2；406,058 人年）；发生前列腺癌 1,546 例
pico.ic: 暴露为膳食炎症指数 DII（由 Oxford WebQ 评估的 27 种膳食成分构建），按连续每增加 1 单位及 Q4 vs Q1 比较；无干预措施，非随机对照

papers.reason: 为‘膳食炎症负荷’类假设提供方法学较严谨的大样本阴性证据，可作为同类营养-炎症暴露队列研究的对照基线与样本量/随访参数参考，并提示年龄校正对结果的决定性影响；对胸外科/胸部肿瘤的临床判断无直接影响。
papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: The Dietary Inflammatory Index (DII) quantifies the inflammatory potential of diet. Evidence linking DII to prostate cancer remains limited and inconsistent. We evaluated the prospective association between DII and incident prostate cancer in a large population-based cohort. METHODS: We included 30,972 men who were free of prostate cancer at baseline. The DII was derived from 27 dietary components assessed by the Oxford WebQ. Incident prostate cancer was identified from linked cancer-registry records (ICD-10 C61). Cox regression was the primary analysis, with age included in all adjusted models; logistic regression was secondary. Lag, additional-covariate, and age-stratified Cox models assessed sensitivity. Mediation and Mean Adequacy Ratio (MAR) analyses were exploratory. RESULTS: During a median follow-up of 13.8 years (IQR 13.5-14.2; 406,058 person-years), 1,546 participants developed incident prostate cancer. The unadjusted inverse association (HR per 1-unit DII increase 0.951, 95% CI 0.927-0.977) was attenuated after adjustment for age and other covariates (fully adjusted HR 0.986, 95% CI 0.956-1.018; P = 0.389; Q4 vs Q1 HR 0.928, 95% CI 0.788-1.093; P for trend = 0.426). The secondary logistic analysis was likewise null (OR per 1-unit increase 0.982, 95% CI 0.950-1.015; P = 0.275). Age-adjusted lag analyses and exploratory CRP/NLR mediation analyses did not materially alter this interpretation. DII was inversely correlated with the revised 18-nutrient MAR (Pearson r = -0.694; Spearman ρ = -0.756), but neither index was associated with prostate cancer in the age-adjusted joint model. CONCLUSIONS: An apparent inverse DII-prostate cancer association in unadjusted analyses was explained largely by age differences across DII categories. After adjustment for age and other covariates, neither logistic nor time-to-event analyses supported an independent association. These findings underscore the importance of rigorous age control in prostate cancer epidemiology and should not be interpreted causally.

papers.authors: Yang J, Li L, Pan Y, Hou W, Wang X, Li Z, Wang W, Sun Y et al.

papers.authors_conclusion: SAN 是通过 Hippo 介导的焦亡通路与肿瘤免疫双重调控发挥抗肿瘤作用的候选治疗药物，为其在 LUAD 的潜在临床应用提供机制基础。

pico.ic: 血根碱（SAN）处理 vs 对照；并采用 YAP 过表达进行通路回补验证

papers.reason: 提供 LUAD 中 Hippo-YAP 通路、细胞焦亡与免疫微环境（CD8+ T 细胞、肌纤维母细胞性 CAF）相互关联的机制假设，可作为转化研究背景与靶点筛选线索引用，但不构成改变当前临床决策的证据。
papers.abstract_en: Sanguinarine (SAN), a natural alkaloid derived from Papaveraceae plants, is an active component in traditional Chinese medicines. SAN exerts inhibitory effects on tumor cells, but research on its effects on lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) and the underlying mechanisms remains limited. The Hippo signaling pathway is commonly downregulated in LUAD, making it a key target for therapeutic intervention. Our study reveals that SAN significantly inhibits LUAD. Mechanistically, SAN bound to Large Tumor Suppressor 1 (LATS1) and promoted its phosphorylation, thereby activating the Hippo pathway and pyroptosis in LUAD. Notably, YAP overexpression inhibited pyroptosis and weakened the antitumor effect of SAN, further confirming that SAN exerts its antitumor effects by regulating the Hippo-YAP axis. Findings from both in vivo experiments and single-cell RNA sequencing consistently show that SAN remodels the tumor immune microenvironment and inhibits tumor growth. Specifically, we observed significant changes in the tumor microenvironment, including increased CD8+ T cell infiltration and a notably reduced number of myofibroblastic cancer-associated fibroblasts. Collectively, our findings establish SAN as a candidate therapeutic agent that exerts antitumor effects through dual modulation of the Hippo-mediated pyroptosis pathway and tumor immunity, providing a mechanistic basis for its potential clinical application in LUAD.

papers.title_en: FTO-mediated demethylation of PRKCB mRNA activates NF-κB to trigger alveolar fibrin deposition in ARDS.
papers.authors: Chen X, Liu Y, Mu S, Chen T, Yuan J, Xiao C, Dong Q, Li Q et al.
papers.affiliation_highlight: Department of Critical Care Medicine, The Affiliated Hospital of Guizhou Medical University, Guiyang, China.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Acute Respiratory Distress Syndrome (ARDS) is characterized by alveolar fibrin deposition, driven by dysregulated hypercoagulation and impaired fibrinolysis. Although alveolar epithelial type II (AEC II) cells contribute to this imbalance by overexpressing Tissue Factor (TF) and Plasminogen Activator Inhibitor-1 (PAI-1), the upstream regulatory mechanisms, particularly at the epitranscriptomic level, remain unclear. The potential role of the N6-methyladenosine (m6A) RNA demethylase FTO in ARDS pathogenesis is unexplored. METHODS: In this study, we employed lipopolysaccharide (LPS)-induced rat ARDS models and LPS-stimulated AEC II cells as primary experimental systems to investigate the underlying mechanisms. Multi-omics profiling, combining methylated RNA immunoprecipitation sequencing (MeRIP-seq) and RNA sequencing (RNA-seq), was performed. Gain and loss-of-function studies were conducted using lentiviral vectors both in vitro and in vivo. Mechanistic investigations involved MeRIP-qPCR, mRNA stability assays, co-immunoprecipitation (Co-IP), Western blot, immunofluorescence, and pharmacological modulation of the NF-κB pathway. RESULTS: Lungs from ARDS rats showed decreased global levels and increased FTO expression. Knockdown of FTO alleviated lung injury, reduced pulmonary edema, and suppressed the expression of TF and PAI-1, concomitant with inhibition of NF-κB signaling. Integrated multi-omics analysis identified Protein Kinase C Beta (PRKCB), a serine/threonine kinase known to regulate inflammatory signaling, as a key target of FTO. Mechanistically, FTO-mediated demethylation of PRKCB mRNA reduced its recognition by reader proteins that typically promote mRNA decay, thereby prolonging its half-life and enhancing protein translation. Elevated PRKCB promoted IKKβ phosphorylation and subsequent NF-κB activation. Rescue experiments confirmed that FTO regulates alveolar hypercoagulation and fibrinolytic inhibition in ARDS via PRKCB-dependent activation of the NF-κB pathway. CONCLUSION: Our study identifies the FTO-PRKCB-NF-κB axis as a novel epitranscriptomic pathway driving alveolar fibrin deposition in ARDS. These findings reveal FTO as a potential therapeutic target for mitigating alveolar hypercoagulation and fibrinolysis inhibition in ARDS.

papers.abstract_en: Uncoupling protein 1 (UCP1)-independent energy dissipation has been proven to serve physiological functions in beige adipocytes. Here we show that a futile sodium/potassium (Na+/K+) transport cycle is preferentially amplified in mouse and human beige adipocytes and contributes to UCP1-independent energy expenditure. In mice, cold exposure activates a sympathetic-thyroid hormone signaling axis that coordinatedly induces the Na+/K+-ATPase subunit ATP1A2 together with Na+ and K+ channels, increasing bidirectional ion flux across the plasma membrane while maintaining ionic balance. Atp1a2+Kcnk3+ adipocytes are detected in mouse inguinal white adipose tissue after cold exposure. Acute inhibition of Na+/K+-ATPase reduces energy expenditure in mouse and human beige adipocytes, whereas overexpressing Atp1a2 in murine adipocytes potentiates energy expenditure, independent of UCP1. Adipocyte-specific Atp1a2 deletion impairs thermogenic capacity and exacerbates diet-induced obesity in mice. Expression of a human ATP1A2 missense variant reduces ATP1A2-dependent respiration in mouse adipocytes. Together, these identify ion transport as a tunable ATP-consuming mechanism that expands the thermogenic repertoire of beige adipocytes.

papers.authors: He J, Zhang K, Liu J, Liu S
papers.affiliation_highlight: Graduate School, Heilongjiang University of Chinese Medicine, No.
papers.results: 共识别31个重叠靶点；机器学习收敛得到4个核心生物标志物：PARP1、ALOX5、CA9、CA2；CA2在独立数据集中于肺肿瘤组织一致下调并具显著预后价值；CA2高表达与免疫激活及VEGF信号抑制相关，低表达与细胞周期活性增强相关；分子对接显示BPDE与CA2存在稳定结合（摘要未给出HR、95%CI或P值）

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Benzo[a]pyrene diol epoxide (BPDE), a key carcinogenic metabolite of the ubiquitous environmental pollutant benzo[a]pyrene, is a well-established etiological agent in lung cancer. However, a systems-level understanding of its molecular targets and pathogenic mechanisms remains incomplete. This study aimed to identify and characterize the core toxicity targets linking BPDE exposure to lung carcinogenesis using an integrative network toxicology approach. METHODS: Putative BPDE targets were retrieved from SwissTargetPrediction and TargetNet. Lung cancer-associated genes were compiled from GeneCards and TCGA datasets. The intersection yielded candidate genes, which were analyzed via protein-protein interaction (PPI) network construction, functional enrichment, and machine learning (LASSO, XGBoost, Random Forest, Boruta) to identify core biomarkers. A nomogram was developed for risk prediction. The key target CA2 was further validated for prognostic value, differential expression across multiple cohorts (TCGA, GEO), and associated biological pathways via gene set enrichment analysis (GSEA) and pathway activity scoring. Molecular docking was performed to simulate the BPDE-CA2 interaction. RESULTS: Thirty-one overlapping targets were identified. Enrichment analysis implicated processes like inflammation, oxidative stress response, and cancer-related pathways (e.g. p53, cell cycle). Machine learning convergence highlighted four core biomarkers: PARP1, ALOX5, CA9, and CA2. Among these, CA2 demonstrated significant prognostic value, consistent downregulation in lung tumor tissues across independent datasets, and distinct molecular phenotypes: its high expression correlated with immune activation and suppressed VEGF signaling, while low expression was linked to enhanced cell cycle activity. Molecular docking revealed a stable binding interaction between BPDE and CA2. CONCLUSION: This integrative study identifies a set of core targets, prominently featuring CA2, that potentially mediate BPDE-induced lung carcinogenesis. CA2 downregulation is associated with poor prognosis, a pro-proliferative phenotype, and may be directly modulated by BPDE, positioning it as a critical molecular link between environmental exposure and lung cancer development. Insight Paragraph This study provides a systems-level molecular bridge connecting environmental carcinogen exposure to lung cancer pathogenesis. By integrating network toxicology, machine learning, and multi-omics validation, we move beyond single-gene associations to identify a core set of toxicity targets, most notably CA2. We demonstrate that CA2 downregulation, potentially via direct interaction with BPDE, is linked to poor prognosis and a pro-proliferative phenotype. This integrative approach offers a novel mechanistic insight, positioning CA2 as a critical node at the intersection of environmental exposure, disrupted metabolism, and tumor progression, with implications for risk prediction and targeted prevention strategies.

papers.abstract_en: We herein describe the structure-based design, synthesis and biological evaluation of a new class of histone deacetylase 6 (HDAC6) inhibitors guided by X-ray crystal structures of our previously identified compounds 13-15. X-ray co-crystal structures of second-generation inhibitors 19b (Subseries I) and 20b (Subseries II) within zHDAC6 CD2 confirmed that these compounds behave as highly potent HDAC6 inhibitors with the ability to engage the S531 residue in the L2 loop HDAC6 catalytic domain. Western-blot analysis confirmed the target engagement in cell-based settings, through the increase of acetylated tubulin levels, without significant variation in the histone acetylation status. Compound 20b extensively reduced the viability of A549 cells in both 2- and 3-dimensional cell cultures, through the activation of pro-autophagic pathways. In addition, HDAC6 inhibition impaired the nucleation of stress-granules, confirming the ability of these compounds to modulate liquid-liquid phase separation, an emerging HDAC6-driven hallmark in cancer.

papers.abstract_en: Cancer is known to be a major cause of death worldwide, with lung cancer responsible for the maximum number of deaths. There is an urgent need for early and effective diagnosis of lung cancer to improve the overall survival rate, which is extremely low to date. Studies have shown that 57% of lung cancers are detected only after metastasis of the tumor. Economic restraints in hospitals are resulting in decreased early diagnosis of lung cancer and an increase in aggressive, incurable grades. Traditional imaging modalities like ultrasound, x-ray, CT, and MRI scans are often unable to precisely locate the extent of metastasis of lung cancer, paving the way for better, more sophisticated diagnostic tools. Nuclear medicine techniques help in better understanding of the metabolic extent of cancer cells using radioactive isotopes. PET/SPECT scans help provide more precise grading and better understanding of tumor morphology. However, the lack of distinction between inflammatory and malignant lesions remains a diagnostic challenge. Gold nanoparticles (GNPs) have been studied as effective contrast agents, enhancing the diagnostic efficiency of lung cancer. Formulation and tagging of GNPs have improved efficacy and biodistribution of cancer drugs; however, no such gold nanoformulation is available for diagnosis to date. The use of different shapes of GNPs functionalized with specific lung cancer biomarkers can potentially increase the specificity of lung tumor diagnosis. In this review, we address the lacunae and provide a strategic roadmap for the effective development of GNP-based diagnostics, from benchtop to high-fidelity biomaterials with clinical applications for efficient lung cancer management.

papers.abstract_en: INTRODUCTION: Central serous chorioretinopathy (CSCR) is characterized by retinal pigment epithelium dysfunction and choroidal hyperpermeability. Beyond established associations such as psychosocial stress and corticosteroid exposure, experimental and epidemiological findings raise the possibility that mast cell and histamine-related pathways may contribute to CSCR pathophysiology. This study reviews mechanistic and clinical evidence for the role of histamine in the pathogenesis of CSCR, as well as the role of histamine-targeted therapies in this condition. We also present two cases, highlighting the possible therapeutic role of anti-allergy agents in CSCR. METHODS: We searched Ovid MEDLINE, Embase, and Cochrane CENTRAL to October 2025 for studies of antihistamines and/or mast-cell stabilizers, alone or in combination in central serous retinopathy and pachychoroid spectrum diseases. Eligible designs included human observational and controlled studies. Two reviewers independently screened, extracted, and appraised data using ROBINS-I, NOS, and GRADE. Results were narratively synthesized. RESULTS: After screening 316 articles, three studies (430 patients, 390 controls) from India and the United States were included. Direct evidence for anti-allergy therapeutics was limited to a single management series, in which short-course antihistamine treatment showed no meaningful visual or anatomical benefit; however, improvements occurred spontaneously or after focal laser. One case-control study reported a higher prevalence of antihistamine use and allergic disorders among CSCR patients (OR 4.1), suggesting a possible histamine-mediated risk. Another case-control study found no statistically significant association between antihistamine use and CSCR after multivariable adjustment. CONCLUSION: Analysis of the literature revealed inconsistent associations between antihistamine use and CSCR risk, with a brief therapeutic trial offering no benefit for acute CSCR. However, two illustrative cases demonstrate temporal associations between interruption of anti-allergic therapy and subsequent CSCR activity, followed by anatomical improvement after treatment re-initiation or modification. These observations are hypothesis-generating but cannot establish therapeutic efficacy or causality, particularly given concurrent treatment changes in case 1. Given the inconclusive therapeutic data, further randomized controlled trials are warranted to more rigorously evaluate sustained mast-cell stabilization regimens before drawing clinical conclusions.

papers.abstract_en: Follicular helper T (TFH) cells are well known for their role in supporting B cell responses. Here, we identify a critical B cell-independent function for TFH cells in sustaining regulatory T (Treg) cells within gut-associated lymphoid tissues (GALT). We demonstrate that TFH cells produce interleukin-2 (IL-2) at the T cell-B cell border and within interfollicular regions and that this localized IL-2 is required to maintain GALT Treg cell homeostasis and restrain the expansion of pathogenic effector T cells. Mice selectively lacking IL-2-producing TFH cells develop colitis and fatal multiorgan inflammation, driven by impaired GALT Treg cell responses and uncontrolled effector T cell activation. Broad-spectrum antibiotic treatment alleviates both intestinal and extraintestinal pathology, indicating that loss of tolerance to commensal-derived antigens is a key driver of disease. Together, these findings define a spatially restricted TFH cell-derived IL-2 niche critical for GALT Treg cell stability and uncover an unexpected immunoregulatory role for TFH cells in maintaining gastrointestinal tolerance beyond B cell help.

papers.abstract_en: The assay for transposase-accessible chromatin using sequencing (ATAC-seq) on formalin-fixed paraffin-embedded (FFPE) samples maps accessible chromatin in archival tissues, but DNA degradation and crosslinking remain significant challenges when processing these samples. Here, we present a protocol for Omni-ATAC-seq on degraded human small-cell lung cancer (SCLC) FFPE-derived samples. We detail steps for successful nuclei isolation, efficient tagmentation, and optimal library amplification to overcome the low signal-to-noise ratio. This protocol enables high-quality epigenetic profiling, turning archived SCLC samples into valuable resources for studying disease progression. For complete details on the use and execution of this protocol, please refer to Kawasaki et al.1.

papers.title_en: Neuroimmune activation of the TRPV1-RAMP1 axis drives type 2 immunity to repair intestinal barrier and alleviate metabolic disease.
papers.authors: Yang X, Li X, Wu Y, An L, Zhang L, Yu Z, Jing X, Xu T et al.
