papers.abstract_en: INTRODUCTION: Obesity is closely associated with intestinal barrier dysfunction and chronic inflammation. Group 2 innate lymphoid cells (ILC2s) can receive and integrate signals from neuropeptides, neurotransmitters, and epithelial cells, thereby regulating local tissue inflammatory responses and promoting repair. However, the specific mechanism by which the nociceptor Transient Receptor Potential Vanilloid 1 (TRPV1) interacts with ILC2s to regulate intestinal homeostasis in obesity remains unclear. OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to investigate whether electroacupuncture (EA) ameliorated obesity-mediated intestinal injury by modulating type 2 immune responses via the TRPV1- calcitonin gene-related peptide (CGRP)- receptor activity-modifying protein 1 (RAMP1) axis. METHODS: A high-fat diet-induced obese mouse model was employed. The expression levels of TRPV1 and CGRP, the abundance of ILC2s, and the levels of type 2 cytokines IL-5 and IL-13 in colon tissues were assessed using flow cytometry, immunofluorescence staining, and Western blotting. Intestinal pathological changes and goblet cell status were evaluated via hematoxylin and eosin staining and Alcian blue-periodic acid-Schiff staining. Mechanistic verification was performed by specific ablation of TRPV1+ dorsal root ganglion neurons and pharmacological inhibition of the CGRP receptor or RAMP1. RESULTS: EA treatment significantly increased CGRP derived from TRPV1-expressing sensory neurons, which subsequently activated type 2 immunity, as evidenced by the expansion of ILC2s and upregulation of related cytokines. This immune activation ultimately promoted the differentiation and proliferation of goblet cells and ameliorated high-fat diet-induced intestinal barrier damage. Notably, in mice with specific ablation of TRPV1+ dorsal root ganglion neurons, or treatment with a CGRP receptor antagonist, or ablation of intestinal ILC2s, EA failed to induce intestinal type 2 immune activation or alleviate diet-induced intestinal injury. CONCLUSION: Our findings demonstrate that electroacupuncture activates intestinal type 2 immunity via the TRPV1-CGRP-RAMP1 axis, identifying this pathway as a crucial mechanism for repairing obesity-associated intestinal barrier dysfunction.

papers.abstract_en: Triosephosphate isomerase 1 (TPI1) is a key glycolytic enzyme that catalyzes the reversible interconversion of dihydroxyacetone phosphate and glyceraldehyde-3-phosphate. Emerging evidence suggests that TPI1 also participates in cancer-associated non-canonical functions involving altered subcellular localization, protein-protein interactions, signaling regulation, and therapeutic responses. This narrative review summarizes the biochemical properties of TPI1 and critically evaluates its expression patterns, prognostic associations, molecular mechanisms, and therapeutic implications across malignancies. TPI1 is frequently upregulated in several cancer types, although its biological and clinical significance varies substantially among tumors. Experimental studies have identified potential moonlighting functions involving nuclear localization in lung adenocarcinoma and protein-interaction-dependent signaling in breast cancer, glioblastoma, and bladder cancer. In hepatocellular carcinoma, apparently conflicting findings may reflect differences in experimental models, cellular contexts, and intracellular versus extracellular-vesicle-associated TPI1. Emerging evidence also implicates TPI1 in tumor immune regulation and therapeutic resistance, although many findings remain based on computational associations or preclinical models. Current research is limited by insufficient prospective clinical validation and the absence of established, broadly applicable pharmacological strategies targeting TPI1. Collectively, TPI1 represents a context-dependent candidate biomarker and potential therapeutic target in cancer, warranting further mechanistic investigation and clinical validation. REGISTRATION: Not applicable; this article is a narrative review.

papers.abstract_en: Intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma carries a poor prognosis making its management challenging. Histotripsy is a non-invasive, non-ionizing, and non-thermal therapy that mechanically disrupts tumors through acoustic cavitation. We present the case of a 59-year-old man with locally advanced, multifocal, stage II intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma who achieved a complete pathologic response in the explanted liver after treatment with histotripsy and systemic drug therapy consisting of gemcitabine, cisplatin, durvalumab, and trastuzumab deruxtecan. This case highlights the potential role of noninvasive histotripsy as a bridging therapy to transplantation in selected patients with cholangiocarcinoma.

papers.title_en: Multimodal precision diagnostics in clinical xenotransplantation.
papers.authors: Meier RPH, Morgand E, Mezine F, Mengel M, Mangiola M, Mohiuddin MM, Montgomery RA, Loupy A et al.
papers.affiliation_highlight: University of Maryland School of Medicine, Baltimore, MD, USA.

papers.reason: 为异种移植免疫监测与多模态诊断框架提供背景性综述；对胸部肿瘤外科日常判断无直接证据贡献，仅可作为异种肺移植或转化研究背景参考。
papers.abstract_en: Recent breakthroughs in pig-to-human xenotransplantation have successfully prevented hyperacute rejection of kidney, heart, liver and lung xenografts, marking a milestone long considered a critical barrier. However, these major advances also brought new challenges into focus, as immune-mediated graft injuries including antibody-mediated rejection, T cell-mediated rejection and innate immune activation have been observed in most xenotransplantation procedures to date. Detection and management of these injuries remain a critical bottleneck, as conventional histopathology and standard clinical monitoring lack the sensitivity required to identify subclinical injury early enough to guide timely intervention. This diagnostic gap underscores an urgent need for the development of advanced, multimodal precision diagnostic frameworks to enhance immune surveillance, which will be essential for standardizing clinical protocols and enabling pathogenesis-driven therapeutic intervention. This approach will inform both immunosuppressive regimens and future gene editing strategies aimed at engineering rejection-resistant porcine organs, ultimately prolonging graft survival. Broad adoption of such an integrative strategy will be essential to transition xenotransplantation from an experimental intervention into a safe, scalable and patient-centred clinical therapy. In this Review, we synthesize recent progress in xenotransplantation and position multimodal precision diagnostics as a pivotal strategy to address the remaining immunological and clinical barriers to widespread clinical implementation.

papers.authors: Sparrow J, Berg F, Gipson C, Rodriguez-Galindo C, Moreira DC
papers.affiliation_highlight: Rehabilitation Services, St.
papers.results: 医疗提供者报告在住院期间（28%，n = 7/25）、门诊（36%，n = 9/25）和生存期照护（40%，n = 10/25）中很少或从不将患者转诊至康复；转诊通常依赖提供者识别需求（85%，n = 50/59）而非标准化路径；助听产品可及性较低（n = 19/59，32%），视力产品为（n = 15/59，25%）；康复受访者中44%（15/34）报告监测功能结局。

papers.abstract_en: INTRODUCTION: Rehabilitation can improve function and quality of life for children with cancer, yet access remains limited and variable across settings. Understanding how rehabilitation is integrated within pediatric oncology care is important to identify opportunities to strengthen access and quality. METHODS: We conducted a cross-sectional survey of medical and rehabilitation professionals caring for children with cancer. The survey assessed rehabilitation service availability, referral practices, care coordination, financing, workforce knowledge and training, and monitoring of quality indicators. Findings were organized using the Health Systems Plus framework. RESULTS: Responses from 59 professionals representing 32 countries were analyzed, including 44 (74.6%) from low- and middle-income countries. Rehabilitation availability varied across disciplines, settings, and phases of care. Medical providers reported rarely or never referring patients to rehabilitation during inpatient (28%, n = 7/25), outpatient (36%, n = 9/25), and survivorship care (40%, n = 10/25). Referrals typically relied on provider identification of need (85%, n = 50/59) rather than standardized pathways. Assistive product availability varied, with lower availability of hearing (n = 19/59, 32%) and vision (n = 15/59, 25%) products. Family payment for rehabilitation services and assistive products was frequently reported. Workforce challenges included limited rehabilitation knowledge among medical providers and limited training opportunities for rehabilitation providers. Among rehabilitation respondents, 44% (15/34) reported monitoring functional outcomes. Qualitative findings highlighted barriers related to workforce, awareness, financial, infrastructure, geographic, and referral-system challenges. CONCLUSIONS: This survey highlights opportunities to improve access to rehabilitation and assistive products through strengthening referral pathways, workforce capacity, financing, care coordination, and monitoring. These components are interdependent and require coordinated system-level action.

papers.abstract_en: Neuroblastoma (NB) is the most common extracranial solid malignancy of childhood, arising from neural crest cells of the sympathetic nervous system. Metastatic spread most frequently involves the bone marrow, bones, lymph nodes, and liver, whereas soft-tissue, central nervous system, and pulmonary metastases are less common. Unusual sites of recurrence may present a significant diagnostic challenge. We report a rare case of thymic relapse of NB presenting as an anterior mediastinal mass with intense uptake on 123I-meta-iodobenzylguanidine (123I-mIBG) scintigraphy. This case highlights an uncommon pattern of NB recurrence and the value of 123I-mIBG imaging in its detection.

papers.authors: Smit EC, Komar ZM, Blommestein HM, Verheul HMW, Jager A, Tauriello DVF, van Gent DC

papers.abstract_en: Personalized cancer treatment requires stratification of patients based on biomarkers. Despite advances in biomarker-guided therapy, biomarkers are not always available or sufficient to predict treatment responses in individual patients. Functional ex vivo cancer models with the potential to assess therapeutic outcomes upfront have been developed but have not been implemented in clinical practice-despite accumulating evidence of their clinical relevance. This review describes how three essential steps in the development of personalized functional prediction tests (analytical validity, clinical validity, and clinical utility) should be combined in a multidisciplinary approach: Integrated Translational Co-design. This approach front-loads clinical utility and validation constraints into early analytical design decisions, so that biological fidelity, clinical implementation, and healthcare costs can be optimized from the start of assay development.

papers.abstract_en: Targeting protein-protein interactions (PPIs) with shallow, extended interfaces remains challenging, as exemplified by the histone chaperone ASF1. Here, we report de novo designed d-sulfonyl-γ-AApeptide foldamers that mimic the hot-spot residues of the histone H3 C-terminal α-helix that are essential for ASF1 recognition. The lead compound ASF-015 shows high-affinity binding to ASF1A and potent antiproliferative activity across cancer cell lines. These foldamers, completely resistant to proteolytic degradation, penetrate cells without a cell-penetrating peptide, engage intracellular ASF1, disrupt the ASF1-histone H3-H4 complex, and transcriptionally suppress proliferation and promote apoptosis. In the 4T1 and CT26 murine models, systemically administered ASF-015 inhibits tumor growth without detectable toxicity. This study establishes d-sulfonyl-γ-AApeptides as the first ASF1 inhibitors that simultaneously achieve high affinity, metabolic stability, autonomous permeability, and in vivo anti-tumor efficacy, offering a new strategy for targeting the ASF1-histone interface and other challenging PPIs in epigenetic drug discovery.

papers.abstract_en: Extranodal NK/T-cell lymphoma (ENKTCL) is a rare aggressive lymphoma whose management is complicated by HIV-1 co-infection due to drug-drug interactions and overlapping toxicities, specifically the convergent hepatorenal and hematological toxicities resulting from the concurrent use of chemotherapeutic regimens and ART. We report a middle-aged HIV-1 positive man (CD4+ T cells:198/μL, HIV-1 RNA:9.70×10³ copies/mL) with stage IE ENKTCL nasal type, whose initial nasal congestion was repeatedly misdiagnosed as sinusitis. An integrase strand transfer inhibitor-based (INSTIs) ART was unaffordable, and efavirenz was contraindicated by prior allergy, necessitating continuation of lopinavir/ritonavir-based ART despite its CYP3A4 inhibition. A multidisciplinary team guided concurrent therapy with two full-dose cycles of P-GemOxD (gemcitabine, pegaspargase, oxaliplatin, dexamethasone) followed by consolidative radiotherapy (20 fractions). The patient tolerated treatment without grade ≥ 3 adverse events. Post-therapy PET-CT confirmed complete metabolic response, with HIV-1 RNA undetectable. At 9-month follow-up, remission persisted and CD4+ T cells rose to 255/μL. This case illustrates that an MDT model offers a practical management framework for delivering full-dose P-GemOxD chemotherapy with non-INSTIs when INSTI-based regimens are not accessible. Our experience provides a reference strategy for managing the therapeutic complexities of concurrent HIV and malignancy.

papers.abstract_en: Secondary neuroinflammation is an important determinant of tissue injury, repair, and neurological recovery after ischemic stroke, yet the lipid-metabolic environment in which this response develops remains incompletely integrated into current mechanistic models. This narrative review synthesizes PubMed-indexed, peer-reviewed literature published between 2010 and 2026 on post-stroke cholesterol metabolism, microglial lipid handling, NLRP3 inflammasome signaling, immunometabolic remodeling, therapeutic intervention, and recovery-related outcomes. Ischemic injury substantially remodels the local lipid environment through neuronal membrane disruption, myelin breakdown, oxidative lipid modification, altered cholesterol turnover, and blood-brain barrier dysfunction, generating a heterogeneous pool of free cholesterol, cholesteryl esters, lipid droplets, cholesterol crystals, oxysterols, and oxidized lipids. Stroke-specific studies increasingly support the emergence of cholesterol- and lipid-loaded microglial states and show that microglial lipid-processing capacity, including TREM2- and SREBP2-related mechanisms, can influence inflammatory and reparative responses. However, the causal connection between cholesterol dysregulation and NLRP3 activation remains only partly resolved. Direct stroke evidence supports the coexistence of microglial cholesterol overload and NLRP3-associated inflammatory changes, whereas detailed mechanisms involving cholesterol crystal-induced lysosomal injury, metabolic remodeling, and intracellular lipid stress remain partly dependent on cross-model evidence. Oxysterol effects are context dependent, and recent cholesterol-mobilization experiments identify mitochondrial DNA leakage-STING signaling as an alternative, more directly validated downstream pathway. Post-stroke microglia are also functionally heterogeneous, with distinct populations contributing to debris clearance, white matter repair, and neurological recovery. Therapeutically, systemic lipid management should be distinguished from experimental strategies that modify brain cholesterol handling or suppress inflammasome-associated inflammation, and no integrated cholesterol-microglia-NLRP3 treatment strategy has yet been clinically validated. Collectively, current evidence supports a proposed, evidence-stratified framework in which cholesterol-related lipid stress, microglial state, inflammasome susceptibility, and tissue repair partially converge rather than forming a single validated linear causal axis.

papers.abstract_en: Bronchopulmonary dysplasia (BPD), the most common chronic lung disease of prematurity, is at its mechanistic core an immune-developmental disease in which inflammatory injury disrupts normal lung maturation. In the United States, BPD remains among the most common morbidities of very preterm birth, affecting a substantial proportion of infants born before 32 weeks' gestation. These infants are born before alveolarization is complete, into an inflammatory environment that can impair ongoing lung development. This review advances a single thesis: the heterogeneous prenatal and postnatal insults that precede BPD (chorioamnionitis and the fetal inflammatory response syndrome, Ureaplasma colonization, hyperoxia, mechanical ventilation, sepsis, and intestinal dysbiosis) converge on a small number of innate sensing pathways, principally TLR2 and TLR4 signaling through NF-κB to the NLRP3 inflammasome - with parallel sterile inputs (mitochondrial reactive oxygen species and additional pattern-recognition receptors) feeding the same inflammasome node. We argue that this convergence is what separates BPD from ordinary neonatal lung injury, and that the outcome depends less on the magnitude of the initiating injurious hits than on failure of the resolution program that should terminate them - a hypothesis supported by convergent preclinical evidence but not yet established in preterm infants. Evidence is assembled across three domains: the cellular substrate (M1-skewed, classically activated-like alveolar macrophages, NETs, Th17/Treg imbalance, deficient transplacental IgG transfer); the mediator network (IL-1β, IL-6, IL-8, TNF-α, and the loss of endogenous brakes - specialized pro-resolving mediators, IL-37, Nrf2, short-chain fatty acids); and the signaling architecture (NF-κB, the NLRP3 inflammasome, and trained immunity). We also discuss the mechanistically supported, druggable nodes and the developmental phase in which each is engageable.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Strategies for repairing spinal cord injury (SCI) emphasize blocking the shift of microglia to the pro-inflammatory M1 phenotype, lowering neuroinflammation, and fostering neuronal survival. The cGMP-PKG pathway modulates immune cell function by decreasing the secretion of pro-inflammatory elements such as IL-1β and TNF and boosting the levels of the anti-inflammatory element IL-10, thereby alleviating inflammatory responses. Additionally, transcranial alternating current stimulation (tACS) at specific frequencies may indirectly regulate immune cell activity and inflammatory cytokine secretion by modulating the autonomic nervous system, thereby demonstrating anti-inflammatory potential. OBJECTIVE: To assess how tACS influences microglial polarization following SCI and investigate the underlying molecular mechanisms. METHODS: Proteomics sequencing, Western blotting, ELISA, Nissl staining, hematoxylin and eosin (HE) staining, real-time quantitative PCR (qPCR), immunofluorescence, live/dead staining and other experimental techniques were employed. Furthermore, an in vivo rat model was used to determine the effect of tACS on the recovery of motor function following injury. RESULTS: The polarization of glial cells towards the M1 proinflammatory phenotype was partially suppressed by tACS, thereby alleviating neuroinflammation and improving neuronal survival to promote functional recovery after SCI. Mechanistic studies revealed that tACS modulates the conversion of the glial inflammatory phenotype by initiating the cGMP-PKG signaling pathway, thereby offering neuroprotective and anti-inflammatory effects. CONCLUSION: The activity of the cGMP-PKG signaling pathway is upregulated by tACS, thereby modulating microglial polarization, suppressing neuroinflammation and protecting neurons from inflammatory injury. As a non-invasive neuromodulation technique, tACS holds potential as a therapeutic approach for SCI.

papers.abstract_en: Autophagy is increasingly recognized as a central immunological process whose roles extend far beyond intracellular recycling. By coordinating lysosomal degradation, organelle quality control, selective antimicrobial clearance, and inflammatory signal termination, autophagy acts as a decisive checkpoint at the crossroads between protective innate immunity and pathological immune persistence. Xenophagy, the selective autophagic elimination of intracellular pathogens, is a particularly important process at the interface between host defense, endosomal trafficking and immune resolution. Distinct monogenic disorders affecting EPG5-dependent autophagosome-lysosome fusion, LYST-dependent lysosomal and granule organization, or RAB27A-dependent lytic-granule exocytosis illustrate how different lesions in intracellular trafficking can impair microbial handling and contribute to immune dysregulation. Functioning autophagy also boosts cellular resilience through the removal of intracellular debris via exocytosis. In parallel, neutrophil extracellular traps (NETs) have emerged as potent antimicrobial structures that also aid cellular resilience but have a dual role in immunity: while NET formation can restrict pathogen dissemination, excessive or insufficiently cleared NETs expose chromatin, histones, proteases and modified autoantigens that can drive autoimmunity, thromboinflammation and tissue damage. In this review, we discuss the intricate links between xenophagy, its intracellular endolysosomal hubs, and its extracellular targets and traps as an integrated cell-biological and immunopathological network. We highlight how autophagy initiation and verified degradative flux, mitochondrial quality control, reactive oxygen species, peptidylarginine deiminase 4 (PAD4)-dependent chromatin decondensation, and endolysosomal trafficking may intersect with neutrophil effector functions in a stimulus- and model-dependent manner. Particular emphasis is placed on endosomal checkpoint proteins such as TOM1, which link ubiquitinated cargo sorting, IL-1R1/NF-κB signal termination, autophagosome maturation, and lysosomal degradation. We propose that defective endosomal and autophagic resolution mechanisms blur the boundary between efficient antimicrobial defense and chronic inflammatory auto-amplification. This concept is highly relevant for a wide range of autoimmune conditions, including systemic lupus erythematosus, rheumatoid arthritis, ANCA-associated vasculitis, autoinflammatory syndromes, immunodeficiency, and neuroinflammatory disease. Finally, we discuss therapeutic strategies aimed at restoring immune resolution, including modulation of autophagy, enhancement of NET clearance, targeting of PAD4 and inflammasome pathways as well as correction of endolysosomal trafficking defects. Understanding these intricately linked networks may open new avenues for mechanism-based treatment of autoimmune and innate immune disorders.

papers.abstract_en: Inflammatory bowel disease (IBD), encompassing Crohn's disease and ulcerative colitis, is a chronic relapsing inflammatory disorder that increases the risk of colitis-associated colorectal cancer (CAC). Despite major advances in biologics and small-molecule therapies, many patients experience primary or secondary treatment failure, adverse effects, and disease recurrence, underscoring the need for more effective, targeted therapeutic strategies. Extracellular vesicles (EVs), including exosomes, microvesicles, and apoptotic bodies, have emerged as promising nanoscale therapeutic platforms owing to their intrinsic biocompatibility, low immunogenicity, cargo-protective lipid bilayer, and natural ability to mediate intercellular communication. Recent advances in EV engineering have further expanded their therapeutic potential through genetic modification of parental cells, cargo loading, surface functionalization, and hybrid biomaterial systems, enabling enhanced targeting, drug delivery, immune modulation, tissue regeneration, and anti-tumor activity. This review summarizes the biological characteristics of EVs and discusses recent progress in engineering strategies aimed at improving their therapeutic efficacy in IBD and CAC. We critically evaluate current preclinical evidence regarding immunomodulation, restoration of intestinal barrier integrity, regulation of gut microbiota, targeted drug delivery, cancer immunotherapy, and inhibition of metastasis. Finally, we discuss the major translational challenges, including manufacturing standardization, quality control, large-scale production, safety evaluation, regulatory considerations, and future perspectives necessary for successful clinical implementation of engineered EV-based therapies.

papers.abstract_en: Despite its fundamental importance, the molecular mechanisms of post-Golgi transport remain incompletely understood. Carrier formation of post-Golgi transport depends on ARF3 and ARF1, very close paralogs; the former localizes on the trans-Golgi network (TGN) whereas the latter localizes on TGN and cis-Golgi. Identifying ARF1/3 interactors on the TGN is critical for elucidating post-Golgi transport mechanisms. To this end, we used GBF1M832L cells, in which ARFs on TGN can be dispersed by the addition of Brefeldin A (BFA) via inhibition of trans-Golgi-localized ARF nucleotide exchange factors BIG1/2, without disturbing cis-localizing ARFs or Golgi structure. We performed proteomic analyses of ARF1 and ARF3 proximal proteins on TGN using TurboID boosted by membrane permeable biotin methyl ester in BFA-treated and untreated GBF1M832L cells. By comparing these conditions, proximal proteins specific to TGN-localizing ARF1 or ARF3, and those common to both, were identified. The ARF1-specific proximal protein SMAP1 and the ARF1/3 common proximal protein LRBA are BIG1/2-dependently localized to the Golgi, whereas the ARF3-specific proximal protein Rab3IL1 is BIG1/2-independently localized on recycling endosomes. This study establishes an approach to selectively control post-Golgi transport and map ARF-dependent interaction networks at the TGN, providing a framework for understanding the molecular mechanisms underlying carrier formation.

papers.abstract_en: Hormone receptor-positive, human epidermal growth factor receptor 2-low (HER2-low) metastatic breast cancer (MBC) constitutes the predominant subtype of advanced breast cancer, with most patients eventually developing resistance to endocrine therapy (ET) and cyclin-dependent kinase 4/6 inhibitors (CDK4/6i). This case report describes a 64-year-old woman with hormone receptor (HR)-positive, HER2-low MBC involving lung, pleural, and lymph node metastases who achieved a remarkable and sustained radiographic complete response (rCR) to palbociclib plus fulvestrant, followed by letrozole after fulvestrant injection intolerance. The patient exhibited near-complete regression of metastatic lesions within 18 months and maintained remission for over 6 years, far exceeding the typical median progression-free survival observed in clinical trials. The prolonged remission observed underscores the existence of biologically distinct tumor subsets with exceptional sensitivity to CDK4/6 inhibition, warranting investigation into underlying molecular mechanisms.

papers.abstract_en: Atopic dermatitis (AD) is a chronic, relapsing inflammatory skin disease driven by a combination of genetic predisposition, epidermal barrier dysfunction, immune dysregulation, aberrant neuroinflammatory signaling, and environmental factors. Genetic defects in barrier-related molecules, particularly loss-of-function mutations in filaggrin (FLG), represent key heritable determinants of impaired epidermal integrity and enhanced allergen penetration. In recent years, advances in the understanding of its molecular pathogenesis have progressively shifted the therapeutic paradigm from conventional broad-spectrum immunosuppression toward precision-targeted interventions aimed at key inflammatory pathways, substantially transforming disease management in patients with moderate-to-severe AD. Current evidence indicates that type 2 immune inflammation remains a central pathogenic axis in AD. Key mediators, including interleukin (IL)-4, IL-13, IL-31, thymic stromal lymphopoietin (TSLP), and the Janus kinase (JAK)-signal transducer and activator of transcription (STAT) signaling pathway, collectively contribute to epidermal barrier disruption, inflammatory amplification, and the itch-scratch cycle. Based on these mechanisms, a range of biologics and small-molecule targeted therapies-including IL-4 receptor α (IL-4Rα) antagonists, IL-13 monoclonal antibodies, IL-31 pathway inhibitors, JAK inhibitors, and emerging OX40/OX40L modulatory strategies-have demonstrated significant efficacy in randomized controlled trials and real-world studies, thereby ushering AD into a mechanism-driven therapeutic era. However, targeted therapies still face critical challenges, including heterogeneous treatment responses, insufficient long-term safety data, limited stratification of disease endotypes, and disparities in treatment accessibility. Increasing evidence suggests that therapeutic response is more closely associated with immunological endotypes than traditional clinical phenotypes, and that single-pathway blockade alone is insufficient to achieve durable disease modification. This review systematically summarizes the key pathogenic mechanisms of AD, current targeted therapeutic strategies, and their clinical translation progress, with a particular focus on existing therapeutic challenges and future directions. Ultimately, integration of biomarkers, multi-omics profiling, real-world evidence, and artificial intelligence-assisted decision-making may facilitate the development of endotype-based precision treatment frameworks, enabling a shift from disease control toward sustained remission and true disease modification.

papers.abstract_en: Cervical cancer is a common malignancy in women worldwide, with distant metastases frequently occurring in the lungs, liver, bones, and lymph nodes. However, this case report presents an extremely rare isolated metastasis to the left scapular region,specifically located between the supraspinatus and the trapezius muscles, in a patient with locally advanced cervical squamous cell carcinoma who developed this lesion during maintenance therapy with a programmed death receptor-1 (PD-1) inhibitor after completing concurrent chemoradiotherapy. The clinical presentation of this metastatic lesion was atypical and posed a significant diagnostic challenge; however, multimodal imaging (MRI, PET/CT) and histopathological examination ultimately confirmed the diagnosis of cervical cancer metastasis. This finding underscores the necessity of maintaining a high level of vigilance for metastases in atypical sites, even in the era of immunotherapy. To manage this rare presentation, a multidisciplinary team developed a comprehensive treatment strategy centered on surgical resection, followed by postoperative adjuvant radiotherapy administered concurrently with chemotherapy and anti-angiogenic therapy(Q3W) consisting of paclitaxel 135 mg/m², cisplatin 50 mg/m², and bevacizumab 10 mg/kg. The patient remained recurrence-free at 13 months, suggesting that a multimodal combined local and systemic strategy may be feasible for selected patients with solitary muscle metastasis. This case not only adds to the clinical understanding of rare metastases in cervical cancer but also demonstrates that tumors can still metastasize to atypical sites under immunotherapy. These findings highlight the need for vigilance regarding metastases at atypical sites during immunotherapy. Any underlying mechanism-including immune editing and clonal evolution-remains speculative in the absence of paired molecular data and requires further validation.

papers.title_zh: 高频超声监测结节型基底细胞癌sonidegib治疗后反应：3例病例系列提示影像完全缓解与病理完全缓解可能对应但特异性有限
papers.title_en: Case report: Clinical utility and limitations of high-frequency ultrasound for monitoring sonidegib response in nodular basal cell carcinoma: a three-case series.
papers.authors: He D, Tao H, Bian K, Xu J, Wang T
papers.affiliation_highlight: Department of Ultrasound, Hangzhou Third People's Hospital, Hangzhou Third Hospital Affiliated to Zhejiang Chinese Medic…
papers.results: 2例达到影像学完全缓解并接受手术切除及组织病理学对照；组织病理显示例1为慢性炎症浸润、例2为轻度真皮纤维化，均无残留肿瘤；第3例在6个月后恶性影像特征消退；基线超声不可获得，结果与最早3-4个月随访比较
papers.authors_conclusion: 在这一小型病例系列中，HFUS监测了靶向治疗后的深部组织变化；在2例有组织病理学确认的患者中，HFUS联合皮肤镜的影像学完全缓解与病理完全缓解相对应；但鉴于样本量小且仅2例有组织病理学确认，这只是可能的对应关系，而非真正预测能力的证据。治疗后低回声区可能反映炎症、纤维化或残留肿瘤，限制了特异性。影像学完全缓解在可行时应通过活检或切除确认。手术仍是金标准；非手术患者需要密切随访。
papers.ai_note: 样本仅3例，且仅2例获得组织病理学确认；无基线超声，无法评估治疗前后真实变化；无对照、无盲法、无预设判读标准；影像学完全缓解定义允许残留非恶性低回声区，而作者亦承认低回声区可为炎症、纤维化或残留肿瘤，因而不能从本系列推断HFUS的预测准确性或特异性。摘要对局限性有较明确说明，但结论仍基于极少病例，信息不足。

pico.p: 3例结节型基底细胞癌患者，接受sonidegib 200 mg每日一次（2024年10月至2026年5月）
pico.ic: 干预：sonidegib靶向治疗联合20-30 MHz高频超声及皮肤镜监测；对照：无独立对照，2例随后手术切除行组织病理学对照，1例拒绝手术

papers.reason: 对胸部肿瘤临床判断影响有限；仅作为靶向治疗后影像-病理对照的弱证据，提示影像学完全缓解不能替代病理确认，并可为皮肤肿瘤治疗反应监测研究设计提供有限的背景参考。
papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Sonidegib, a Hedgehog pathway inhibitor, can induce clinical and imaging remission in locally advanced basal cell carcinoma (BCC). Residual deep tumor may persist after malignant dermoscopic and ultrasound features disappear. This case series assessed the utility and limitations of 20-30 MHz high-frequency ultrasound (HFUS) for confirming complete imaging remission after sonidegib. CASES PRESENTATION: Three patients with nodular BCC received sonidegib 200 mg daily (October 2024-May 2026). Two achieved complete imaging remission, defined as resolution of malignant imaging features with residual non-malignant hypoechoic areas allowed, and underwent surgical resection with histopathological correlation; the third declined surgery. Baseline ultrasound was unavailable, so findings were compared with the earliest 3-4-month follow-up. RESULTS: Response involved lesion shrinkage and loss of intratumoral blood flow. Serial imaging showed gradual resolution of hypoechoic nodules with vascularity on HFUS and blue-gray nests with arborizing vessels on dermoscopy, leaving avascular scar-like structures. Preoperative HFUS residual hypoechoic areas were correlated with histopathology, which showed chronic inflammatory infiltration (case 1) and mild dermal fibrosis (case 2), with no residual tumor. The third patient's malignant features regressed after six months. CONCLUSIONS: In this small case series, HFUS monitored deeper tissue changes after targeted therapy. In two histopathologically confirmed patients, complete imaging remission on HFUS plus dermoscopy corresponded to pathological complete response; however, given the small sample and histopathological confirmation in only two patients, this is a possible correspondence rather than evidence of true predictive capability. Post-treatment hypoechoic areas may reflect inflammation, fibrosis, or residual tumor, limiting specificity. Imaging-based complete response should be confirmed by biopsy or excision when feasible. Surgery remains the gold standard; non-surgical patients require close follow-up.

papers.abstract_en: The Joint 12th Asia Oceania Human Proteome Organization (AOHUPO), 8th Asia Oceania Agricultural Proteomics Organization (AOAPO), 3rd π-HuB Global Summit, 1st π-HuB Industry Conference and 13th China Human Proteome Organization (CNHUPO) Congress, a landmark 5-in-1 international academic gathering, was successfully held in Guangzhou, China, from October 11 to 14, 2025. Centered on the theme "Navigating the Protein Universe: Toward New Biology and Precision Medicine," the meeting served as a pivotal platform for global proteomics collaboration in the post-pandemic era. Almost 2000 participants from 22 countries and regions, including approximately 200 leading scientists, clinicians, and industry innovators, attended the event. The comprehensive program encompassed diverse formats, including four pre-congress training courses (focused on MaxQuant, PEAKS, AI for protein science, and deep visual proteomics), council meetings of AOHUPO and CNHUPO, over 30 parallel symposia, two satellite symposia, the 1st π-HuB Industry Conference, 246 poster presentations, and plenary lectures by international experts. Cutting-edge topics such as AI-driven proteomics, spatial proteomics, chemoproteomics, drug discovery, and proteomics-driven precision medicine were highlighted, fostering multi-dimensional academic exchanges and technological dissemination. Key outcomes included the launch of the Asian-Pacific Proteome Organization (APPO) to promote pan-species proteomics and One Health governance, and the establishment of π-HuB Park to support the translation of basic research into health practice. Additionally, significant awards were presented, including the CNHUPO Innovation Award and the inaugural "Top 10 Proteomics Highlights in China". This congress reaffirmed the global proteomics community's commitment to unifying research efforts and overcoming boundaries to shape the future of new biology and precision medicine through sustained collaboration, technological innovation, and talent cultivation.
